# Kafka 4.3.1 wire protocol

This document is the grammar that the `main` branch implements. It is written towards what Apache Kafka **4.3.1**
speaks — the last 4.x release when the 4.x line started, so it will cover everything Kafka 4.0, 4.1, 4.2 and 4.3
added and the bug-fix releases after them — and, until the milestones of the line land, it describes what the 3.x
line delivered: Kafka **3.9.2** and the KIP-848 consumer protocol, re-measured on a 4.3.1 node. Every line carries
only its own protocol document: the grammars of the lines below live on their own branches (`docs/protocol/3.9.md`
on `3.x`, `docs/protocol/2.8.md` on `2.x`, `docs/protocol/1.1.md` on `1.x`, `docs/protocol/0.11.0.md` on `0.11.x`,
`docs/protocol/0.10.2.md` on `0.10.x`, `docs/protocol/0.9.0.md` on `0.9.x`, `docs/protocol/0.8.2.md` on `0.8.x`),
while their wire vectors travel upwards in [`vectors/`](vectors) and are replayed against the classes of this line.
**Kafka 4.0 is the first release that stops serving versions the lines below captured** (KIP-896): the replay of
those vectors needs no broker and stays, but a 4.3.1 node refuses a frame of them — see "What 4.3.1 adds to the
3.9.2 protocol".

**The 4.x line is built one Kafka minor at a time**, from 4.0 upwards, on the plan in
[`docs/handoff/main.md`](../handoff/main.md). **Current milestone: Kafka 4.1.** The foundation brought the node of
the line (Apache Kafka 4.3.1 in KRaft mode, `docker/kafka-4.3.1`), declared the constants of the whole line — the
api keys 88 to 92 in `Protocol\Kafka\Protocol\ApiKeys`, the error codes 128 to 133 in `KafkaException`, with one
exception class each in `src/Kafka/Common/Errors/` — and rebuilt the api-key table below from the ApiVersions
answer of the node. **The 4.0 milestone** brought the inherited suite to the 4.3.1 node — the versions KIP-896
removed are measured as closed connections, their classes and vectors stay — and every version Kafka 4.0 added to
an api the client speaks: Produce **v12** (the transaction protocol v2 of KIP-890 part 2, capped at v11 inside a
transaction of the protocol v1), Metadata **v13** (the top-level error code of KIP-1102), ListOffsets **v10** (the
`timeout_ms` of KIP-1075), DescribeGroups **v6** (the 69 of KIP-1043), ConsumerGroupHeartbeat **v1** (the regex
subscription of KIP-848 and the member id of KIP-1082), ConsumerGroupDescribe **v1** (the member type of KIP-1099),
EndTxn **v5** and TxnOffsetCommit **v5** (the transaction protocol v2 in `TransactionManager`, the v1 path kept for a
3.x node), UpdateFeatures **v2**, DescribeCluster **v2** (KIP-1073) and the admin methods of the raft-voter apis 80
and 81 on the `kraft.version` 1 quorum (KIP-853). **The 4.1 milestone** added Produce **v13** (topics named by id,
KIP-516), Fetch **v18** (the tagged high watermark of a follower, KIP-1166), AlterPartitionReassignments **v1**,
ListTransactions **v2** (the id pattern of KIP-1152), ListConfigResources **v1** (key 74, KIP-1142,
`AdminClient::listConfigResources()`), the share-group wire of KIP-932 at **v1** (76 to 79, the membership, the
share session, the acquired records and their acknowledgement, `AdminClient::describeShareGroups()`), the
share-group state apis 83 to 87 at v0 as wire classes, and the share-group offset apis 90 to 92 at v0 as wire
classes, whose admin methods come with the share consumer. A version the node serves above them is named in the
table as *not yet implemented on this line*, with the release that added it.

What the 3.x line delivered, and what this document carries over from it:

**The 3.x line was built one Kafka minor at a time**, from 3.0 upwards, and this document grew with it. **That
line is complete**: the constants of the whole line are declared — the api keys 65 to 87 in
`Protocol\Kafka\Protocol\ApiKeys`, the error codes 105 to 127 in `KafkaException`, with one exception class each in
`src/Kafka/Common/Errors/` — the inherited suite of the 2.x line is green on the KRaft node (the re-baseline wave
T0), and the client sends every version this package implements at the highest one a 3.9.2 node serves: of Kafka
3.0, DescribeTransactions and ListTransactions (65, 66), ListOffsets v7, OffsetFetch v8 and FindCoordinator v4; of
3.1, the topic ids of Fetch v13 and Metadata v12; of 3.2, the `reason` and the `skip_assignment` of JoinGroup v9
and LeaveGroup v5 and DescribeLogDirs v3; of 3.3, the ACL apis 29 to 31 at v3 (the first line of this package to
speak them), UpdateFeatures v1, DescribeQuorum v1, DescribeLogDirs v4 and the token apis 38 and 41 at v3 — Kafka
3.4 added nothing a client sends (KIP-866 raised broker-to-broker apis only); of 3.5, Fetch v14 and v15 (the
tiered-storage error of KIP-405 and the replica state of KIP-903), ListOffsets v8 (the local log start offset `-4`
of KIP-405) and the classes of the broker version AddPartitionsToTxn v4 of KIP-890, which the client does not
send; of 3.6, OffsetCommit v9, the v8 frame that may carry the 69 of an unknown group and the 113 of a KIP-848
member epoch; of 3.7, Produce v10 and Fetch v16 (the leader discovery of KIP-951: the tagged `current_leader` and
`node_endpoints` of a refused partition), OffsetFetch v9 (the member id and epoch of KIP-848 per group entry),
DescribeCluster **v1** (the endpoint type of KIP-919, with the error codes 114 and 115) and the three
client-metrics apis 71, 72 and 74 of KIP-714, which are **wire only**: classes and vectors, no client method; of
3.8, the abortable transaction error of KIP-890 part 2 on the apis that declare no field for it — Produce **v11**,
FindCoordinator **v5**, InitProducerId **v5**, AddOffsetsToTxn **v4**, EndTxn **v4** and TxnOffsetCommit **v4**,
which the client sends, and AddPartitionsToTxn **v5**, which is a broker version as its version 4 is — next to the
group types of ListGroups **v5** (KIP-848), the new api **DescribeTopicPartitions** (75, KIP-966) and the duration
filter of ListTransactions **v1** (KIP-994); of 3.9, ApiVersions **v4** (KAFKA-17011), DescribeQuorum **v2**
(KIP-853), Fetch **v17** (the `replica_directory_id` of KIP-853), ListOffsets **v9** (the last tiered offset `-5`
of KIP-1005) and FindCoordinator **v6** (the share coordinator type of KIP-932, which this client never sends);
and, as the last wave, the **KIP-848 consumer protocol** — ConsumerGroupHeartbeat (68) and ConsumerGroupDescribe
(69) behind `group.protocol=consumer`. What the line leaves out by the owner's decision — the share-group apis, the
raft-voter apis 80 and 81, the controller apis — is probed and written down, and no row of the api-key table below
says *not yet implemented on this line* any more. The 669 wire vectors of the lines up to 2.x are replayed
unchanged next to the 466 frames of Kafka 3.0 to 3.9 and of the KIP-848 consumer captured on the node.

Sources, in decreasing order of authority:

1. The node itself (Apache Kafka 4.3.1, `docker/kafka-4.3.1`, the container `kafka-4-3-1`): a **KRaft** node in
   combined mode — `process.roles=broker,controller`, one node with the id 1, and, unlike the static
   `controller.quorum.voters` of the 3.9.2 node of the 3.x line, a **dynamic quorum** of KIP-853:
   `controller.quorum.bootstrap.servers=localhost:9096` and a storage formatted at the first start with
   `kafka-storage.sh format --standalone`, which is how the `server.properties` and the quickstart shipped with
   4.3.1 format a combined node. No ZooKeeper (Kafka 4.0 removed it). The four client listeners PLAINTEXT 9092, SSL
   9093, SASL_PLAINTEXT 9094 and SASL_SSL 9095 and the CONTROLLER listener 9096 inside the container are those of
   the 3.9.2 node, and so are the two log directories, the `delegation.token.secret.key`, the one-node transaction
   settings (plus the two of the share-group state topic, `share.coordinator.state.topic.replication.factor=1` and
   `.min.isr=1`), the `StandardAuthorizer` with `super.users=User:ANONYMOUS;User:admin;User:kafkatest`,
   `allow.everyone.if.no.acl.found=false` and the SASL user `acltest` as the one principal that is *not* a super
   user. `group.coordinator.rebalance.protocols` is left at the default of the release, `classic,consumer,streams`;
   no client-telemetry plugin, `unstable.api.versions.enable` off. **Every feature is finalized at the default level
   of the release**, read back from the node with `kafka-features.sh describe`:

   | Feature | Finalized | Supported | What the level switches on |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | `metadata.version` | **4.3-IV0** (30) | 3.3-IV3 … 4.3-IV0 | the metadata records of the release |
   | `kraft.version` | **1** | 0 … 1 | the reconfigurable quorum of KIP-853: AddRaftVoter (80), RemoveRaftVoter (81), UpdateRaftVoter (82) |
   | `transaction.version` | **2** | 0 … 2 | the transaction protocol v2 of KIP-890 part 2: the partitions of a transaction added by Produce v12+, the epoch bumped by every EndTxn v5 |
   | `group.version` | **1** | 0 … 1 | the consumer protocol of KIP-848 |
   | `share.version` | **1** | 0 … 1 | the share groups of KIP-932 (the apis 76 to 79 and 90 to 92) |
   | `streams.version` | **1** | 0 … 1 | the streams groups of KIP-1071 (the apis 88 and 89) |
   | `eligible.leader.replicas.version` | **1** | 0 … 1 | the eligible leader replicas of KIP-966 |

   The 3.9.2 node of the 3.x line finalized `metadata.version` 3.9-IV0 and `kraft.version` 0 and nothing else;
   every answer the document attributes to "the node" was measured there until the milestone of the api re-measures
   it here, and the sections say which node they mean.
2. The sources at the release tags, `4.0.0` to `4.3.1` for what this line adds and `3.9.2` for what it inherits.
   **The JSON message specifications are the schema authority**, as on the 2.x and 3.x lines:
   `clients/src/main/resources/common/message/<Api>{Request,Response}.json` with `validVersions`,
   `flexibleVersions`, the `listeners` an api is served on, `latestVersionUnstable` and, per field, `versions`,
   `nullableVersions`, `taggedVersions`/`tag`, `default` and `entityType`, next to a `// Version N …` comment that
   names the KIP of a version — where it names one; this document names a KIP for a 3.x or 4.x version only when
   that comment does. Next to the specifications: `clients/src/main/java/org/apache/kafka/common/protocol/{ApiKeys,Errors}.java`
   for the api table and the error codes, `common/protocol/types/*.java` for the primitive types,
   `common/record/*.java` for the message format, `common/requests/ApiVersionsResponse.java` and
   `core/src/main/scala/kafka/server/ApiVersionManager.scala` for which keys the answer of a listener holds, and
   `core/src/main/scala/kafka/server/KafkaApis.scala` for what a **KRaft** node does with a request — which is not
   always what the ZooKeeper broker of the 2.x line did (`MetadataSupport.requireZkOrThrow`, see "Broker quirks and
   observations") — with `core/src/main/scala/kafka/coordinator/{group,transaction}/*.scala`, the `group-coordinator`
   module of KIP-848 and `core/src/main/scala/kafka/log/*.scala` behind it. The tags `3.0.2`, `3.1.2`, `3.2.3`,
   `3.3.2`, `3.4.1`, `3.5.2`, `3.6.2`, `3.7.2`, `3.8.1` and `3.9.2` are the last release of every 3.x minor, and
   `4.0.0`, `4.0.2`, `4.1.0`, `4.1.2`, `4.2.0`, `4.2.1`, `4.3.0` and `4.3.1` the first and the last release of every
   4.x minor; "@ 3.5.2" in this repository means that tag, and a version is attributed to the minor whose `.0` tag
   first carries it in `validVersions` (the one exception of the 4.x line is JoinGroup, whose v0 and v1 4.0.0
   removed and 4.0.1 restored). Kafka 4.x moved much of `core/src/main/scala/kafka/server` to Java modules
   (`server`, `group-coordinator`, `share-coordinator`, `transaction-coordinator`, `metadata`); a class named here
   at a 4.x tag is looked up where that tag keeps it.
3. The wiki page [A Guide To The Kafka Protocol](https://cwiki.apache.org/confluence/display/KAFKA/A+Guide+To+The+Kafka+Protocol)
   and the KIPs of the additions of this line — only those the JSON version comments name: KIP-516 (the topic ids
   of Fetch v13), KIP-405 (the tiered-storage offsets of Fetch v14 and ListOffsets v8), KIP-903 (Fetch v15,
   AlterPartition v3), KIP-951 (the current leader in a Produce v10 and Fetch v16 answer), KIP-853 (the directory
   ids of Fetch v17 and DescribeQuorum v2), KIP-734 (ListOffsets v7), KIP-1005 (ListOffsets v9), **KIP-848 (the
   new consumer group protocol: OffsetCommit v9, OffsetFetch v9, ListGroups v5 and the apis 68 and 69)**, KIP-699
   (FindCoordinator v4), KIP-890 (the code 120: Produce v11, FindCoordinator v5 and the last version of the five
   transaction apis), KIP-932 (share groups: FindCoordinator v6 and the apis 76 to 79), KIP-800 (JoinGroup v8,
   LeaveGroup v5), KIP-919 (DescribeCluster v1), KIP-836 (DescribeQuorum v1), KIP-704 and KIP-841 (AlterPartition
   v1 and v2) and KIP-994 (ListTransactions v1) — next to the KIPs of the grammar this document inherits from the
   2.x line: KIP-219, KIP-320 (leader epochs), KIP-110 (zstd), KIP-290, KIP-380, KIP-368, KIP-207, KIP-394,
   KIP-430, KIP-339, KIP-392, KIP-345, **KIP-482 (flexible versions: compact types and tagged fields)**, KIP-511,
   KIP-455, KIP-460, KIP-464, KIP-467, KIP-496, KIP-525, KIP-360, KIP-447, KIP-559, KIP-546, KIP-554, KIP-569,
   KIP-497, KIP-584, KIP-588, KIP-599, KIP-516 (topic ids), KIP-518, KIP-664 and KIP-700, and from the lines
   below: KIP-98, KIP-82, KIP-101, KIP-107, KIP-112/113, KIP-124, KIP-133, KIP-152, KIP-186, KIP-195, KIP-226,
   KIP-227, KIP-229 and KIP-48. The wiki was written for 0.10 and never caught up with anything after it; where it
   disagrees with the node, the node wins.

Notation follows the wiki: productions are camel case, primitive types lower case, `[foo]` is an array of `foo`,
and a sequence of productions means concatenation.

Like every line above `0.9.x`, this branch does not have to guess what its broker speaks: Kafka 0.10.0 added the
**ApiVersions** api (key 18), and the api-key table below is the literal answer of a real 3.9.2 node to it.

## What 4.3.1 adds to the 3.9.2 protocol

Four releases (4.0 to 4.3) add **5 api keys** (88 to 92), **32 new versions of the apis that already existed** — of
which **30** belong to keys the client listener of the node serves, the other 2 to controller apis — and the **6 error codes 128 to 133**; and, for the first time since Kafka 1.0, they **remove** versions. Nothing
changes in *how* a frame is written: no new request or response header, no new message format and no new codec,
and one new field type only (`[]int16`, in the topology of a StreamsGroupHeartbeat, an api this line leaves out).
Every one of the five new apis declares `"flexibleVersions": "0+"`, and no api the client listener serves changes
its flexible range — the engine of the 3.x line writes every frame of this one.

The attributions below were read off `validVersions` of every `*Request.json` at the tags `3.9.2`, `4.0.0`, `4.0.1`,
`4.0.2`, `4.1.0`, `4.1.2`, `4.2.0`, `4.2.1`, `4.3.0` and `4.3.1`, and the error codes off `Errors.java` at the same
tags; a KIP is named only where the version comment of the JSON names it. The bug-fix releases changed no
`validVersions` but one: **4.0.1 gave JoinGroup back its v0 and v1**, which 4.0.0 had removed.

### The four minors

| Release | New keys | New versions (client listener) | New error codes | What drove them |
|---------|----------|--------------------------------|-----------------|-----------------|
| **4.0** | – | **10** (Vote v2, controller) | 128, 129 | **KIP-896 removes the versions below the Kafka 2.1 baseline** (below); Produce v12 (the same frame as v11: the promise of the transaction protocol v2 of KIP-890 part 2 — a v12 inside a transaction needs `transaction.version` 2 and adds its partitions itself), ListOffsets v10 (`timeout_ms`, KIP-1075), Metadata v13 (a top-level error code, which may be the 129 `RebootstrapRequired`), DescribeGroups v6 (the 69 `GroupIdNotFound` for an unknown group, KIP-1043), EndTxn v5 (the epoch bumped by every transaction, KIP-890 part 2), TxnOffsetCommit v5 (the same frame as v4, the v2 half of KIP-890), UpdateFeatures v2 (no per-feature results in the answer), DescribeCluster v2 (`include_fenced_brokers`, KIP-1073), ConsumerGroupHeartbeat v1 (`subscribed_topic_regex` of KIP-848 and the member id a client generates itself, KIP-1082), ConsumerGroupDescribe v1 (the member type of KIP-1099); the ZooKeeper apis 4 to 7 lose every version |
| **4.1** | 88, 89 (unstable), 90, 91, 92 | **9** | 130-133 | Produce v13 (topics named by **id**, KIP-516), Fetch v18 (the tagged high watermark of a follower, KIP-1166), AlterPartitionReassignments v1 (`allow_replication_factor_change`), ListTransactions v2 (`transactional_id_pattern`, KIP-1152), key 74 v1 (`resource_types`, KIP-1142: ListClientMetricsResources becomes ListConfigResources), the share-group apis 76 to 79 at **v1** — their early-access v0 of 3.9 is gone — and the share-group state apis 83 to 87 stable; OffsetCommit v10, OffsetFetch v10 and InitProducerId v6 arrive `latestVersionUnstable` |
| **4.2** | (88, 89 stable) | **10** | – | OffsetCommit v10 and OffsetFetch v10 stable (**topic ids replace topic names**, KIP-848), ListOffsets v11 (the earliest pending upload offset, KIP-1023), ShareFetch v2 and ShareAcknowledge v2, DescribeShareGroupOffsets v1, WriteShareGroupState v1 and ReadShareGroupStateSummary v1, AddRaftVoter v1 (`ack_when_committed`), WriteTxnMarkers v2 (the transaction version of a marker, KIP-1228; broker-to-broker) |
| **4.3** | – | **1** (BrokerHeartbeat v2, controller) | – | DescribeLogDirs v5 (`is_cordoned` in the answer) |

InitProducerId v6 (the two-phase commit of KIP-939) is still `latestVersionUnstable` at 4.3.1: the node does not
serve it and this line does not send it.

### The versions Kafka 4.0 removed (KIP-896)

The minimum version of fifteen apis rose in 4.0 — the versions below the Kafka 2.1 baseline of KIP-896 — and the
four ZooKeeper apis lost every version with ZooKeeper itself:

| Key | Api | Versions @ 3.9.2 | Versions @ 4.3.1 | Removed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Produce | 0-11 | 3-13 (**0-13 advertised**) | v0-v2 — still in the ApiVersions answer and refused otherwise (`ApiKeys.PRODUCE_API_VERSIONS_RESPONSE_MIN_VERSION`, KAFKA-18659: a librdkafka bug needs the row to start at 0) |
| 1 | Fetch | 0-17 | 4-18 | v0-v3 |
| 2 | ListOffsets | 0-9 | 1-11 | v0 |
| 4-7 | LeaderAndIsr, StopReplica, UpdateMetadata, ControlledShutdown | 0-7, 0-4, 0-8, 0-3 | none | every version (the constants stay) |
| 8 | OffsetCommit | 0-9 | 2-10 | v0, v1 |
| 9 | OffsetFetch | 0-9 | 1-10 | v0 |
| 11 | JoinGroup | 0-9 | 0-9 | v0, v1 in **4.0.0 only**; 4.0.1 restored them |
| 19 | CreateTopics | 0-7 | 2-7 | v0, v1 |
| 20 | DeleteTopics | 0-6 | 1-6 | v0 |
| 23 | OffsetForLeaderEpoch | 0-4 | 2-4 | v0, v1 |
| 27 | WriteTxnMarkers | 0-1 | 1-2 | v0 |
| 29-31 | DescribeAcls, CreateAcls, DeleteAcls | 0-3 | 1-3 | v0 |
| 32 | DescribeConfigs | 0-4 | 1-4 | v0 |
| 34 | AlterReplicaLogDirs | 0-2 | 1-2 | v0 |
| 35 | DescribeLogDirs | 0-4 | 1-5 | v0 |
| 38-41 | the delegation-token apis | 0-3, 0-2, 0-2, 0-3 | 1-3, 1-2, 1-2, 1-3 | v0 |
| 56 | AlterPartition (`AlterIsr`) | 0-3 | 2-3 | v0, v1 (a controller api) |

**What this means for this package** (the owner's decision 7 of the line): a published class is never removed, so
the classes of every removed version stay, and so do their wire vectors — the compliance replay needs no broker.
The client sends the highest version the node serves, as before, and never one below the minimum of the answer; the
integration suite stops sending what the node refuses. The frame of a removed version is the probe's to measure
("API keys").

### The new api keys, 88 to 92

All five are Kafka **4.1**, and all five are `broker` apis, flexible from their version 0:

| Key | Api | Versions @ 4.3.1 | Added | On this line |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 88 | StreamsGroupHeartbeat | 0 | 4.1 (unstable), stable 4.2 | **out by decision** (KIP-1071 streams groups): the constant and a probe |
| 89 | StreamsGroupDescribe | 0 | 4.1 (unstable), stable 4.2 | **out by decision**: the constant and a probe |
| 90 | DescribeShareGroupOffsets | 0-1 | 4.1, v1 4.2 | **in** (KIP-932): the wire classes at v0 (4.1 milestone); the admin surface of the share consumer |
| 91 | AlterShareGroupOffsets | 0 | 4.1 | **in**: the wire classes (4.1 milestone), the admin method with the share consumer |
| 92 | DeleteShareGroupOffsets | 0 | 4.1 | **in**: like the 91 |

`ApiKeys.java` @ 4.3.1 ends at **92**. Key 74 was renamed `ListConfigResources` in 4.1 (KIP-1142); the constant and
the classes keep their published name `ListClientMetricsResources` (rule 2 of `CLAUDE.md`).

**What Kafka 4.2 changed on the streams keys 88 and 89.** Both requests lost their `"latestVersionUnstable": true`
(the diff of `StreamsGroup{Heartbeat,Describe}{Request,Response}.json` between 4.1.2 and 4.2.0), so a 4.2 node lists
them without `unstable.api.versions.enable`; **no field of either request changed**, and the probe body
`ApiVersionProbeTest` sends - the leave of a member of a group that does not exist, and the description of that group
- is the body of 4.1. Two answers changed without a schema change: the `Status` array of a StreamsGroupHeartbeat
answer lost its `"default": "null"`, so an answer the coordinator does not fill carries an **empty** array (`01`)
where a 4.1 node wrote the null `00`; and StreamsGroupDescribe dropped its `TopicPartitions` common structure, which
no field referenced. The 4.3.1 node answers both frames with the **69** (`GroupIdNotFound`, `Group <id> not found.`),
the heartbeat with the empty member id, four zero integers, that empty status array and three null task arrays, the
description with the empty state, a null topology, no member and the authorized operations `-2147483648`
(`ApiVersionProbeTest::testTheStreamsApisAnswerAnUnknownGroupInTheSchemaOfKafka42`). The api version is still 0 in
both directions, and the codes 130 to 132 stay unreached: they answer a topology, which a leave does not carry.

### The 6 error codes

| Code | Constant | Class | Added in | Retriable | Message |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 128 | INVALID_REGULAR_EXPRESSION | `InvalidRegularExpressionException` (the Java class is `InvalidRegularExpression`) | 4.0 | no | The regular expression is not valid. |
| 129 | REBOOTSTRAP_REQUIRED | `RebootstrapRequiredException` | 4.0 | no | Client metadata is stale. The client should rebootstrap to obtain new metadata. |
| 130 | STREAMS_INVALID_TOPOLOGY | `StreamsInvalidTopologyException` | 4.1 | no | The supplied topology is invalid. |
| 131 | STREAMS_INVALID_TOPOLOGY_EPOCH | `StreamsInvalidTopologyEpochException` | 4.1 | no | The supplied topology epoch is invalid. |
| 132 | STREAMS_TOPOLOGY_FENCED | `StreamsTopologyFencedException` | 4.1 | no | The supplied topology epoch is outdated. |
| 133 | SHARE_SESSION_LIMIT_REACHED | `ShareSessionLimitReachedException` | 4.1 | **yes** | The limit of share sessions has been reached. A ShareFetch of the epoch 0 on a node that holds `group.share.max.share.sessions` (2000) sessions; not driven on the shared node — see "ShareAcknowledge API (key 79, v1)". |

`Errors.java` @ 4.3.1 ends at **133**; the retriable flag is the one of the Java class (`RetriableException` for 133
alone). 4.2 and 4.3 added no code.

**Which of them a frame reaches on the node.** The **128** is answered to a ListTransactions **v2** whose
`transactional_id_pattern` RE2/J cannot compile (Kafka 4.1, KIP-1152, see "The transactional id pattern of KIP-1152
(v2)") and to the regex subscription of a ConsumerGroupHeartbeat v1. The **130** to **132** belong to the streams
apis 88 and 89, which this line leaves out, and the **133** to a ShareFetch that opens one share session too many.
The five share-group state apis 83 to 87 answer none of them: their per-partition codes on the node are 0, 31 and
42, next to the coordinator codes of their specifications (see "The share-group state apis (keys 83 to 87) — wire
only").

### What is out of this line by decision

The owner's decisions for the 4.x line (epic [#213](https://github.com/lisachenko/kafka-client/issues/213)):

* **Share groups (KIP-932) are in**, as a share-consumer surface: the apis 76 to 79 and 90 to 92 as client apis, a
  share consumer and its admin methods as the last wave of the line; the coordinator-internal state apis 83 to 87
  **wire only**.
* **The raft-voter apis 80 and 81 get admin methods** on the `kraft.version` 1 node; UpdateRaftVoter (82) is a
  controller-listener api and stays a probe.
* **The transactional producer moves to the transaction protocol v2** of KIP-890 part 2 on a node that finalizes
  `transaction.version` 2, with the v1 path kept for a 3.x node.
* **`group.protocol` keeps the default `classic`** (the default of the Java consumer at 4.3.1 as well).
* **Out**: the streams groups of KIP-1071 (88, 89, the codes 130 to 132 declared only), client metrics beyond the
  wire classes, and every controller-only api beyond a probe.

## What 3.9.2 adds to the 2.8.2 protocol

Ten releases (3.0 to 3.9) add **23 api keys** (65 to 87), **55 new versions of the 65 apis that already existed** —
of which **39** belong to keys the client listener of the node serves, the other 16 to the replication and raft
apis — and the **23 error codes 105 to 127**. Nothing changes in *how* a frame is written: no new primitive type,
no new encoding, no new request or response header, no new message format and no new codec. Every one of the 23
new apis declares `"flexibleVersions": "0+"`, and no api the client listener serves changes its flexible range —
the engine of the 2.x line writes every frame of this one. The raise is smaller than the 2.x one in bytes and larger
in *meaning*: a second consumer group protocol (KIP-848), a second kind of group (share groups, KIP-932, early
access in 3.9), a metadata quorum instead of ZooKeeper (KRaft), tiered storage and client metrics.

Nothing is *removed* either: every version below is still served, which is why the api-key table starts every row
at v0 and why the 669 vectors of the lines below are replayed here unchanged. **Kafka 4.0 is the release that
removes versions**: `4.0.0` drops the versions below the Kafka 2.1 baseline of every api, and the ZooKeeper apis
with ZooKeeper itself. That is the next line's first problem, not this one's.

### The ten minors

The counts are the rows of the api-key table below: new versions of the keys the node serves on its client
listener (the versions of the replication, controller and raft apis in parentheses), read off `validVersions` of
every `*Request.json` at the tags `2.8.2`, `3.0.2`, `3.1.2`, `3.2.3`, `3.3.2`, `3.4.1`, `3.5.2`, `3.6.2`, `3.7.2`,
`3.8.1` and `3.9.2`. A KIP is named only where the version comment of the JSON names it.

|---------|----------|--------------|-----------------|-----------------|
| **3.0** | 65, 66 (67, controller) | **3** | 105 | ListOffsets v7 (the max timestamp of a partition, KIP-734), OffsetFetch v8 (several groups in one request), FindCoordinator v4 (several keys in one request, KIP-699); DescribeTransactions and ListTransactions, whose JSON names no KIP |
| **3.1** | – | **2** | 106 | Fetch v13 (topics named by **id**, KIP-516, with the codes 100 and 106 that come with it), Metadata v12 (a request by topic **id** that the broker honours — v10 carried the field, but "this functionality was not implemented on the server") |
| **3.2** | – | **4** (LeaderAndIsr v6, AlterPartition v1) | – | JoinGroup v8 and LeaveGroup v5 (the *reason* of a rejoin or a leave, KIP-800), JoinGroup v9 (`skip_assignment` in the answer), DescribeLogDirs v3 (a top-level error code in the answer); AlterIsr becomes AlterPartition (KIP-704) |
| **3.3** | – | **8** (AlterPartition v2) | 107, 108 | The three ACL apis v3 (the *user* resource type), DescribeLogDirs v4 (the total and usable bytes of a directory in the answer), CreateDelegationToken v3 (the owner principal) and DescribeDelegationToken v3 (the token requester), UpdateFeatures v1 (`upgrade_type` in place of `allow_downgrade`, and `validate_only`), DescribeQuorum v1 (KIP-836) |

`group.coordinator.rebalance.protocols`, 71 and 72 a client-metrics receiver, 76 to 79 the early-access flag of
KIP-932). Both are the work of the milestone that implements the version, and the "Implemented here" column of the
api-key table says which milestones have not happened yet.

The 22 keys of the 2.x line that a ZooKeeper broker did not serve are not all served by a KRaft node either: of

The constants of all 23 new keys exist in `ApiKeys` so that a probe can name what it did not get. Their JSON uses
no type the engine lacks: the foundation checked every `"type"` of the 23 request and response specifications
against `BinarySchema`, and they are the ones already there — `int8` to `int64`, `uuid`, `bool`, `string`,
`bytes`, arrays and tagged fields.

### The 23 error codes

| Release | Codes | What they belong to |
|---------|-------|---------------------|
| 3.0 | 105 | DescribeTransactions (65): a transactional id the coordinator does not know |
| 3.1 | 106 | A fetch session that mixes topics named by id (Fetch v13) with topics named by name |
| 3.3 | 107, 108 | AlterPartition (56): an ineligible replica in the new ISR, and a leader that changed while the request was applied — two broker→controller codes |
| 3.5 | 109-112 | The offset that moved to tiered storage (Fetch v14, ListOffsets v8, KIP-405), and the first three codes of the KIP-848 protocol: a fenced member epoch, an instance id another member still holds, an assignor the group does not support |
| 3.6 | 113 | The stale member epoch of the same protocol, what an OffsetCommit v9 with an old epoch is answered |
| 3.7 | 114-119 | The endpoint type of DescribeCluster v1 (KIP-919): the wrong endpoint, an unsupported one and an unknown controller id; the two refusals of PushTelemetry (72); and a broker or controller registration the controller considers invalid |
| 3.8 | 120 | The abortable transaction error of KIP-890, which Produce v11, FindCoordinator v5 and the last version of the five transaction apis promise to understand |
| 3.9 | 121-127 | The four share-group codes of KIP-932 (a record state, a share session, its epoch, the state epoch of the share coordinator) and the three voter codes of AddRaftVoter (80) and RemoveRaftVoter (81); none of the seven is reachable on a node of this configuration |

The rows are in the code table of "Error codes". Only **106, 122 and 123** extend `RetriableException` in the Java
client, and they are the three `RetriableException`s here.

### The KRaft node and its listeners

The 2.x line measured a **ZooKeeper** broker; this line measures a **KRaft** node, and that decides which keys an
ApiVersions answer holds before any version does. `ApiVersionManager` @ 3.9.2 answers the apis of the
`ApiMessageType.ListenerType` the request arrived on — `apiKey.inScope(listenerType)` — and the client listeners of
a KRaft node are `broker` listeners, where a ZooKeeper broker's were `zkBroker` ones. Every JSON specification
names its listeners; the `zkBroker`-only apis (4, 5, 6) and the ones that are `zkBroker, controller` (7, 56, 58,
67) are therefore not on the client listener at all, the `controller`-only apis (52, 53, 54, 59, 62, 63, 70, 73,
82) are on 9096 alone, and the apis that are `broker, controller` — 55, 64 and the two voter apis 80 and 81 — are
in the answer of a client for the first time. Two more filters follow:
`ApiVersionsResponse.intersectForwardableApis` drops 71 and 72 while no client-telemetry receiver is configured,
and `ApiKeys.toApiVersion(enableUnstableLastVersion)` leaves out every api whose JSON says
`"latestVersionUnstable": true` — 76 to 79 and 83 to 87, whose only version is the unstable one — while
`unstable.api.versions.enable` is off. **61 keys** remain, against the 56 of the 2.8.2 broker, see
"API keys".

What a KRaft node does with a request is not always what the ZooKeeper broker did either: `KafkaApis` @ 3.9.2 asks
`metadataSupport.requireZkOrThrow(…)` on every path that needs ZooKeeper, and the two such paths a *client* can
reach — OffsetCommit **v0** and OffsetFetch **v0**, the ZooKeeper-stored offsets of `offsets.storage = zookeeper`
— throw an `UnsupportedVersionException`, the error code **35**, from a node. See "Broker quirks and observations".

### The rest of the raise

| Area | 2.8.2 | 3.9.2 | Since |
|---|---|---|---|
| Primitive types | `int8`…`int64`, `string`, `bytes`, arrays and their compact forms, `uuid`, `float64`, `varint`/`varlong` in a record batch | **unchanged** — the foundation read every `"type"` of the new specifications against `BinarySchema` | – |
| Request and response headers | v0 to v2, v0 and v1 | **unchanged** | – |
| Message format | record batch v2 (magic 2) | **unchanged**: magic 2, no new attribute bit, the same four codecs. A 3.9.2 node still down-converts for a Fetch below v4, which is what keeps the vectors of the 0.x lines replayable | – |
| Error codes | -1 … 104 | -1 … **127**: the 23 codes of this line, of which 3 are retriable, 7 belong to share groups and raft voters this line does not speak and 3 to the controller | 3.0-3.9 |
| Api keys | 0 … 64 | 0 … **87**; a KRaft node lists 61 of them on a client listener | 3.0-3.9 |
| Topics | named by name, ids in Metadata v10 and the topic apis | named by **id** in a Fetch v13 and in a Metadata v12 request (KIP-516), with the codes 100 and 106 | 3.1 |
| Group protocol | the classic protocol of JoinGroup/SyncGroup, with static membership | plus the **consumer group protocol of KIP-848**: one ConsumerGroupHeartbeat (68) carries subscription, assignment and liveness, the coordinator assigns, and a member epoch takes the place of the generation — OffsetCommit v9 is the v8 frame that protocol may send, OffsetFetch v9 adds the member id and epoch — next to the classic protocol, which keeps every version | 3.5-3.7 |
| Consumer semantics | leader epochs, fetch sessions, `read_committed`, preferred read replicas | plus the **new leader in the answer** (Produce v10, Fetch v16, KIP-951: a client learns the leader it should have asked without a metadata refresh), the offsets of **tiered storage** (ListOffsets v8 and v9, the code 109 of Fetch v14) and the reason of a rejoin or leave (JoinGroup v8, LeaveGroup v5, KIP-800) | 3.0-3.9 |
| Producer semantics | the five-batch window, the codes 47 and 90 | plus the code **120** of KIP-890: a transaction error the client can abort out of instead of failing the producer, promised by Produce v11 and the transaction apis' last version | 3.8 |
| Feature discovery | ApiVersions v3 | **v4**, the same frame with a supported feature allowed to report the minimum version 0 (KAFKA-17011) — which on a KRaft node is `kraft.version`, the feature that says whether the voter set can be reconfigured at all | 3.9 |
| Security | SASL/PLAIN, SCRAM credentials managed but not used, ACL apis served but unimplemented | the same transport, and the **ACL apis 29 to 31 implemented for the first time** on this line — the node runs `StandardAuthorizer` | – |
| An unparseable frame | the broker closes the connection | to be re-measured on the node; the versions the 2.x line saw the connection close for (Produce v10, Fetch v13, key 65 …) are served here | – |

### What is out of this line by decision

Decisions of the owner, taken before the first milestone:

* **Share groups (76 to 79 and 83 to 87) are out**: early access in 3.9, hidden by `latestVersionUnstable` on a
  node with the default configuration. Their constants and the codes 121 to 124 exist so that a frame can be named.
* **Client metrics (71, 72, 74) are wire only**: classes and vectors of what a node without a client-metrics
  receiver answers, no client method.
* **The raft and controller apis (52 to 54, 58, 59, 62 to 64, 67, 70, 73, 80 to 82) are probe only**, like the
  replication apis of the lines below. **DescribeQuorum (55) is the exception**: it is the one raft api of KIP-595
  that reads instead of writing, a `broker` listener serves it, and this line implements it at v0 to v2.
* **Tiered storage is wire only**: ListOffsets v8 and the code 109 are implemented, no test writes a remote log.
* **SASL stays PLAIN**: no SCRAM, no OAUTHBEARER, no GSSAPI.
* **The ACL apis 29, 30 and 31 are in**, for the first time — the authorizer of the node is what the two lines
  below lacked.
* **The KIP-848 consumer (68, 69, OffsetCommit v9, OffsetFetch v9, ListGroups v5) is in**, as the last wave of
  the line.

## What 2.8.2 adds to the 1.1.1 protocol

*This section is the record of the 2.x line, inherited unchanged: everything it says was measured on the 2.8.2
ZooKeeper broker of that line and is still true of the frames a 3.9.2 node serves, except where "Broker quirks and
observations" says otherwise.*

The 2.x line is the largest raise of this cascade, and it is the first one that changes **how a frame is written**
rather than only what is in it. Nine releases (2.0 to 2.8) add **22 api keys** (43 to 64), **129 new versions of
the 43 apis that already existed**, the **33 error codes 72 to 104**, one new primitive type and one new codec —
and, with KIP-482, a second encoding of every string, byte array and array in the protocol, plus a second request
header and a second response header.

Nothing is *removed*: every version below is still served, which is why the api-key table starts every row at v0
and why the vectors of the four lines below this one are replayed here unchanged.

### The four big additions

| | What | KIP | Release | Where it is in this document |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Flexible versions** — compact strings, compact byte arrays and compact arrays (an unsigned varint `length + 1`, `0` for null), a tagged-field section at the end of every structure and of every body, the **request header v2** and the **response header v1** | 482 | **2.4** | "Flexible versions (KIP-482)" |
| 2 | **Leader epochs in the client's requests** — `current_leader_epoch` on Fetch, ListOffsets and OffsetCommit, the two codes 74/75 that police it, and the epoch a consumer remembers per partition | 320 | **2.1** | "Leader epochs (KIP-320)" |
| 3 | **The zstd codec** — attribute bits `100` of a record batch v2, and the produce and fetch versions that promise a client can read it | 110 | **2.1** | "Compression" |
| 4 | **22 new api keys** — of which a ZooKeeper-backed broker serves **13**: 43 to 51, 56, 57, 60 and 61 | many | 2.2-2.8 | the api-key table below |

| Feature discovery | ApiVersions v1 | **v3**: the client names its own software and version, and the answer carries the supported and finalized **features** of KIP-584 as tagged fields — the read half of UpdateFeatures | 511, 584 | 2.4, 2.7 |

Everything else in this document is the 1.1.1 grammar, unchanged and re-verified against a 2.8.2 broker.

## Implementation model

Protocol classes do not hand-roll `pack()`/`unpack()` calls: every message and DTO declares its binary layout and the
engine reads and writes it. The design came up the cascade from `0.10.x`, which is why the shape of a class here is
the shape it has on the four lines below.

* `Protocol\Kafka\Protocol\BinarySchemaInterface::getScheme(): array` maps a property name to its type.
* `Protocol\Kafka\Protocol\BinarySchema` is the engine: `readObjectFromStream()`, `writeObjectToStream()`,
  `readSingleType()`, `writeSingleType()`, `getObjectTypeSize()`.
* A request extends its parent scheme: `parent::getScheme() + ['topics' => [BinarySchema::TYPE_STRING]]`.
* Arrays are `[ItemType]` for a plain list, `['keyField' => ItemClass::class]` for a list indexed by one of the item
  fields, and gain `BinarySchema::FLAG_NULLABLE => true` when `-1` is a valid count.

The type set of the apis is the one of 0.10, and **Kafka 1.1 adds no primitive type to it**: `TYPE_INT8`,
`TYPE_INT16`, `TYPE_INT32`, `TYPE_INT64`, `TYPE_BOOLEAN`, `TYPE_STRING`, `TYPE_NULLABLE_STRING`, `TYPE_BYTEARRAY`
(nullable) and int32-prefixed arrays. A *request* can carry a nullable array since 0.10 (the topics of Metadata v1
and of OffsetFetch v2, the log directories of DescribeLogDirs v0 and the owners of DescribeDelegationToken v0), so
`null` written as `ff ff ff ff` and `[]` written as `00 00 00 00` are two different requests here.

Kafka 0.11 added one family on top of it, and **only inside a record batch v2** — no request or response body of any
api uses it:

* `TYPE_VARINT_ZIGZAG` (11) — an int32 written zigzag-encoded, 7 bits per byte;
* `TYPE_VARLONG_ZIGZAG` (12) — the same for an int64;
* `TYPE_VARCHAR_ZIGZAG` (13) — a byte array whose length is such a varint, `-1` (`01`) meaning `null`;
* `FLAG_VARARRAY` (14) — an array whose element count is a varint instead of an int32.

`Common\Utils\ByteUtils` holds the zigzag and CRC-32C helpers of `org.apache.kafka.common.utils.ByteUtils`, and
`Stream::readVarint()`/`writeVarint()` the byte loop. **The numbers 5, 6 and 7 stay reserved**: they were
`TYPE_VARINT`, `TYPE_VARLONG` and `TYPE_VARCHAR` of the pre-schema `main`, which wrote *raw* (non-zigzag) varints,
and they are left free so that a reader of an old scheme cannot mistake one for the other.

An api that has more than one version and whose layout changes between them is described by one class per version:
a scheme is a static property of a class, so `OffsetCommitRequest` (the highest version) and `OffsetCommitRequestV0`
differ in their `VERSION` constant, which the version-aware `getScheme()` of the request and of its DTOs follows.
`XRequest` is always the highest version the broker of this line serves, and every `XRequestV<n>` below it only
lowers that constant.

Two defects of the engine of the pre-schema `main` are fixed here: `TYPE_INT8` is read as a **signed** value (the
attributes byte of a message and the error codes are signed), and `TYPE_BYTEARRAY` round-trips `null` as the int32
`-1` that the specification prescribes.

### Flexible versions in the engine (KIP-482)

**Kafka 2.4 gave the protocol a second encoding of the same types, and it is a mode rather than a set of types.**
From the `flexibleVersions` of an api on, *every* string, byte array and array of that version announces its length
as an unsigned varint of `length + 1` (`0` meaning `null`), and *every* structure of it — the body, every nested
structure and the request header — ends in a **tagged-field section**. There is no version in Kafka 2.8.2 that mixes
the two encodings, and the JSON specifications have no way of expressing one: a version is flexible or it is not.

The engine follows that shape exactly. **Flexibility is asked once per message and handed down**, so a DTO never
needs a version of its own and the same `FetchRequestTopic` scheme serves a Fetch v11 and a Fetch v12:

* `Protocol\Kafka\Protocol\FlexibleSchemaInterface::isFlexible()` is the question, and
  `AbstractProtocolMessage` answers it with `VERSION >= FLEXIBLE_VERSION`. A message class declares
  `public const int FLEXIBLE_VERSION = 12;` next to its `VERSION`; the default is `PHP_INT_MAX`, i.e. "never", which
  is what every api of the lines below this one is, and what SaslHandshake (17) and OffsetDelete (47) stay.
* Every method of `BinarySchema` takes the answer as its last parameter — `readSingleType($type, $stream, $path,
  $flexible)`, `writeSingleType($type, $value, $stream, $flexible)`, `getSingleTypeSize($type, $value, $flexible)` —
  and `readObjectFromStream()`, `writeObjectToStream()` and `getObjectTypeSize()` take it as `?bool`, where `null`
  means "ask the class itself". A top-level message is therefore read with `null` and every structure inside it with
  the `true` or `false` that came out of that question.
* `TYPE_STRING`, `TYPE_NULLABLE_STRING`, `TYPE_BYTEARRAY` and every array notation change their encoding with that
  flag and **nothing else changes**: the PHP value of a field is the same in both, which is what makes a scheme
  version-independent. `TYPE_STRING_NEVER_COMPACT` (9) is the one type that ignores the flag — the `client_id` of
  the request header v2, `"flexibleVersions": "none"` in `RequestHeader.json`.
* **Tagged fields are declared in the scheme** as ordinary `property => type` entries whose type is a
  `Protocol\Kafka\Protocol\TaggedField(tag, type, default)`, at the end of the structure:

  ```php
  public static function getScheme(): array
  {
      $body = parent::getScheme() + [
          'errorCode'      => BinarySchema::TYPE_INT16,
          'apiVersions'    => ['apiKey' => ApiVersionsResponseMetadata::class],
          'throttleTimeMs' => BinarySchema::TYPE_INT32,
      ];
      if (static::VERSION >= 3) {
          $body['supportedFeatures']      = new TaggedField(0, ['name' => ApiVersionsSupportedFeature::class], []);
          $body['finalizedFeaturesEpoch'] = new TaggedField(1, BinarySchema::TYPE_INT64, -1);
          $body['finalizedFeatures']      = new TaggedField(2, ['name' => ApiVersionsFinalizedFeature::class], []);
      }

      return $body;
  }
  ```

  The engine takes those entries out of the field sequence, writes them at the end of the structure in ascending
  order of their tag, and **leaves out every field whose value equals its declared default** — the rule of
  `Message.write()` in the Java client, and the reason a captured frame survives a decode and encode round trip. A
  structure of a flexible version that declares no tagged field at all still gets the empty section (`00`), and one
  that is not flexible ignores the declaration altogether.
* A tag that the scheme does not declare is **skipped by its announced size** and kept as raw bytes by every class
  that uses `Protocol\Kafka\Protocol\PreservesUnknownTaggedFields` — every request and response does — so that a
  frame of a later Kafka release survives the round trip instead of losing bytes.
* **A structure of the specification ends in a tagged-field section; a group of fields does not.** The difference is
  invisible in the plain encoding - neither is counted or delimited on the wire - but a flexible version gives every
  real structure a `00` the broker expects and a field group none. Where this package wraps two or more *flat* fields
  of a specification in an object of its own, the field is declared `new InlineStruct(TheClass::class)` instead of
  `TheClass::class`: the scheme of that class is inlined into the enclosing structure and gets no section. The marker
  belongs to the **field**, not to the class - `Common\Security\KafkaPrincipal` is an `InlineStruct` as the `owner`
  of a CreateDelegationToken or DescribeDelegationToken answer, where `PrincipalType` and `PrincipalName` are two
  ordinary fields of the response, and a *real* structure as an entry of the `[]CreatableRenewers` of the request.
  An entry of a `[]Something` array of the specification is never an `InlineStruct`.
* The **headers** are part of the same mechanism: `AbstractRequest::getHeaderVersion()` and
  `AbstractResponse::getHeaderVersion()` are the `ApiKeys.requestHeaderVersion()`/`responseHeaderVersion()` of the
  Java client, and they decide whether the scheme of the header carries a `TYPE_TAG_BUFFER` entry
  (`headerTaggedFields`). The two exceptions of the protocol are two overrides: `ControlledShutdownRequest` answers
  the header v0 for its version 0, and `ApiVersionsResponse` answers the header **v0 for every version**, flexible
  body or not.

A version bump therefore adds a class, a `VERSION` and - when the version is flexible - a `FLEXIBLE_VERSION`, and
never a second scheme for the same structure.

## Protocol primitive types

| Type    | Encoding                                                                         |
|---------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `int8`  | 1 byte, signed                                                                    |
| `int16` | 2 bytes, signed, big endian                                                       |
| `int32` | 4 bytes, signed, big endian                                                       |
| `int64` | 8 bytes, signed, big endian (two's complement)                                    |
| `boolean` | 1 byte: `00` is false, **any** non-zero byte is true; this client writes `01`   |
| `float64` | **Kafka 2.6 (KIP-546).** 8 bytes of an IEEE 754 double in **network order**, `Type.FLOAT64` of the Java client (`ByteBuffer.putDouble`); the quota values of the keys 48 and 49 are the only fields of 2.8.2 that use it. `TYPE_FLOAT64`, `pack('E')` |
| `string`| `int16` length `N` followed by `N` bytes of UTF-8; `N = -1` (`ff ff`) means `null` |
| `bytes` | `int32` length `N` followed by `N` bytes; `N = -1` (`ff ff ff ff`) means `null`    |
| `[foo]` | `int32` element count `N` followed by `N` repetitions of `foo`                     |
| `varint` | **Kafka 0.11, record batch v2 only.** An int32 zigzag-encoded (`0 → 0, -1 → 1, 1 → 2, -2 → 3 …`) and written 7 bits per byte, least significant group first, the high bit set on every byte but the last: 1 to 5 bytes (`ByteUtils.writeVarint` @ 0.11.0.3). `TYPE_VARINT_ZIGZAG` of the engine, `Common\Utils\ByteUtils` for the zigzag step |
| `varlong` | The same encoding of an int64, 1 to 10 bytes. `TYPE_VARLONG_ZIGZAG` |
| varint `bytes` | `varint` length `N` followed by `N` bytes; `N = -1` (`01`) means `null` - the key, value and headers of a record. `TYPE_VARCHAR_ZIGZAG` |
| varint `[foo]` | `varint` element count `N` followed by `N` repetitions of `foo` - the headers of a record. `FLAG_VARARRAY` (the count is zigzag-encoded too) |
| `uuid` | **Kafka 2.8 (KIP-516).** 16 raw bytes, no length prefix; `00…00` is "no id". `TYPE_UUID` |
| `unsigned_varint` | **Kafka 2.4 (KIP-482).** The value itself, 7 bits per byte, least significant group first, the high bit set on every byte but the last: 1 to 5 bytes, **no zigzag step** (`ByteUtils.writeUnsignedVarint` @ 2.8.2). `Stream::readUnsignedVarint()`/`writeUnsignedVarint()`; it carries every length of the flexible encoding |
| `compact_string` | **Flexible versions only.** `unsigned_varint` `N + 1` followed by `N` bytes of UTF-8; `0` means `null` (`compact_nullable_string`), and a non-nullable field that is sent as `0` is a protocol error |
| `compact_bytes` | **Flexible versions only.** The same encoding for a byte array |
| `compact_[foo]` | **Flexible versions only.** `unsigned_varint` `N + 1` element count followed by `N` repetitions of `foo`; `0` means `null` |
| `TAG_BUFFER` | **Flexible versions only.** The tagged-field section that closes every structure: `unsigned_varint` number of fields, then per field an `unsigned_varint` tag, an `unsigned_varint` size and `size` bytes of value, the tags ascending. An empty section is the single byte `00`, and a reader skips a tag it does not know by its size |

**The compact types are not new types but the same ones in a flexible version**, which is why the table above lists
them once: from the `flexibleVersions` of an api on, every `string`, `bytes` and `[foo]` of that version *is* the
compact one and every structure of it ends in a `TAG_BUFFER`. The one field of Kafka 2.8.2 that stays behind is the
`client_id` of the request header v2 (`"flexibleVersions": "none"`).

Byte-exact examples, as implemented by `Protocol\Kafka\IO\Stream`:

| Value                     | Bytes                     |
|---------------------------|---------------------------|
| `int16` `-1`              | `ff ff`                   |
| `int16` `-32768`          | `80 00`                   |
| `int32` `-1`              | `ff ff ff ff`             |
| `int64` `-1`              | `ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff` |
| `string` `null`           | `ff ff`                   |
| `string` `""`             | `00 00`                   |
| `string` `"test"`         | `00 04 74 65 73 74`       |
| `bytes` `null`            | `ff ff ff ff`             |
| `bytes` `""`              | `00 00 00 00`             |
| `boolean` `false` / `true`| `00` / `01`               |
| empty array               | `00 00 00 00`             |
| null array                | `ff ff ff ff`             |
| `varint` `0` / `-1` / `1` | `00` / `01` / `02`        |
| `varint` `64` / `-65`     | `80 01` / `81 01`         |
| `varint` `300`            | `d8 04`                   |
| `varint` `2147483647`     | `fe ff ff ff 0f`          |
| `varint` `-2147483648`    | `ff ff ff ff 0f`          |
| `varlong` `2^31`          | `80 80 80 80 10`          |
| `varlong` `PHP_INT_MAX`   | `fe ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff 01` |
| varint `bytes` `null` / `""` / `de ad be ef` | `01` / `00` / `08 de ad be ef` |
| `unsigned_varint` `0` / `1` / `127` | `00` / `01` / `7f` |
| `unsigned_varint` `128` / `16383` / `16384` | `80 01` / `ff 7f` / `80 80 01` |
| `unsigned_varint` `2^28-1` / `2^28` / `2^32-1` | `ff ff ff 7f` / `80 80 80 80 01` / `ff ff ff ff 0f` |
| `compact_string` `null` / `""` / `"test"` | `00` / `01` / `05 74 65 73 74` |
| `compact_bytes` `null` / `""` / `de ad` | `00` / `01` / `03 de ad` |
| empty `compact_[foo]` / null `compact_[foo]` | `01` / `00` |
| `compact_[foo]` of two items | `03` … |
| empty `TAG_BUFFER` | `00` |
| `TAG_BUFFER` with the int64 tag 1 = 0 | `01 01 08 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00` |

An empty string and a null string are different values on the wire; the client id of a request, for example, is always
an empty string and never null. The same holds for the compact types, where the distinction is `01` against `00` — and
a compact length is never `-1`: the `0` that the `+ 1` frees up is what `null` is written as.

## Common request and response structure

Every request and every response is framed by its size:

```
RequestOrResponse => Size (RequestMessage | ResponseMessage)
  Size => int32
```

`Size` is the length in bytes of everything that follows it. A client reads a response by first reading these four
bytes as an integer `N` and then reading exactly `N` more bytes.

### Requests

There are **three** request headers in Kafka 2.8.2, and `RequestHeader.json` declares all three:

```
RequestHeader (Version: 0) => ApiKey ApiVersion CorrelationId
RequestHeader (Version: 1) => ApiKey ApiVersion CorrelationId ClientId
RequestHeader (Version: 2) => ApiKey ApiVersion CorrelationId ClientId TAG_BUFFER
  ApiKey        => int16
  ApiVersion    => int16
  CorrelationId => int32
  ClientId      => string     (int16 length, never compact)
```

* `ApiKey` — numeric id of the API being invoked (see the table below).
* `ApiVersion` — version of that API; the broker answers in exactly the format that matches the requested version.
* `CorrelationId` — user-supplied value that the broker passes back unmodified.
* `ClientId` — user-supplied identifier of the client application.

**Which header a frame carries follows from its api version and nothing else**, and the broker decides it the same
way the client does: `ApiKeys.requestHeaderVersion(apiVersion)` @ 2.8.2 answers the header **v2** from the first
flexible version of that api on, the header **v0** for the single frame that has no client id — ControlledShutdown
v0 — and the header **v1** everywhere else. The client side of it is
`AbstractRequest::getHeaderVersion()`.

Two consequences a client has to know:

* The `ClientId` keeps its `int16` length prefix **even in the header v2**, where every other string of the frame is
  compact. `RequestHeader.json` marks the field `"flexibleVersions": "none"` with the comment *"older brokers must be
  able to read the request header for any ApiVersionsRequest, even if it is from a newer version"*.
* `RequestHeader.parse` reads the api key and the api version **before** anything validates them, so a frame of a
  version the broker does not serve is read with the header that version *would* have. Asking an unknown version of
  ApiVersions with the old header is therefore a parse failure and costs the connection, while the same frame with
  an empty tag buffer is answered — see "An api the broker does not serve closes the connection".

A Metadata request v0 with client id `test`, correlation id `1` and an empty topic list is therefore:

```
00 00 00 12   Size = 18
00 03         ApiKey = 3 (Metadata)
00 00         ApiVersion = 0
00 00 00 01   CorrelationId = 1
00 04 74 65 73 74   ClientId = "test"
00 00 00 00   [TopicName] = empty
```

and the ApiVersions v3 request of the same client — the first flexible frame this branch sends — is:

```
00 00 00 2c   Size = 44
00 12         ApiKey = 18 (ApiVersions)
00 03         ApiVersion = 3
00 00 00 01   CorrelationId = 1
00 04 74 65 73 74   ClientId = "test"      (int16 length: the one string that stays plain)
00            TAG_BUFFER of the request header v2: no tagged field
18 6c 69 73 61 63 68 65 6e 6b 6f 2d 6b 61 66 6b 61 2d 63 6c 69 65 6e 74
              ClientSoftwareName = "lisachenko-kafka-client"   (compact: 23 + 1 = 0x18)
04 33 2e 39   ClientSoftwareVersion = "3.9"                    (compact: 3 + 1)
00            TAG_BUFFER of the body
```

### Responses

There are **two** response headers, and a response carries the one its api version prescribes
(`ApiKeys.responseHeaderVersion(apiVersion)`, `AbstractResponse::getHeaderVersion()`):

```
ResponseHeader (Version: 0) => CorrelationId
ResponseHeader (Version: 1) => CorrelationId TAG_BUFFER
  Size          => int32
  CorrelationId => int32
```

The broker guarantees that responses on a single connection come back in the order the requests were sent, and every
response repeats the correlation id of its request.

**The header v1 belongs to every flexible version — except one.** The answer of **ApiVersions** (key 18) always
carries the header v0, flexible body or not; the generator writes that exception out by hand, with the comment
*"ApiVersionsResponse always includes a v0 header. See KIP-511 for details."* The reason is the same as for the
plain `client_id` above: a client that guessed the version too high has to be able to read the correlation id and
the error code of the answer without knowing which header the broker used. The v3 answer of the container therefore
opens with the correlation id and the error code directly, and its compact api array follows:

```
00 00 01 9e   Size = 414
00 00 00 6a   CorrelationId = 106          (and no TAG_BUFFER: the response header v0 of this api)
00 00         ErrorCode = 0
39            [ApiKeys] = 56 entries       (compact: 56 + 1 = 0x39)
00 00 00 00 00 09 00                       Produce, v0-v9, and the TAG_BUFFER of the entry
…
00 00 00 00   ThrottleTimeMs = 0
01            TAG_BUFFER of the body: one tagged field
01 08 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00              tag 1 = FinalizedFeaturesEpoch, 8 bytes, 0
```

There is exactly one exception to the request/response symmetry: a Produce request with `RequiredAcks = 0` gets no
response at all.

## API keys

From `clients/src/main/java/org/apache/kafka/common/protocol/ApiKeys.java` @ 4.3.1, which ends at key **92**
(`DELETE_SHARE_GROUP_OFFSETS`), and from the JSON message specifications next to it, which say for every api
which versions are valid, which of them are **flexible** (KIP-482), on which **listener** it is served and whether
its last version is **unstable** (`latestVersionUnstable`). Identifiers follow the classes of the `3.x` line
wherever the concept exists on both, and the Java client's names for what Kafka 4.x adds. Api key 10 is therefore
still called **GroupCoordinator** here, although the sources renamed it to `FindCoordinator` in 0.11 (the 0.8.2
sources called it `ConsumerMetadataRequest`), key 56 is still **AlterIsr** although Kafka 3.2 renamed it
`AlterPartition` (KIP-704), and key 74 is still **ListClientMetricsResources** although Kafka 4.1 renamed it
`ListConfigResources` (KIP-1142).

The table below is not a guess but the literal answer of the node to an **ApiVersions** request (key 18), decoded
by [`tests/Integration/ApiVersionProbeTest.php`](../../tests/Integration/ApiVersionProbeTest.php) and measured
with `Client::apiVersions()` on the PLAINTEXT listener of the 4.3.1 node: error code 0, throttle time 0, a
finalized-features epoch that is the offset of the metadata log and therefore never the same twice, seven
finalized features (see the sources at the top of this document), and **75 keys**, `key:min-max`:

```
0:0-13  1:4-18  2:1-11  3:0-13  8:2-10  9:1-10  10:0-6  11:0-9  12:0-4  13:0-5  14:0-5  15:0-6  16:0-5  17:0-1
18:0-4  19:2-7  20:1-6  21:0-2  22:0-5  23:2-4  24:0-5  25:0-4  26:0-5  27:1-2  28:0-5  29:1-3  30:1-3  31:1-3
32:1-4  33:0-2  34:1-2  35:1-5  36:0-2  37:0-3  38:1-3  39:1-2  40:1-2  41:1-3  42:0-2  43:0-2  44:0-1  45:0-1
46:0-0  47:0-0  48:0-1  49:0-1  50:0-0  51:0-0  55:0-2  57:0-2  60:0-2  61:0-0  64:0-0  65:0-0  66:0-2  68:0-1
69:0-1  74:0-1  75:0-0  76:1-1  77:1-1  78:1-2  79:1-2  80:0-1  81:0-0  83:0-0  84:0-0  85:0-1  86:0-0  87:0-1
88:0-0  89:0-0  90:0-1  91:0-0  92:0-0
```

The same test sends a real frame of every key at the **maximum version** of the table — with the request header
v2 and a compact body wherever that version is flexible — one frame above every one of them, and one frame of every
version **below** a minimum: all of those close the connection (see "An api the broker does not serve closes the
connection").

**A 4.3.1 KRaft node answers with 75 keys** where the 3.9.2 node of the 3.x line answered 61. The fourteen new
rows are the share-group apis 76 to 79 and their state apis 83 to 87, which Kafka 4.1 made stable (3.9 hid them
as unstable), and the five keys 88 to 92 Kafka 4.1 added. Of the 93 keys of `ApiKeys.java` @ 4.3.1, eighteen are
not in the answer, for three reasons:

* **4, 5, 6 and 7 have no version at all**: Kafka 4.0 removed ZooKeeper, and with it `LeaderAndIsr`,
  `StopReplica`, `UpdateMetadata` and `ControlledShutdown` (`"validVersions": "none"`, no listener). A frame of any
  of them ends in `InvalidRequestException: Unsupported api with key 7 (ControlledShutdown) and version 0`.
* **52, 53, 54, 56, 58, 59, 62, 63, 67, 70, 73 and 82 are `controller` apis** — the raft apis `Vote`,
  `BeginQuorumEpoch`, `EndQuorumEpoch` and `FetchSnapshot`, `AlterPartition`, `Envelope`, the lifecycle apis
  `BrokerRegistration`, `BrokerHeartbeat`, `AllocateProducerIds`, `ControllerRegistration` and
  `AssignReplicasToDirs`, and `UpdateRaftVoter` — served on the CONTROLLER listener 9096 inside the container and
  nowhere a client of this repository connects.
* **71 and 72 are hidden while no client-telemetry receiver is configured**, as on the 3.9.2 node: both are
  `broker` apis and answered, but the answer of ApiVersions drops their rows. `ListClientMetricsResources` (74)
  stays.

**Kafka 4.0 is the first release that raises a minimum** (KIP-896, see "What 4.3.1 adds to the 3.9.2 protocol"):
fifteen rows of the answer start above 0, the four share-group apis start at 1 because their early-access v0 was
dropped, and **Produce** is the one row whose answer and behaviour disagree — it reports the minimum 0, and every
frame of its v0, v1 and v2 is refused (`ApiKeys.PRODUCE_API_VERSIONS_RESPONSE_MIN_VERSION`, KAFKA-18659). A client
of this line reads the `min_version` of the answer as well as the `max_version`.

The columns:

* **Versions served (4.3.1)** is the range the node reports, which is the `validVersions` of the JSON specification
  for every key in the answer (Produce aside). A key that is not in the answer says so, and why.
* **Flexible from** is the first version whose frame is written with the compact types and the tagged fields of
  KIP-482 (`flexibleVersions` of the *request*); `–` means the api never became flexible (or, for 4 to 7, has no
  version left). No 4.x release moved the flexible version of an api, and every api Kafka 4.x added is flexible
  from its version 0.
* **What Kafka 4.x added** names every version above the 3.9.2 ceiling, every version Kafka 4.0 removed, and the
  minor release, verified against the tags `4.0.0` to `4.3.1`; **What Kafka 3.x added** is the column of the 3.x
  line, verified against the tags `3.0.2` to `3.9.2`. A KIP is named only where the version comment of the JSON
  names it.
* **Implemented here** lists the versions this branch has a class for; the one in **bold** is the version the
  client sends. **The 4.x line is built one Kafka minor at a time**, and a version the node serves that the branch
  has not reached yet is named as *not yet implemented on this line*, with the release that added it. The rows
  either name the version the client sends, or say **by design** why this repository does not implement the api at
  all — the broker-to-broker and controller apis, which are probed and never sent in earnest — or **by decision**
  what the owner decided for this line: share groups **in** (a share consumer), the share-group state apis **wire
  only**, the raft-voter apis 80 and 81 **admin methods**, the streams groups and client metrics beyond the wire
  **out**. A removed version keeps its class for the wire vectors of the lines below.

| 84 | ReadShareGroupState | v0 | 0 | v0 stable 4.1 | v0 3.9 | **v0, wire only by decision** (Kafka 4.1, the share coordinator's own apis of KIP-932: classes and vectors, no client method) |
| 85 | WriteShareGroupState | v0, v1 | 0 | v0 stable 4.1, v1 4.2 | v0 3.9 | **v0, wire only by decision** (Kafka 4.1, the share coordinator's own apis of KIP-932: classes and vectors, no client method) — *not yet implemented on this line*: v1 (4.2) |
| 86 | DeleteShareGroupState | v0 | 0 | v0 stable 4.1 | v0 3.9 | **v0, wire only by decision** (Kafka 4.1, the share coordinator's own apis of KIP-932: classes and vectors, no client method) |
| 87 | ReadShareGroupStateSummary | v0, v1 | 0 | v0 stable 4.1, v1 4.2 | v0 3.9 | **v0, wire only by decision** (Kafka 4.1, the share coordinator's own apis of KIP-932: classes and vectors, no client method) — *not yet implemented on this line*: v1 (4.2) |
| 88 | StreamsGroupHeartbeat | v0 | 0 | v0 4.1 (KIP-1071, unstable), stable 4.2 | – | no — **out by decision** (KIP-1071 streams groups): the constant and a probe |
| 89 | StreamsGroupDescribe | v0 | 0 | v0 4.1 (KIP-1071, unstable), stable 4.2 | – | no — **out by decision** (KIP-1071 streams groups): the constant and a probe |
| 90 | DescribeShareGroupOffsets | v0, v1 | 0 | v0 4.1 (KIP-932), v1 4.2 | – | **v0, wire classes** (Kafka 4.1, KIP-932: an unknown or classic group answers 0 with the start offset -1, never the 69); the admin method comes with the share consumer — *not yet implemented on this line*: v1 (4.2) |
| 91 | AlterShareGroupOffsets | v0 | 0 | v0 4.1 (KIP-932) | – | **v0, wire classes** (Kafka 4.1, KIP-932: it creates the share group, the 69 of a classic group, the 68 of a group with members); the admin method comes with the share consumer |
| 92 | DeleteShareGroupOffsets | v0 | 0 | v0 4.1 (KIP-932) | – | **v0, wire classes** (Kafka 4.1, KIP-932: the 69 of an unknown group, the 68 of a group with members); the admin method comes with the share consumer |

The keys **4, 5, 6, 27 and 56** were answered by the 2.8.2 broker of the 2.x line like any other request, and its
probe sent one frame of each without changing anything: 4, 5 and 6 with the controller epoch `-1` and the broker
epoch `-1`, which are stale, so the broker answered the error code **11** (`StaleControllerEpoch`) and changed
nothing; 27 with an empty marker array, which it answered with an empty array of its own; and 56 (`AlterIsr`) with
the broker epoch `-1`, answered with the code **77** (`StaleBrokerEpoch`). On the 3.9.2 and the 4.3.1 node only
**27** is still in the table (at v1 and v2 on 4.3.1); a frame of 4, 5, 6 or 56 on a client listener costs the
connection.

**The rows no longer all start at the minimum version 0.** That had been true from Kafka 1.0, which gave the
client-id-less frame of ControlledShutdown v0 a request header schema of its own (a 0.9 to 0.11 broker reported
`MinVersion = 1` for key 7), to Kafka 3.9. Kafka **4.0** raised fifteen minimums (KIP-896), and this line is the
first that has to read the `min_version` of the answer before it sends.

**The set of keys is not a constant of the release**, and a client must read the table it gets instead of the one
printed here: the listener decides it (above), and so do the client-metrics receiver, `unstable.api.versions.enable`
and the finalized features — the 3.9.2 node of the 3.x line hid the share-group apis as unstable, the 4.3.1 node
serves them because Kafka 4.1 made them stable and its `share.version` is finalized at 1.

**The ACL apis 29, 30 and 31 are in on this line**, for the first time: the two lines below left them by decision,
because they only do anything on a broker configured with an `authorizer.class.name`, and every wire vector of this
repository comes from a real broker. The node carries one —
`authorizer.class.name=org.apache.kafka.metadata.authorizer.StandardAuthorizer`, `allow.everyone.if.no.acl.found=false`,
and `super.users=User:ANONYMOUS;User:admin;User:kafkatest`, so that every test of the suite keeps working as a super
user while the SASL user `acltest`, the one principal that is not one, is what an ACL can be written for and
measured against. The 2.8.2 broker answered every one of the three with **54** (`SecurityDisabled`) and
`No Authorizer is configured on the broker`; what the node answers was measured for the ACL ticket of the 3.3 wave
and is this. **Since that wave the three apis are implemented** - `AdminClient::describeAcls()`, `createAcls()`
and `deleteAcls()` at the version 3 of Kafka 3.3 - and the sections
"DescribeAcls API (key 29, v0 to v3)", "CreateAcls API (key 30, v0 to v3)" and
"DeleteAcls API (key 31, v0 to v3)" carry the whole measurement; what follows here is the first look the
foundation took:

**A DescribeAcls v3 whose filter matches everything** — resource type, pattern type, operation and permission type
all `ANY` (1), every name null — is answered to each of the three super users (`ANONYMOUS` on the PLAINTEXT
listener, `admin` and `kafkatest` over SASL_PLAINTEXT) with the same nine bytes,
`00000000 0000 01 01 00`: the throttle time, the code **0**, an `error_message` that is the **empty string** (the
compact `01`, not the null `00` — the generated `DescribeAclsResponseData` initialises it with `""` and the
handler never sets it — `AclApis.handleDescribeAcls` @ 3.9.2 sets the throttle time and the resources and
nothing else) and an empty resource array. The same filter sent by **`acltest`** is answered **31**
(`ClusterAuthorizationFailed`) — the api asks the authorizer for `DESCRIBE` on the **CLUSTER** resource before it
reads the filter at all — with an empty resource array and an `error_message` that is the whole request object of
the broker:

```
Request Request(processor=8, connectionId=172.18.0.2:9094-172.18.0.1:44220-27,
session=org.apache.kafka.network.Session@2aa27ff7, listenerName=ListenerName(SASL_PLAINTEXT),
securityProtocol=SASL_PLAINTEXT, buffer=null, envelope=None) is not authorized.
```

— `AuthHelper.authorizeClusterOperation` @ 3.9.2 builds the `ClusterAuthorizationException` with
`s"Request $request is not authorized."`, so the sentence carries a processor number, a connection id, the
identity hash of a Java object and the listener of the connection. It is a diagnosis for a log file and never a
second source of truth: the code 31 is.

**What a non-empty answer looks like** was measured with two acls written by
`kafka-acls.sh --bootstrap-server localhost:9092 --add --allow-principal User:acltest` (a literal `TOPIC` and a
prefixed `GROUP` resource) and removed again afterwards; the same filter then answers, for a super user:

```
00 00 00 00                                       # throttle_time_ms
00 00                                             # error_code = 0
01                                                # error_message = "" (compact, the default of the field)
03                                                # [resources] = 2, as the compact count 2 + 1
  02                                              #   resource_type = 2 (TOPIC)
  13 74342d61636c2d70726f62652d746f706963         #   resource name, compact: "t4-acl-probe-topic"
  03                                              #   pattern_type = 3 (LITERAL)
  03                                              #   [acls] = 2
    0d 557365723a61636c74657374                   #     principal, compact: "User:acltest"
    02 2a                                         #     host, compact: "*"
    03                                            #     operation = 3 (READ)
    03                                            #     permission_type = 3 (ALLOW)
    00                                            #     the tag buffer of the acl
    0d 557365723a61636c74657374  02 2a  08 03 00  #     the same principal, operation 8 (DESCRIBE)
  00                                              #   the tag buffer of the resource
  03                                              #   resource_type = 3 (GROUP)
  0e 74342d61636c2d70726f62652d                   #   resource name, compact: "t4-acl-probe-"
  04                                              #   pattern_type = 4 (PREFIXED)
  02                                              #   [acls] = 1
    0d 557365723a61636c74657374  02 2a  03 03 00  #     User:acltest, host *, READ, ALLOW
  00                                              #   the tag buffer of the resource
00                                                # the tag buffer of the body
```

One resource per pattern, its acls inside it, the principal as the `User:name` string the authorizer stores and
the host as the literal `*` of an acl that names no host. The codes are the ones of
`org.apache.kafka.common.acl.AclOperation` and `AclPermissionType` @ 3.9.2 and the pattern types those of
`PatternType` (KIP-290): `LITERAL` 3 and `PREFIXED` 4 in a stored acl, with `ANY` 1 and `MATCH` 2 in a *filter*
alone; `ALLOW` is the permission type 3 and `DENY` the 2. An ACL is a write of the
controller like every other one, so a describe that follows a create reads the image of the broker and may need a
second look.

**The four delegation-token apis 38 to 41 are served and answered 64 on the PLAINTEXT listener of the 2.8.2
broker.** A token is only issued over a channel that authenticated a real principal, so `KafkaApis` @ 2.8.2 refused
the request with `DELEGATION_TOKEN_REQUEST_NOT_ALLOWED` before it read the body. The node carries a
`delegation.token.secret.key` like the 2.8.2 image did, so the answer is not expected to be the 61
(`DELEGATION_TOKEN_AUTH_DISABLED`) of a broker without one, and the apis are exercised over the SASL listeners 9094
and 9095, where the principal of the connection is the SASL/PLAIN user. *Using* a token afterwards needs SASL/SCRAM,
which this client does not implement.

### An api the broker does not serve closes the connection

**This is the behaviour that changed in Kafka 0.10 and that every release since keeps, and it is the one a client of
the two lowest lines gets wrong.** A 0.9.0.1 broker silently *dropped* a frame it could not parse and kept the
connection open; every broker from 0.10.2.2 to 2.8.2 **closes the connection**.

*Every frame and log line quoted in this subsection was measured on the 2.8.2 ZooKeeper broker of the 2.x line.*
*A 3.9.2 node serves the versions named here — OffsetCommit v9, the api key 65 — and the probe of the foundation
measured its edges anew: the first frame above the table (OffsetCommit v10, Produce v12, Fetch v18, Metadata v13,
the key 88) still **closes the connection**, but the version check moved out of the message class into
`SocketServer.parseRequestHeader → ApiVersionManager.isApiEnabled(apiKey, apiVersion)` @ 3.9.2, before any body is
read, so that every refusal — a version above the table, a `zkBroker` or `controller` api, an unstable api — logs
the one line `Received request api key OFFSET_COMMIT with version 10 which is not enabled`; a key above
`ApiKeys.java` (88) still dies in the header parser (`Error parsing request header. Our best guess of the apiKey
is: 88`), and a body that does not match its schema still ends in a `BufferUnderflowException` behind `Error getting
request for apiKey: …`. Two apis of the node do something a 2.8.2 broker never did: they answer **nothing** to a
well-formed frame and keep the connection open — an OffsetFetch v9 with an empty `groups` array (the handler runs,
then `RequestChannel.sendResponse` fails in `RequestMetrics.markErrorMeter` with `NoSuchElementException: key not
found: null`, logged as `Unexpected error handling request`) and an AddPartitionsToTxn v5 with an empty
`transactions` array (`addResultAndMaybeSendResponse` sends when every transaction has answered, which zero
transactions never do). → "Broker quirks and observations".*

*The 4.3.1 node of this line closes the connection in every one of those cases, and in one more: a version
**below** the minimum of its table, which is new with Kafka 4.0 (KIP-896). The log lines changed again, and the
probe of the foundation measured them: a version below or above the table, Produce v0 to v2 included, is
`UnsupportedVersionException: Received request for api with key 0 (Produce) and unsupported version 2`; a key of
the controller listener or one of the four ZooKeeper apis without a version is `InvalidRequestException:
Unsupported api with key 7 (ControlledShutdown) and version 0`; a key `ApiKeys.java` @ 4.3.1 cannot name is
`Error parsing request header. Our best guess of the apiKeyId is: 93`, and so, oddly, is **WriteTxnMarkers v0**,
whose removed version no longer has a request header version to parse it with; a body that does not match its
schema is still `Error getting request for apiKey: JOIN_GROUP, apiVersion: 0` with the exception behind it.*

What changed with the generated message classes of Kafka 2.4 is only the *reason* the broker logs.
`RequestContext.parseRequest()` @ 2.8.2 parses every incoming frame with the `<Api>RequestData` class of the version
in its header, and that class refuses a version it does not know with an `UnsupportedVersionException`;
`Processor.parseRequestHeader` refuses an api key that is not enabled on the listener and one that `ApiKeys.forId()`
cannot name at all; and a body that does not match the schema of its version still ends in a
`BufferUnderflowException` or a `SchemaException`. `SocketServer.processCompletedReceives` wraps all of them in an
`InvalidRequestException` and closes the channel. All five frames below were sent to the container of this line:

```
ERROR Closing socket for 172.18.0.2:9092-172.18.0.1:49438-545 because of error (kafka.network.Processor)
org.apache.kafka.common.errors.InvalidRequestException: Error getting request for apiKey: OFFSET_COMMIT,
apiVersion: 9, connectionId: …, listenerName: ListenerName(PLAINTEXT), principal: User:ANONYMOUS
Caused by: org.apache.kafka.common.errors.UnsupportedVersionException: The OFFSET_COMMIT protocol does not
support version 9
```

```
ERROR Closing socket for … because of error (kafka.network.Processor)
org.apache.kafka.common.errors.InvalidRequestException: Received request api key VOTE which is not enabled
```

```
ERROR Closing socket for … because of error (kafka.network.Processor)
org.apache.kafka.common.errors.InvalidRequestException: Error parsing request header. Our best guess of the
apiKey is: 65
Caused by: java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Unexpected api key: 65
```

```
ERROR Closing socket for … because of error (kafka.network.Processor)
org.apache.kafka.common.errors.InvalidRequestException: Error getting request for apiKey: JOIN_GROUP,
apiVersion: 1, connectionId: …, listenerName: ListenerName(PLAINTEXT), principal: User:ANONYMOUS
Caused by: org.apache.kafka.common.protocol.types.SchemaException: Error reading field 'member_id': Error reading
string of length 25455, only 10 bytes available
```

```
ERROR Closing socket for … because of error (kafka.network.Processor)
```
