`__cluster_metadata`, partition **0** - with a raft protocol, and everything ZooKeeper used to hold is a record in
that log. This api is how a client reads the state of that quorum: who leads it, in which epoch, how far it is
replicated and how far behind every replica of it is. `Admin.describeMetadataQuorum()` sends exactly one request,
the one {@see \Protocol\Kafka\Protocol\Request\DescribeQuorumRequest::metadataQuorum()} builds, and
`AdminClient::describeMetadataQuorum()` answers the `QuorumInfo` of that partition.

**It is the one raft api of KIP-595 a client can send.** `Vote` (52), `BeginQuorumEpoch` (53), `EndQuorumEpoch`
(54) and `FetchSnapshot` (59) are `controller` apis and are not in the table of a client listener at all, while
`DescribeQuorumRequest.json` @ 3.3.2 is `"listeners": ["broker", "controller"]`. A 2.8.2 broker with ZooKeeper has
no quorum to describe and does not serve the key on a client listener either: every version of it closes the
connection there.

**There is no `throttle_time_ms`.** The answer opens with the top-level error code instead - the api is not part
of the quota machinery of KIP-219 - and up to the version 1 there is no `error_message` next to it either; the
version 2 of Kafka 3.9 (KIP-853) adds one, together with the nodes of the quorum and the directory ids of its
replicas.

Measured on the 3.9.2 node, a single **combined** node (`process.roles=broker,controller`); the last column is what
the **version 2** adds to the same question:

| Request | Answer (v0, v1) | What v2 adds |
|---|---|---|
| `__cluster_metadata` partition 0 | top-level **0**; the leader is the node id **1** in the epoch **1**, the high watermark is the offset of the metadata log, **one voter** - the node itself, with its own log end offset - and **no observer at all** | two `error_message` fields that are the **empty string**, the **zero** directory id of that voter and a `nodes` array with the node 1 at `CONTROLLER://localhost:9096`; 137 bytes against the 88 of the version 1 |
| an ordinary topic, partition 0 | top-level **0**, and the partition carries **3** (`UnknownTopicOrPartition`). Every other field of that entry is the zero of its type - the `leader_id` is **0**, not the -1 that "unknown" would be - and both replica arrays are empty | the sentence `This server does not host this topic-partition.` in the partition, and an **empty** `nodes` array: the node writes the array from a quorum it really described |
| no topic at all | top-level **0** with an empty topic array: nine bytes, the shortest answer of this api | eleven bytes - the empty error message and the empty `nodes` array cost one byte each |
| the same request as the SASL user `acltest` | top-level **31** (`ClusterAuthorizationFailed`) with **no topic at all**: the api needs `Describe` on the *cluster*, and this version has no `error_message` to say so | it does now: `Cluster authorization failed.` |

A node that is both broker and controller is a **voter** and never an observer: `CurrentObservers` is empty here,
and `kafka-metadata-quorum.sh --bootstrap-server localhost:9092 describe --status` prints the same thing.
A separate broker of a cluster whose controllers are their own processes is the observer case, which this
one-node container cannot show.

Error codes observed on the container:

| Code | Where | Request that produces it |
|------|-------|--------------------------|
| 0    | top level | A principal that may describe the cluster, whatever the request asks about |
| 31   | top level | `ClusterAuthorizationFailed` — a principal without `Describe` on the cluster; the whole answer is the code and an empty topic array |
| 3    | per partition | A topic or partition that is not replicated by a raft quorum, i.e. anything but `__cluster_metadata`-0 |

### The two timestamps of a replica state (v1, KIP-836)

Kafka **3.3** raised the api to the version 1, and the comment above its `validVersions` says what for: "Version 1
adds additional fields in the response. The request is unchanged (KIP-836)". The two fields are
`LastFetchTimestamp` and `LastCaughtUpTimestamp` of every `ReplicaState`, both `int64`, both `ignorable` with the
default **-1**, both milliseconds of the **leader's** wall clock:

* `LastFetchTimestamp` is when the leader last answered a fetch of that replica;
* `LastCaughtUpTimestamp` is the append time of the offset the replica last fetched, i.e. how far back the data it
  holds reaches.

Without them a client sees a `log_end_offset` and cannot tell a follower that is *behind* from one that is
**gone**: the stale offset of a dead voter looks exactly like the offset of a slow one. KIP-836 -
*"Addition of Information in DescribeQuorumResponse about Voter Lag"* - is what
`kafka-metadata-quorum.sh describe --replication` prints as `LastFetchTimestamp` and `LastCaughtUpTimestamp`, and
what the lag columns next to them are computed from.

**The `about` of `LastFetchTimestamp` is wrong about the leader, and the node proves it.** The specification says
the field "is reported as -1 both for the current leader or if it is unknown for a voter", but
`LeaderState.describeReplicaState` @ 3.3.2 sets **both** timestamps to `currentTimeMs` when the entry is the
leader's own, and the 3.9.2 node answers exactly that: the one voter of the container reports the same real
millisecond in both fields, a value that moves with every request. The -1 is what a *follower* the leader has not
heard from yet carries, which a one-node quorum has no way to show.

A version 0 answer has neither field, and `AdminClient::describeMetadataQuorum()` reports both as **null** then -
the empty `OptionalLong` of `QuorumInfo.ReplicaState` @ 3.3.2, which is also what the -1 of the wire becomes.

### The nodes, the directory ids and the error messages of KIP-853 (v2)

Kafka **3.9** raised the api to the version 2, and the comment above its `validVersions` @ 3.9.2 names the KIP:
"Version 2 adds ErrorMessage, Nodes, ErrorMessage in ParitionData, ReplicaDirectoryId in ReplicaState (KIP-853)"
(the typo is the specification's). KIP-853 is what makes a KRaft quorum **reconfigurable** - a voter can be added
to it and removed from it while it runs, through the apis 80 and 81 - and the four fields it adds here are what a
client needs before it may do that:

* **`ReplicaDirectoryId`** (uuid, inside every replica state, in front of the log end offset and *not* appended
  like the timestamps of KIP-836). Together with the replica id it is the **key** of a voter: a node that loses its
  disk and comes back with a fresh directory is not the replica that left, whatever its id says, and a
  reconfiguration that could not tell the two apart would let a re-imaged node vote with an empty log.
* **`Nodes`**, a top-level array next to the topics: one entry per node of the quorum with its id and its
  listeners, each a name, a host and a **`Port`**. The replica states name a voter by two ids and never by an
  address, so this array is the only place in the answer where an id can be resolved to an endpoint.
* **`ErrorMessage`**, once at the top level and once in every partition, both nullable. They carry the sentence
  the error code used to leave to the reader.

**The `Port` is a `uint16`, and it is the first and only field of the client-facing protocol that is one.**
`Type.UINT16` reads the two big-endian bytes of an int16 without the sign, because a port runs to 65535 and an
int16 turns everything above 32767 into a negative number. `Protocol\Kafka\Protocol\BinarySchema` gained
`TYPE_UINT16` for this field and for nothing else.

What the node answers is the smallest possible case of all four, and one of them is a **negative** result worth
writing down:

* The `nodes` array names the node id **1** with one listener, `CONTROLLER` at `localhost:9096` — the controller
  listener *inside* the container, which no client of this repository ever connects to. A combined node answers
  its controller endpoint here and not the PLAINTEXT 9092 the request arrived on: the array describes the raft
  quorum, not the broker.
* Every `replica_directory_id` is the **zero uuid**, although `meta.properties` of the container carries a real
  `directory.id` (`UZcrwW8KpJUY7I9lFtsjSA`). The reason is the feature `kraft.version`: the node supports 0 to 1
  and has **finalized 0**, which is the static `controller.quorum.voters` of KIP-595, and a static voter set has no
  directory ids to report. The same 0 is why the apis 80 and 81 refuse every frame, see "The raft-voter apis (keys
  80 and 81) and the share groups — probe only".
* Both `error_message` fields are the **empty string** where there is no error, not the null the specification
  defaults them to: the generated `DescribeQuorumResponseData` initialises them with `""` and the handler sets
  them only when it has something to say. The same thing was measured at DescribeAcls in the 3.3 wave, and it is
  the answer to "is a null the same as an empty string here" — on the wire they are one byte apart, `00` against
  `01`, and this api writes the `01`.
* A partition the node could not describe carries its message: `This server does not host this topic-partition.`
  for the **3** of a topic that no raft quorum replicates, and the top level carries `Cluster authorization
  failed.` for the **31** of a principal without `Describe` on the cluster.

**(4.x) The 4.3.1 node answers the real directory id.** Its storage was formatted `--standalone`, the way the
release formats a combined node, so its quorum is the **dynamic** one of KIP-853 and `kraft.version` is finalized
at **1**: the one voter reports the `directory.id` of its `meta.properties` - `7QxpXGVBQTWaHmiG7IDrEQ` on the node
the vectors were captured on, the same value `kafka-metadata-quorum.sh describe --status` prints as its
`directoryId` - and that key, `(1, 7QxpXGVBQTWaHmiG7IDrEQ)`, is what AddRaftVoter and RemoveRaftVoter compare (see
"AddRaftVoter API (key 80, v0 and v1)"). Everything else of the answer is the answer of the 3.9.2 node: the one voter, no
observer, the empty error messages and the `nodes` array with `CONTROLLER` at `localhost:9096`
(`describequorum.response.v2.kraft-version-1`).

`AdminClient::describeMetadataQuorum()` sends the version 2 and answers a `QuorumInfo` that carries the nodes as
`Admin\QuorumNode` objects with `Admin\RaftVoterEndpoint` endpoints (`QuorumInfo.Node` and `RaftVoterEndpoint` of
the Java client @ 3.9.2; the `Node` of the Java nested class is `QuorumNode` here, because
`Protocol\Kafka\Common\Node` is the broker of a Metadata answer). `Admin\ReplicaState` gained
`$replicaDirectoryId` with a `replicaDirectoryIdAsString()` next to it, and against a peer that only serves the
version 1 or 0 the map is empty and every directory id is the zero uuid.

## The raft-voter apis (keys 80 and 81) and the share groups — probe only

**(4.x) What this section describes is the 3.9.2 node of the 3.x line.** On the 4.3.1 node of this line the quorum
is dynamic and `kraft.version` is finalized at 1, so the raft-voter apis 80 and 81 are answered past the feature
check, and the owner's decision 3 of the line gave them message classes and admin methods: see "AddRaftVoter API
(key 80, v0 and v1)" and "RemoveRaftVoter API (key 81, v0)" below. Key 82 is still a controller-listener api and a probe,
and the share-group apis 76 to 79 are spoken since Kafka 4.1: see "Share groups (KIP-932)".

Kafka 3.9 adds twelve api keys, and this client implements none of them. Three are the **raft-voter** apis of
KIP-853 — 80 `AddRaftVoter`, 81 `RemoveRaftVoter` and 82 `UpdateRaftVoter` — and nine are the **share groups** of
KIP-932 — 76 to 79 and 83 to 87. Both groups are decisions of the owner (see "What is out of this line by
decision"): the raft apis are probe only, like every other api that reconfigures a cluster from the inside, and
share groups are early access in 3.9 and out. There are no message classes for any of the twelve, and there are no
wire vectors either, because a vector of this repository is a frame a class of this repository replays. What there
is, is a measurement, and it is the one the error codes 121 to 127 hang on.

**The share-group apis are not refused, they are not there.** All nine carry `"latestVersionUnstable": true` in
their JSON @ 3.9.2, so `ApiKeys.toApiVersion(enableUnstableLastVersion = false)` leaves them out of the ApiVersions
answer altogether and `ApiVersionManager.isApiEnabled` then refuses every version of them. A ShareGroupHeartbeat
v0 with an empty body and a request header v2 therefore ends the way a `zkBroker` api ends — the node **closes the
connection** while it parses the header, and the log says

```
Received request api key SHARE_GROUP_HEARTBEAT with version 0 which is not enabled
```

— and the same for 77, 78, 79 and 83 to 87. `unstable.api.versions.enable=true` would put them in the table; the
node does not set it, and a client cannot tell the difference between "early access and hidden" and "not
implemented" from the outside. **The four share-group error codes 121 to 124 are therefore declared on this line
and unreachable on this node.**

**The two raft-voter apis are in the table** — 80 and 81 are `"listeners": ["controller", "broker"]`, so a client
listener serves them and a broker forwards them to the controller — **and every frame of them is refused, in three
different places.** The probe sends each of them three times, with a voter that no cluster has and a directory id
drawn at random, so that nothing could be reconfigured even if the node allowed it:

| Frame | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| a **foreign** cluster id (`not-this-cluster`) | **104** `InconsistentClusterId` | `The given id "not-this-cluster" doesn't match the cluster id "<id>"` |
| the real cluster id (or a **null** one, which the check accepts) and a voter key the api cannot read — the zero directory id, no listener | **42** `InvalidRequest` | `Add voter request didn't include a valid voter` / `Remove voter request didn't include a valid voter` |
| the real cluster id and a **well-formed** voter — a random directory id and one `CONTROLLER` endpoint | **35** `UnsupportedVersion` | `Cluster doesn't support adding voter because the kraft.version feature is 0` / `… removing voter …` |

The order is the order of the checks in `KafkaRaftClient.handleAddVoterRequest` @ 3.9.2: the cluster id first, the
voter key second, the feature last. And the last one is the answer to the question the codes **125** `InvalidVoterKey`,
**126** `DuplicateVoter` and **127** `VoterNotFound` were declared for: **a 3.9.2 node with the default
configuration never writes one of them.** The reconfiguration of KIP-853 is gated on the feature `kraft.version`,
which this node supports at 0 to 1 and has **finalized at 0** — the static `controller.quorum.voters` of KIP-595 —
and a static voter set is refused before a voter is ever compared to the quorum. The three codes are declared here
and observed nowhere; raising the feature to the level 1 is a one-way change of a cluster's metadata and is not
something a test suite of this repository does to the node it shares with three other agents.

Key **82** `UpdateRaftVoter` is `"listeners": ["controller"]` and is not on a client listener at all: every version
of it closes the connection, like the other controller-only apis (see "API keys").

The whole measurement is `tests/Integration/ApiVersionProbeTest.php`, and nothing it sends changes the node: the
quorum stays `[{id: 1, endpoints: [CONTROLLER://localhost:9096]}]`, which is what `DescribeQuorum` **v2** reports
in its `nodes` array.

## AddRaftVoter API (key 80, v0 and v1)

Adds a voter to the metadata quorum of a KRaft cluster. New in Kafka **3.9** (KIP-853), **v0**, flexible from that
version; `validVersions` @ 4.0.0 is still `0`, and **v1** is Kafka **4.2**, which appended `ack_when_committed` (see
"The acknowledgement mode of Kafka 4.2 (v1)" below). Kafka **4.0** made the reconfigurable quorum of KIP-853
generally available - a cluster formatted with `--standalone` or `--initial-controllers` finalizes `kraft.version` 1 -
and gave the Java admin client `addRaftVoter()` and `removeRaftVoter()`, which `AdminClient::addRaftVoter()` and
`AdminClient::removeRaftVoter()` are.

```
AddRaftVoterRequest => ClusterId TimeoutMs VoterId VoterDirectoryId [Listeners] AckWhenCommitted
  ClusterId        => compact nullable string
  TimeoutMs        => int32
  VoterId          => int32
  VoterDirectoryId => uuid
  Listeners => Name Host Port
    Name => compact string
    Host => compact string
    Port => uint16
  AckWhenCommitted => boolean   (v1+, "default": true)
```

```
AddRaftVoterResponse => ThrottleTimeMs ErrorCode ErrorMessage
  ThrottleTimeMs => int32
  ErrorCode      => int16
  ErrorMessage   => compact nullable string
```

**A voter is a key, not an id.** KIP-853 names a voter by its replica id **and** the directory id of the disk its
metadata log lives on - a controller that comes back with an empty disk is a different voter, and must not vote with
the log it lost - so the request carries both, next to the endpoints the quorum reaches the new voter at. The
`Port` is the `uint16` of the listener of a DescribeQuorum v2 answer.

**Any broker takes it.** The api is `"listeners": ["controller", "broker"]`: a broker forwards the request to the
active controller, and `KafkaRaftClient.handleAddVoterRequest` @ 4.0.0 checks, in this order, the cluster id
(**104** `InconsistentClusterId`; a **null** id is not checked), the leadership of the receiving controller, the
voter key (**42** for the zero directory id) and an endpoint on the controller's own listener (**42** again), and
hands the request to `AddVoterHandler`: a voter change in flight (**7** `RequestTimedOut`), a high watermark not
yet established (**7**), the feature (**35** below `kraft.version` 1), an uncommitted voter set (**7**) and the
voter **id** (**126** `DuplicateVoter` - the id alone is compared). Only then does the leader send the new voter an
**ApiVersions**: an error aborts the operation (**7**), a `kraft.version` range that does not cover the finalized
level refuses it (**42**), a new voter whose log has not caught up is refused (**7**), and a new voter that passes
is appended to a new voter set, whose commit the answer waits for.

Measured on the 4.3.1 node, whose quorum is the one voter `ReplicaKey(id=1, directoryId=7QxpXGVBQTWaHmiG7IDrEQ)` -
never with an endpoint that answers, so that no request below can add a voter:

| Request | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| the voter id 1, its own or a random directory id, `CONTROLLER://127.0.0.1:1` | **126** | `The voter id for ReplicaKey(id=1, directoryId=<asked>) is already part of the set of voters [ReplicaKey(id=1, directoryId=7QxpXGVBQTWaHmiG7IDrEQ)].` |
| the cluster id `not-this-cluster` | **104** | `The given id "not-this-cluster" doesn't match the cluster id "<id>"` |
| the zero directory id | **42** | `Add voter request didn't include a valid voter` |
| only a `PLAINTEXT` endpoint | **42** | `Add voter request didn't include the endpoint (Endpoints(endpoints={ListenerName(PLAINTEXT)=127.0.0.1/<unresolved>:1})) for the default listener ListenerName(CONTROLLER)` |
| a well-formed voter 4243 at `CONTROLLER://127.0.0.1:1`, a closed port | **7** | `Aborted add voter operation for since API_VERSIONS returned an error BROKER_NOT_AVAILABLE` |

**An unreachable voter is never appended.** The last row is the ApiVersions of `AddVoterHandler` failing on the
closed port: the raft client reports the failed request as `BROKER_NOT_AVAILABLE`, and the handler aborts the
operation and answers the 7 within milliseconds - the missing word of the message is in the source. The voter set
is unchanged afterwards (`kafka-metadata-quorum.sh describe --status` prints the one voter before and after, and
`RaftVoterApiTest` reads it back after every test). The **125** `InvalidVoterKey` stays unobservable: `KafkaRaftClient` @
4.0.0 answers it to a Vote (52) and a BeginQuorumEpoch (53) addressed to another replica key, both controller-listener
apis between voters.

`AdminClient::addRaftVoter()` takes the id, the 16 raw bytes of the directory id (`Uuid::fromString()` turns the
text form into them), a list of `Admin\RaftVoterEndpoint`, an optional cluster id, a timeout and - last - the
`ack_when_committed` of v1, sends the request to any broker and throws the exception of every code but 0.

### The acknowledgement mode of Kafka 4.2 (v1)

"Version 1 adds the AckWhenCommitted field" stands above the `validVersions` of `AddRaftVoterRequest.json` @ 4.2.0,
and "Version 1 is the same as version 0" above the one of the answer. The field is a boolean at the end of the body,
`"default": "true"`: "When true, return a response after the new voter set is committed. Otherwise, return after
the leader writes the changes locally." It is the version Kafka 4.2 added, and `AddRaftVoterRequestV0` /
`AddRaftVoterResponseV0` are the frames below it, whose flag never reaches the wire - a version 0 frame always
waits for the commit.

`AddVoterHandler` @ 4.2.0 reads the flag at **one** place: once the new voter has answered its ApiVersions, has
caught up and the leader has appended the new voter set, `ackWhenCommitted() == false` completes the answer right
there, and the operation stays in flight until the high watermark passes the new set. The Java admin client @ 4.2.0
has no option for it - `AddRaftVoterOptions` carries the cluster id alone, so `Admin.addRaftVoter()` always sends the
default - and the one sender of `false` is the controller itself: `KafkaRaftClient.buildAddVoterRequest` @ 4.2.0, the
auto-join of a follower controller that is not yet a voter (`controller.quorum.auto.join.enable`,
`quorumConfig.autoJoin()` in `shouldSendAddOrRemoveVoterRequest`). `AdminClient::addRaftVoter()` takes it as a
trailing parameter, `true` by default like the field.

**Every refusal comes before the flag.** Measured on the 4.3.1 node - whose voter is now
`ReplicaKey(id=1, directoryId=IpNOvhXLTxiMH2J_81GOUw)`, the node having been recreated since the table above - with
both values:

| Request (v1) | `ack_when_committed` | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|---|
| the voter id 1, `CONTROLLER://127.0.0.1:1` | true, false | **126** | `The voter id for ReplicaKey(id=1, …) is already part of the set of voters [ReplicaKey(id=1, directoryId=IpNOvhXLTxiMH2J_81GOUw)].` |
| a well-formed voter 4243 at the closed port | true, false | **7** | `Aborted add voter operation for since API_VERSIONS returned an error BROKER_NOT_AVAILABLE` |
| the same voter again, sent the moment the previous answer arrived | either | **7** | `New voter ReplicaKey(id=4243, directoryId=…) is not ready to receive requests` |

**The last row is a backoff, not a new check.** The raft client of the leader remembers the failed ApiVersions of a
replica id and backs it off for `controller.quorum.retry.backoff.ms` (20 ms by default): `DefaultRequestSender.send`
@ 4.3.1 refuses to send to a node that `RequestManager.isBackingOff`, and `AddVoterHandler` answers that refusal with
its own sentence before it starts an operation. Two adds of the same unreachable id within those milliseconds meet
it, whatever the flag; a few hundred milliseconds later the add is the aborted operation again
(`addraftvoter.response.v1.voter-in-backoff`, and `RaftVoterApiTest` waits it out like an operation in flight).
Nothing is appended in any row - the quorum still has its one voter after every test of `RaftVoterApiTest`, and
the frames that could take the new branch (a reachable voter that catches up) are the frames this repository never
sends.

## RemoveRaftVoter API (key 81, v0)

Removes a voter from the metadata quorum. New in Kafka **3.9** (KIP-853), **v0**, flexible from that version, and
unchanged up to 4.3.1.

```
RemoveRaftVoterRequest => ClusterId VoterId VoterDirectoryId
  ClusterId        => compact nullable string
  VoterId          => int32
  VoterDirectoryId => uuid
```

```
RemoveRaftVoterResponse => ThrottleTimeMs ErrorCode ErrorMessage
  ThrottleTimeMs => int32
  ErrorCode      => int16
  ErrorMessage   => compact nullable string
```

The voter is named by its whole key, and there is neither a timeout - the leader waits for the commit of the
smaller voter set as long as its `controller.quorum.request.timeout.ms` - nor a listener. `KafkaRaftClient` @ 4.0.0
checks the cluster id (**104**) and the voter key (**42**), `RemoveVoterHandler` a voter change in flight (**7**),
the feature (**35**) and the key (**127** `VoterNotFound` for a key the voter set does not hold). A leader that
removed **itself** resigns once the new voter set is committed, and a quorum whose last voter was removed has none:
this repository never sends the key of the voter 1.

| Request | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| the key `(4242, RFZofEWhQXF9JVjHbJjVuQ)` | **127** | `Cannot remove voter ReplicaKey(id=4242, directoryId=RFZofEWhQXF9JVjHbJjVuQ) from the set of voters [ReplicaKey(id=1, directoryId=7QxpXGVBQTWaHmiG7IDrEQ)]` |
| the cluster id `not-this-cluster` | **104** | `The given id "not-this-cluster" doesn't match the cluster id "<id>"` |
| the zero directory id | **42** | `Remove voter request didn't include a valid voter` |

`AdminClient::removeRaftVoter()` takes the id, the 16 raw bytes of the directory id and an optional cluster id.

## Share groups (KIP-932)

**Kafka 4.1** made the share groups of KIP-932 generally available: a group whose members do not own partitions
but **share** them, record by record. A member *acquires* records for a while, processes them and *acknowledges*
each one - accept, release or reject -, and what it releases, or does not acknowledge before its acquisition lock
expires, is delivered again, to it or to another member, with a delivery count one higher. Four apis are the
client's half of it: **76 ShareGroupHeartbeat** and **77 ShareGroupDescribe** go to the group coordinator,
**78 ShareFetch** and **79 ShareAcknowledge** to the leader of the partitions. The five apis 83 to 87 are the
broker's half (the share coordinator and its state topic `__share_group_state`, see "The share-group state apis
(keys 83 to 87) — wire only" below), the three 90 to 92 the admin apis of the share-group offsets.

All four client apis are at **version 1** on this line, flexible from the first version, and the node lists
exactly that: 76 and 77 at `1-1`, 78 and 79 at `1-2` (the version 2 of the two is Kafka 4.2, KIP-1206 and KIP-1222,
and not on this line yet). The JSON files @ 4.1.0 say why the range starts at 1: *"Version 0 was used for early
access of KIP-932 in Apache Kafka 4.0 but removed in Apache Kafka 4.1."* - so a 4.0 frame of them is a frame no 4.x
node from 4.1 on accepts, and the 3.9 hiding of "The raft-voter apis (keys 80 and 81) and the share groups — probe
only" is history. On the 4.3.1 node the feature `share.version` is finalized at 1, which is all it takes: no
`unstable.api.versions.enable`, and no `group.coordinator.rebalance.protocols` entry.

This package speaks the four apis by hand - `Client::joinShareGroup()`, `shareGroupHeartbeat()`,
`leaveShareGroup()`, `shareFetch()` and `shareAcknowledge()`, and `Admin\AdminClient::describeShareGroups()` -
and has no share consumer yet. What it measured on the node is below, api by api; the frames are the vectors of
`share-group-heartbeat.json`, `share-group-describe.json`, `share-fetch.json` and `share-acknowledge.json`,
captured with the client id `kafka-client-t3-41`, the topic `t3-41-vectors` of one partition and the group
`t3-41-vectors-group`, and the integration suites are `ShareGroupApiTest` and `ShareFetchApiTest`.

**The group configs of a share group.** A share group reads from **`latest`** unless its group config
`share.auto.offset.reset` says `earliest` (or `by_duration:<ISO-8601>`): a fresh group that joins a topic with
three records in it never sees them, and is delivered the two produced after its first ShareFetch at the offsets
3 and 4 (`ShareFetchApiTest::testAFreshGroupReadsFromLatestByDefault`). The configs of a group are set with
IncrementalAlterConfigs on the config resource type **32** (`ConfigResource.Type.GROUP`) - the one this
package's `Admin\ConfigResource` has no constant for, because its type 3 is the ACL resource type of a group - and
the node answers them 0 for a group that does not exist yet. The other configs a share group reads are
`share.record.lock.duration.ms` (30000 by default, the `acquisition_lock_timeout_ms` of every ShareFetch answer),
`share.delivery.count.limit` (5 deliveries, after which a record is archived), `share.isolation.level` and
`share.heartbeat.interval.ms` (5000), with the broker's `group.share.max.size` (200) above them. A share group is deleted with **DeleteGroups (key 42)** like any other,
once it is `Empty` - measured: the error code 0, after which ShareGroupDescribe answers the 69.

### ShareGroupHeartbeat API (key 76, v1)

The whole membership of a share member in one frame, the KIP-848 heartbeat without what an *owner* of partitions
needs: no rebalance timeout, no instance id, no server assignor and no owned partitions.

```
ShareGroupHeartbeatRequest => GroupId MemberId MemberEpoch RackId [SubscribedTopicNames]
  GroupId              => compact string
  MemberId             => compact string              -- the member's own, 22 base64 characters in the Java client
  MemberEpoch          => int32                       -- 0 joins, -1 leaves, else the epoch of the last answer
  RackId               => compact nullable string     -- null: unchanged
  SubscribedTopicNames => compact nullable array of compact string   -- null: unchanged

ShareGroupHeartbeatResponse => ThrottleTimeMs ErrorCode ErrorMessage MemberId MemberEpoch HeartbeatIntervalMs Assignment
  ThrottleTimeMs      => int32
  ErrorCode           => int16
  ErrorMessage        => compact nullable string
  MemberId            => compact nullable string
  MemberEpoch         => int32
  HeartbeatIntervalMs => int32
  Assignment          => [TopicPartitions]            -- NULLABLE STRUCT: one int8, -1 = null (unchanged), 1 = present
    TopicPartitions => TopicId [Partitions]
      TopicId    => uuid (16 raw bytes)
      Partitions => compact array of int32
```

Measured on the 4.3.1 node:

| Frame | Answer |
|---|---|
| join (epoch 0) with the member's own id and one topic (`sharegroupheartbeat.*.v1.join`) | the id back, epoch **2**, interval 5000 and a **present but empty** assignment |
| the next heartbeats, 0.5 s apart (`sharegroupheartbeat.*.v1.assignment`) | epoch 3 and every partition of the topic: the coordinator initialises the share state of the partitions first (a write to `__share_group_state` through the apis 83-87) and assigns them on a later heartbeat |
| the same heartbeat again (`sharegroupheartbeat.*.v1.steady`) | the epoch unchanged, the null assignment of "nothing changed" |
| a join with the empty member id (`sharegroupheartbeat.*.v1.join-without-member-id`) | **42** with **no message**: `KafkaApis.isMemberIdValid` refuses an empty, null or longer than 36 characters id before the coordinator is asked |
| a join with the empty topic list (`sharegroupheartbeat.*.v1.join-without-topics`) | **42** "SubscribedTopicNames must be set in first request." |
| an epoch ahead of the coordinator's (`sharegroupheartbeat.*.v1.fenced`) | **110** "The share group member has a greater member epoch (13) than the one known by the group coordinator (3). The member must abandon all its partitions and rejoin." The previous epoch is accepted, any other smaller one is the 110 as well |
| a member id the group does not know, epoch 1 | **25** `UnknownMemberId` |
| a group the coordinator does not know, epoch 1 | **69** `GroupIdNotFound`: only the epoch 0 creates a share group |
| a second member of the same group | partitions of the topic as well, on a later heartbeat (the `simple` assignor) |
| the leave (epoch -1, `sharegroupheartbeat.*.v1.leave`) | the id and the epoch -1 back, interval 0, null assignment |

Every refusal carries the member id null and the epoch 0. There is no static membership: the epoch -2 of a KIP-848
member that will come back has no meaning here.

### ShareGroupDescribe API (key 77, v1)

The share-group twin of ConsumerGroupDescribe (key 69): the same shape without the target assignment and the
member type, and with the topic of an assignment named by id **and** by name.

```
ShareGroupDescribeRequest => [GroupIds] IncludeAuthorizedOperations
  GroupIds                    => compact array of compact string
  IncludeAuthorizedOperations => boolean

ShareGroupDescribeResponse => ThrottleTimeMs [Groups]
  ThrottleTimeMs => int32
  Groups => ErrorCode ErrorMessage GroupId GroupState GroupEpoch AssignmentEpoch AssignorName [Members] AuthorizedOperations
    ErrorCode       => int16
    ErrorMessage    => compact nullable string
    GroupId         => compact string
    GroupState      => compact string                 -- Empty, Stable, Dead; "" in a refused entry
    GroupEpoch      => int32
    AssignmentEpoch => int32
    AssignorName    => compact string
    Members => MemberId RackId MemberEpoch ClientId ClientHost [SubscribedTopicNames] Assignment
      MemberId             => compact string
      RackId               => compact nullable string
      MemberEpoch          => int32
      ClientId             => compact string
      ClientHost           => compact string
      SubscribedTopicNames => compact array of compact string
      Assignment => [TopicPartitions]                 -- a plain struct
        TopicPartitions => TopicId TopicName [Partitions]
          TopicId    => uuid (16 raw bytes)
          TopicName  => compact string
          Partitions => compact array of int32
    AuthorizedOperations => int32                     -- -2147483648 when not asked for
```

| Question | Answer on the 4.3.1 node |
|---|---|
| a group of one member, with the operations (`sharegroupdescribe.*.v1.stable`) | `Stable`, group epoch 3 = assignment epoch 3, assignor **`simple`** (the one assignor of share groups), the member with its client id, its host `/172.18.0.1`, its subscription and its assignment, and the operations **3400** of the anonymous super user |
| a group that does not exist (`sharegroupdescribe.*.v1.unknown-group`) | **69** "Group t3-41-vectors-none not found." inside the entry, the state `""`, the epochs 0, the empty assignor |
| the group after its last member left (`sharegroupdescribe.*.v1.empty`) | `Empty`, the group epoch 4 one above the assignment epoch 3, no member |
| the group after DeleteGroups | the 69 again |

`AdminClient::describeShareGroups()` sends one request per coordinator and throws the exception of an entry's code
with its message, as `describeConsumerGroups()` does; the descriptions are the `ShareGroupDescribedGroup` entries
of the answer, keyed by group id, their members keyed by member id.

### ShareFetch API (key 78, v1)

The fetch of a share member, and the frame its acknowledgements usually ride on. It goes to the **leader** of the
partitions and works in a **share session** of the member there: the epoch 0 opens it with the partitions of the
request, every later request carries the next epoch (1, 2, ...) and names only what changed - partitions to add in
`Topics`, partitions to drop in `ForgottenTopicsData` -, and the epoch -1 closes it.

```
ShareFetchRequest => GroupId MemberId ShareSessionEpoch MaxWaitMs MinBytes MaxBytes MaxRecords BatchSize [Topics] [ForgottenTopicsData]
  GroupId           => compact nullable string
  MemberId          => compact nullable string
  ShareSessionEpoch => int32                          -- 0 opens, -1 closes, else the next epoch
  MaxWaitMs         => int32
  MinBytes          => int32
  MaxBytes          => int32                          -- 0x7fffffff by default
  MaxRecords        => int32                          -- v1: records to acquire at most, exceeded to finish a batch
  BatchSize         => int32                          -- v1: the optimal size of the batches of acquired records
  Topics => TopicId [Partitions]
    TopicId    => uuid (16 raw bytes)
    Partitions => PartitionIndex [AcknowledgementBatches]
      PartitionIndex => int32
      AcknowledgementBatches => FirstOffset LastOffset [AcknowledgeTypes]
        FirstOffset      => int64
        LastOffset       => int64
        AcknowledgeTypes => compact array of int8     -- one for the range, or one per offset: 0 gap, 1 accept, 2 release, 3 reject
  ForgottenTopicsData => TopicId [Partitions]
    TopicId    => uuid (16 raw bytes)
    Partitions => compact array of int32

ShareFetchResponse => ThrottleTimeMs ErrorCode ErrorMessage AcquisitionLockTimeoutMs [Responses] [NodeEndpoints]
  ThrottleTimeMs           => int32
  ErrorCode                => int16
  ErrorMessage             => compact nullable string
  AcquisitionLockTimeoutMs => int32                   -- v1
  Responses => TopicId [Partitions]
    TopicId    => uuid (16 raw bytes)
    Partitions => PartitionIndex ErrorCode ErrorMessage AcknowledgeErrorCode AcknowledgeErrorMessage CurrentLeader Records [AcquiredRecords]
      PartitionIndex          => int32
      ErrorCode               => int16
      ErrorMessage            => compact nullable string
      AcknowledgeErrorCode    => int16
      AcknowledgeErrorMessage => compact nullable string
      CurrentLeader => LeaderId LeaderEpoch           -- a plain struct, no default in the spec
        LeaderId    => int32
        LeaderEpoch => int32
      Records         => compact bytes (a record batch v2), never null in v1
      AcquiredRecords => FirstOffset LastOffset DeliveryCount
        FirstOffset   => int64
        LastOffset    => int64
        DeliveryCount => int16
  NodeEndpoints => NodeId Host Port Rack
    NodeId => int32
    Host   => compact string
    Port   => int32
    Rack   => compact nullable string
```

**`records` is not what the member may process, `acquired_records` is.** The records are whole record batches of
the log - a batch that was partly acknowledged comes back whole - and the ranges of `acquired_records` name the
offsets this member holds now, each range with its delivery count. `ShareFetchResponsePartition::acquiredRecords()`
of this package returns exactly those records, keyed by offset.

Measured on the 4.3.1 node, one member, one partition of six records `v0` to `v5`, `share.auto.offset.reset`
`earliest`:

| Frame | Answer |
|---|---|
| epoch 0, partition 0 (`sharefetch.*.v1.open`) | `acquisition_lock_timeout_ms` **30000**; the whole batch 0-5 in `records`, `acquired_records` **0-5** with the delivery count **1** |
| epoch 0 with an acknowledgement batch (`sharefetch.*.v1.acknowledgements-in-epoch-zero`) | **42** of the request, no message, no partition: a session that has not acquired anything has nothing to acknowledge |
| epoch 5 in a session whose next epoch is 1 (`sharefetch.*.v1.wrong-epoch`) | **123** `InvalidShareSessionEpoch`, no message, no partition; the session keeps its epoch, and the right one works afterwards |
| epoch 1, acknowledging 0-2 per offset (accept, release, reject) and 3-5 as one range (release) (`sharefetch.*.v1.acknowledge-and-redeliver`) | `acknowledge_error_code` 0, and the fetch half acquires **1** and **3-5** again with the delivery count **2**: the released records are redelivered at once, the accepted 0 and the rejected 2 never |
| a piggybacked acknowledgement of an offset already accepted (`sharefetch.*.v1.acknowledge-error`) | `error_code` 0 for the fetch, **121** in `acknowledge_error_code` with "The offset cannot be acknowledged. The offset is not acquired." |
| a ShareFetch after the session was closed (`sharefetch.*.v1.session-not-found`) | **122** `ShareSessionNotFound`, no message |
| a ShareFetch with the null group id | **42**, no message |

**The current leader is `0 0` on every partition the node served.** The spec gives `LeaderId` and `LeaderEpoch` no
default, and `KafkaApis.processShareFetchResponse` @ 4.3.1 fills them in - and puts the endpoint of the leader into
`node_endpoints` - only for a partition it answers **6** `NotLeaderOrFollower` or **74** `FencedLeaderEpoch`. The
leader of the one-node cluster is node 1, so the 0 is not a node id.

**The session lives on its connection.** `ShareSessionCache` keys a session by the group and the member and
remembers the connection that opened it: a connection the node sees closed takes the session with it and releases
what the member held (`ShareSessionCache.ConnectionDisconnectListener` and `SharePartitionManager.onMemberLeave` @
4.3.1). A member that lost its connection opens a new session with the epoch 0; its next epoch on the old session
is the 122. `Client::shareFetch()` reuses the connection of the node, and so do the suites.

**The 4.3.1 node does not check the membership of a ShareFetch.** A member id the coordinator has never heard of,
on a partition nobody assigned to it, opens a session and acquires records like a member of the group (probed on the
node, not a suite: a well-behaved client never sends it). The assignment of ShareGroupHeartbeat is what a share
consumer *should* fetch, not what the leader enforces.

### ShareAcknowledge API (key 79, v1)

The acknowledgements of a member without a fetch - what a member sends when it has what it needs, and the frame
that **closes** its share session (epoch -1). It needs an open session: it cannot open one.

```
ShareAcknowledgeRequest => GroupId MemberId ShareSessionEpoch [Topics]
  GroupId           => compact nullable string
  MemberId          => compact nullable string
  ShareSessionEpoch => int32                          -- the next epoch, or -1 to close
  Topics => TopicId [Partitions]
    TopicId    => uuid (16 raw bytes)
    Partitions => PartitionIndex [AcknowledgementBatches]      -- the batches of ShareFetch
      PartitionIndex => int32

ShareAcknowledgeResponse => ThrottleTimeMs ErrorCode ErrorMessage [Responses] [NodeEndpoints]
  ThrottleTimeMs => int32
  ErrorCode      => int16
  ErrorMessage   => compact nullable string
  Responses => TopicId [Partitions]
    TopicId    => uuid (16 raw bytes)
    Partitions => PartitionIndex ErrorCode ErrorMessage CurrentLeader
      PartitionIndex => int32
      ErrorCode      => int16
      ErrorMessage   => compact nullable string
      CurrentLeader  => LeaderId LeaderEpoch          -- as in ShareFetch
  NodeEndpoints => NodeId Host Port Rack              -- as in ShareFetch
```

Measured in the session of the ShareFetch table above, after the redelivery (the member holds 1, 3, 4 and 5):

| Frame | Answer |
|---|---|
| epoch 2, accept 3 (`shareacknowledge.*.v1.accept`) | the partition answered 0 |
| epoch 3, accept 3 again (`shareacknowledge.*.v1.accept-twice`) | **121** `InvalidRecordState` **of the partition**, "The offset cannot be acknowledged. The offset is not acquired."; the request itself is 0 |
| an offset another member acquired | **121** "Member is not the owner of batch record" (or "... of offset" once the batch is tracked per offset) |
| an offset past everything acquired (9 of a partition that ends at 5) | **42** of the partition, "Batch record not found. The first offset in request is past acquired records." |
| an acknowledgement type 4 (the `Renew` of version 2) | **42** of the partition, no message |
| an `AcknowledgeTypes` array whose length is neither 1 nor the length of the range | **42** of the partition |
| the type 0 `Gap` on an acquired offset | 0: the member says the offset is not a record (a compacted gap or a control record) |
| epoch 0 (`shareacknowledge.*.v1.epoch-zero`) | **123** of the request |
| a member without a session, epoch 1 | **122** of the request |
| epoch -1 without topics (`shareacknowledge.*.v1.close`) | 0 and no partition: the session is closed, and what the member still held is **released** - a second member acquires those records at once with the delivery count **2** (`ShareFetchApiTest::testClosingTheSessionReleasesTheRecordsToAnotherMember`) |

Acknowledging an offset that is **below** the start offset of the share partition is not an error: the node skips
it (`SharePartition.acknowledgePerOffsetBatchRecords` @ 4.3.1). That is why a second accept of the offset 0 right
after it was accepted answers 0 - the accepted 0 moved the start offset to 1 - and the 121 is measured on an offset
behind one that is still acquired.

**The codes 121 to 124 and 133 on this node.** **121**, **122** and **123** are measured above. **124**
`FencedStateEpoch` is an answer of the share-coordinator apis 83 to 87 to the broker that holds a share partition;
`SharePartition.fetchPersisterError` @ 4.3.1 turns it into the 6 `NotLeaderOrFollower` of the partition before a
client sees anything, so no client api of this node writes it. **133** `ShareSessionLimitReached` is the answer
of a ShareFetch of the epoch 0 when the node holds `group.share.max.share.sessions` sessions already - **2000** per
broker by default, and at least `group.share.max.size` (200). Since the node checks no membership, 2000 epoch-0
fetches of 2000 member ids would reach it; the suites do not, because the session cache is the node's and three
other agents share it. The code is retriable in the Java client, and in this package.

## The share-group state apis (keys 83 to 87) — wire only

The **share coordinator** of KIP-932 owns the state of every share partition - which records of a partition a share
group has handed out, acknowledged or archived, and where the group starts reading - in the compacted topic
`__share_group_state`, and five apis read and write it: **83** InitializeShareGroupState, **84**
ReadShareGroupState, **85** WriteShareGroupState, **86** DeleteShareGroupState and **87**
ReadShareGroupStateSummary. Their callers are the brokers: a partition leader reads and writes the state of the share
partitions it leads, a group coordinator initializes, summarizes and deletes it. Kafka 3.9 declared them unstable;
Kafka **4.1** made them stable at **v0**, and a client listener serves them. Kafka **4.2** added the **v1** of 85 and
87 for the `DeliveryCompleteCount` of KIP-1226 - the number of records at or above the start offset of a share
partition whose delivery is complete, which a partition leader writes with its state and a group coordinator
subtracts for the lag of a share group; `WriteShareGroupStateRequestV0`, `WriteShareGroupStateResponseV0`,
`ReadShareGroupStateSummaryRequestV0` and `ReadShareGroupStateSummaryResponseV0` are the frames below them.

They are **wire only** on this line (the owner's decision 2): message classes and vectors, no client method. The
state is keyed by the group, the topic **id** and the partition, so every topic is named by its id and every array
of topics is a list; the answers have **neither a throttle time nor a top-level error**, and every partition carries
the code of its key. A broker authorizes the five as `CLUSTER_ACTION` on the cluster, the operation of inter-broker
traffic, and answers a principal without it the **31** in every partition of the request
(`toGlobalErrorResponse`). `ShareCoordinatorService` @ 4.3.1 answers a request without a topic, a topic without a
partition and an empty group id with an empty result array, before it looks up a key.

The measurements - `tests/Integration/ShareGroupStateApiTest.php` - write no state through these apis: the three
writing apis carry a topic without a partition, or - the write of v1 - a partition of a share group that does not
exist, and the two reading apis name the partition 0 of a topic of their own for the share group
`t1-41-no-such-share-group`, which does not exist, with the leader epoch **-1**, which a read never writes back. The
one share group the class creates, `t1-42-share-state-group-…`, is its own: a member of it fetches and acknowledges
real records, so that the summary of v1 has a count to report, and the group is deleted afterwards.

| Api | Frame | Answer |
|---|---|---|
| 83, 85, 86 | a topic id without a partition | an empty result array, seven bytes |
| 84 | the partition 0, never initialized | per partition **42** `Read operation on uninitialized share partition not allowed.`, the state epoch 0, the start offset 0 and no batch |
| 84 | the same, as the SASL user `acltest` | per partition **31** `Cluster authorization failed.` |
| 87 | the partition 0, never initialized | per partition **0**, the state epoch 0, the leader epoch 0 and the start offset **-1** - the initial state (`PartitionFactory.UNINITIALIZED_START_OFFSET`), where the full read is the 42 |
| 87 | the empty group id | an empty result array |
| 85 v1 | the partition 0 of the group that does not exist, with a `DeliveryCompleteCount` 2 and one batch | per partition **42** `Write operation on uninitialized share partition not allowed.` - and the summary afterwards is still the initial state |
| 87 v1 | the partition 0, never initialized | as at v0, plus the `DeliveryCompleteCount` **-1** (`PartitionFactory.UNINITIALIZED_DELIVERY_COMPLETE_COUNT`) |
| 87 v1 | the partition 0 of a share group whose member acquired six records and accepted one, rejected one and released four | the start offset **0**, the `DeliveryCompleteCount` **2**, the state epoch 2 - and, before the first ShareFetch, the start offset -1 and the count -1 |

### InitializeShareGroupState API (key 83, v0)

```
InitializeShareGroupStateRequest => GroupId [Topics]
  GroupId => compact string
  Topics => TopicId [Partitions]
    TopicId    => uuid
    Partitions => Partition StateEpoch StartOffset
      Partition   => int32
      StateEpoch  => int32
      StartOffset => int64      (-1 when the start offset is not initialized)
```

```
InitializeShareGroupStateResponse => [Results]
  Results => TopicId [Partitions]
    TopicId    => uuid
    Partitions => Partition ErrorCode ErrorMessage
      Partition    => int32
      ErrorCode    => int16
      ErrorMessage => compact nullable string
```

The group coordinator initializes a share partition when a share group first subscribes to its topic: the state
epoch it starts with and the offset it starts at. The specification names the codes 16, 15, 14, 124
(`FencedStateEpoch`) and 42.

### ReadShareGroupState API (key 84, v0)

```
ReadShareGroupStateRequest => GroupId [Topics]
  GroupId => compact string
  Topics => TopicId [Partitions]
    TopicId    => uuid
    Partitions => Partition LeaderEpoch
      Partition   => int32
      LeaderEpoch => int32      (-1 to leave the recorded one alone)
```

```
ReadShareGroupStateResponse => [Results]
  Results => TopicId [Partitions]
    TopicId    => uuid
    Partitions => Partition ErrorCode ErrorMessage StateEpoch StartOffset [StateBatches]
      StateBatches => FirstOffset LastOffset DeliveryState DeliveryCount
        FirstOffset   => int64
        LastOffset    => int64
        DeliveryState => int8   (0 available, 2 acknowledged, 4 archived)
        DeliveryCount => int16
```

The whole state of a share partition, which its leader reads to load it. **A read can write**: a leader epoch above
the one the coordinator recorded is written back with the state (`ShareCoordinatorShard
.readStateAndMaybeUpdateLeaderEpoch` @ 4.3.1), which is why the probe of this repository sends the -1. The batch
structure is the one of WriteShareGroupState; this package carries both as `Data\ShareGroupStateBatch`.

### WriteShareGroupState API (key 85, v0 and v1)

```
WriteShareGroupStateRequest => GroupId [Topics]
  GroupId => compact string
  Topics => TopicId [Partitions]
    TopicId    => uuid
    Partitions => Partition StateEpoch LeaderEpoch StartOffset DeliveryCompleteCount [StateBatches]
      DeliveryCompleteCount => int32   (v1+, "default": -1, ignorable)
```

```
WriteShareGroupStateResponse => [Results]
  Results => TopicId [Partitions]
    Partitions => Partition ErrorCode ErrorMessage
```

The delivery state a partition leader has handed out and seen acknowledged, appended to `__share_group_state`.

**Version 1 (Kafka 4.2, KIP-1226) puts `DeliveryCompleteCount` between the start offset and the batches** - "Version 1
introduces DeliveryCompleteCount (KIP-1226)" in `WriteShareGroupStateRequest.json` @ 4.2.0, and "… in the request"
in the answer, which is the frame of v0. The count is `SharePartition.deliveryCompleteCount` @ 4.3.1: the records at
or above the start offset whose state is terminal, acknowledged or archived. The share coordinator keeps it with the
state (the tagged field 0 of `ShareSnapshotValue` and `ShareUpdateValue`, "added in Apache Kafka 4.2") and answers
it in the summary. A partition the coordinator has no state for is the per-partition **42**
`Write operation on uninitialized share partition not allowed.` at either version, and nothing is appended.
`Data\WriteShareGroupStateRequestTopicV0` and `Data\WriteShareGroupStateRequestPartitionV0` are the entries of v0;
each topic class converts the partitions it is given into the entry of its own version.

### DeleteShareGroupState API (key 86, v0)

```
DeleteShareGroupStateRequest => GroupId [Topics]
  GroupId => compact string
  Topics => TopicId [Partitions]
    TopicId    => uuid
    Partitions => Partition
      Partition => int32
```

```
DeleteShareGroupStateResponse => [Results]
  Results => TopicId [Partitions]
    Partitions => Partition ErrorCode ErrorMessage
```

The state of share partitions whose group, or whose offsets of a topic, were deleted.

### ReadShareGroupStateSummary API (key 87, v0 and v1)

```
ReadShareGroupStateSummaryRequest => GroupId [Topics]
  GroupId => compact string
  Topics => TopicId [Partitions]
    TopicId    => uuid
    Partitions => Partition LeaderEpoch
```

```
ReadShareGroupStateSummaryResponse => [Results]
  Results => TopicId [Partitions]
    Partitions => Partition ErrorCode ErrorMessage StateEpoch LeaderEpoch StartOffset DeliveryCompleteCount
      DeliveryCompleteCount => int32   (v1+, "default": -1, ignorable)
```

The state of a share partition without its batches, which a group coordinator reads to answer
DescribeShareGroupOffsets (90). The request is the frame of ReadShareGroupState with another api key, and this
package reads its topics with the same `Data\ReadShareGroupStateRequestTopic`. **The summary of a partition the
coordinator has never seen is its initial state, not an error** - the 87 is answered 0 where the 84 is answered 42.

**Version 1 (Kafka 4.2, KIP-1226) appends `DeliveryCompleteCount` to every partition of the answer**; the request of
v1 is the frame of v0 ("Version 1 introduces DeliveryCompleteCount in the response (KIP-1226)",
`ReadShareGroupStateSummaryRequest.json` @ 4.2.0). It is the count of the last WriteShareGroupState v1 of the
partition leader, which `GroupCoordinatorService` @ 4.3.1 subtracts together with the start offset from the end
offset of the partition to report the lag of a share group. **-1** is "not known": the answer for a key the share
coordinator has never seen (`UNINITIALIZED_DELIVERY_COMPLETE_COUNT`) and for a partition whose start offset is still
-1, which is the state a group coordinator initializes when a share group is assigned the partition. Measured with a
real share group: -1 and -1 before the first ShareFetch; after six records were acquired and the offset 1 accepted,
the offset 2 rejected and the offsets 0 and 3 to 5 released, the start offset **0** and the count **2** - the released
offset 0 keeps the start offset where it was, and the accepted and the archived record are the two whose delivery is
complete. `Data\ReadShareGroupStateSummaryResponseTopicV0` and `Data\ReadShareGroupStateSummaryResponsePartitionV0`
are the entries of the answer of v0, whose count keeps the -1 of the default.

## DescribeCluster API (key 60, v0 to v2)

The cluster id, the controller and the brokers, without naming a topic. New in Kafka **2.8** (KIP-700), **v0**,
flexible from that version; **v1** is Kafka **3.7** (KIP-919), which added the endpoint type, and **v2** Kafka
**4.0** (KIP-1073), which added the fenced brokers.

```
DescribeClusterRequest => IncludeClusterAuthorizedOperations EndpointType IncludeFencedBrokers
  IncludeClusterAuthorizedOperations => boolean
  EndpointType                       => int8    (v1+, 1 = brokers, 2 = controllers)
  IncludeFencedBrokers               => boolean (v2+)
```

```
DescribeClusterResponse => ThrottleTimeMs ErrorCode ErrorMessage EndpointType ClusterId ControllerId [Brokers]
                           ClusterAuthorizedOperations
  ThrottleTimeMs => int32
  ErrorCode      => int16
  ErrorMessage   => compact nullable string
  EndpointType   => int8                        (v1+)
  ClusterId      => compact string
  ControllerId   => int32                       (-1 while the cluster has no controller)
  Brokers => BrokerId Host Port Rack IsFenced
    BrokerId => int32
    Host     => compact string
    Port     => int32
    Rack     => compact nullable string
    IsFenced => boolean                         (v2+)
  ClusterAuthorizedOperations => int32
```

**This is among the smallest requests of the protocol** — at version 0; ListClientMetricsResources (74) of
Kafka 3.7 has no body at all, and ApiVersions v0, which is not flexible, has neither a body nor a tag buffer. Until Kafka 2.8 the three facts it carries could only be read out of a **Metadata** answer — a
request about *topics* that happens to name the cluster id, the controller and the brokers — so a client that
wanted them alone sent an empty topic array and paid for the topic machinery on the broker. KIP-700 gave them a
request of their own, served by any broker (`"listeners": ["zkBroker", "broker"]`, and `"controller"` from Kafka
3.7 on).

**`cluster_authorized_operations` is `Integer.MIN_VALUE` (`-2147483648`) when the request did not ask for it**,
which is the default of the specification and not an error; `Admin\ClusterDescription::hasAuthorizedOperations()`
is that test. A request that *does* ask gets the bit field of KIP-430, one bit per `AclOperation` the caller may
perform on the cluster. Measured on the 2.8.2 container, which runs **without** an authorizer and therefore allows
everything: **8096**, i.e. `0b1111110100000` — the bits 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 and 12, which are `CREATE`, `ALTER`,
`DESCRIBE`, `CLUSTER_ACTION`, `DESCRIBE_CONFIGS`, `ALTER_CONFIGS` and `IDEMPOTENT_WRITE` of `AclOperation` @ 2.8.2
— the whole set `AclEntry.supportedOperations(CLUSTER)` names. (The same field appears in Metadata v8 and in
DescribeGroups v3 for their own resource types, with their own sets.) The **3.9.2 KRaft node**, which does run an
authorizer, answers the very same 8096 to a super user and **0** — not one bit — to the SASL user `acltest` that
no acl names, with the code 0 and the broker list in both.

`AdminClient::describeCluster()` sends this api at **version 2**; `AdminClient::describeClusterFromMetadata()`
builds the same `ClusterDescription` out of a Metadata answer, which is what a broker below Kafka 2.8 needs — the
choice is the caller's, because a 2.8.2 broker is the first that serves the key 60 at all.

### The endpoint type of KIP-919 (v1)

A cluster without ZooKeeper has **two** sets of nodes: the brokers that serve clients and the controllers that
hold the metadata log. Until Kafka 3.7 this api could only describe the first of them — a client that wanted the
controller endpoints had to be configured with them — and KIP-919 gave the request an `endpoint_type` byte and the
answer one of its own. `EndpointType` @ 3.9.2 has three values, `UNKNOWN` (0), `BROKER` (1) and `CONTROLLER` (2);
the field's `"default": "1"` is what a version 0 frame means, so the version is a widening and not a change.
`Admin\EndpointType` is the enum of this client, and `DescribeClusterRequestV0`/`DescribeClusterResponseV0` are
the frames below it.

`AuthHelper.computeDescribeClusterResponse` @ 3.9.2 checks the byte **before** anything else, in this order:

1. a type that is neither 1 nor 2 — `EndpointType.fromId` maps it to `UNKNOWN` — is the **115**
   `UnsupportedEndpointType` with the message `Unsupported endpoint type <byte>`;
2. a type the server is not of — the 2 of a controller asked on a **broker** listener — is the **114**
   `MismatchedEndpointType` with `The request was sent to an endpoint of type BROKER, but we wanted an endpoint of
   type CONTROLLER`;
3. a version **0** request is answered the **42** `InvalidRequest` in both of those places instead, which no frame
   can actually reach, because a version 0 frame carries no type to be wrong about.

**Both refusals are the error alone.** The method returns a bare `DescribeClusterResponseData` with the code and
the message, so what the client reads back is the `endpoint_type` **1** of the schema default (never the type it
asked for), the cluster id as the **empty string**, the controller id -1, an empty broker array and the
`Integer.MIN_VALUE` of a bit field nobody filled. A client cannot tell from the answer which type was described
when the answer is a refusal, and `AdminClient::describeCluster()` throws before a caller sees it.

Measured on the node, on its PLAINTEXT listener: the type 1 is the ordinary answer, the type 2 is the 114, the
types 0 and 3 are the 115. The controller endpoints themselves are only reachable on the CONTROLLER listener,
which this repository does not expose outside the container, so the **only** answer this line can capture for the
type 2 is its refusal.

**`controller_id` of a KRaft node is not the controller.** `KafkaApis.handleDescribeCluster` @ 3.9.2 maps a
`KRaftCachedControllerId` to `metadataCache.getRandomAliveBrokerId` — the controller of a KRaft cluster is not a
broker and has no endpoint a client may use, so the field carries **a broker** instead, the node 1 on this
container, and `AuthHelper` replaces even that with -1 when the id is not in the broker list it just built. The
field means "somebody who will forward your controller request" here, not "the leader of the metadata quorum",
which is what DescribeQuorum (55) answers.

Error codes observed on the container:

| Code | Request that produces it                                                        |
|------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 0    | Always, on a broker that serves the api                                          |
| 114  | `MismatchedEndpointType` — **(3.7)** a **v1** with the `endpoint_type` 2 on a broker listener; observed on the node |
| 115  | `UnsupportedEndpointType` — **(3.7)** a **v1** with an `endpoint_type` that is neither 1 nor 2; observed on the node with the bytes 0 and 3 |
| 31   | `ClusterAuthorizationFailed` — *not producible on either broker of this repository*: the 2.8.2 container ran without an authorizer, and the 3.9.2 KRaft node, which runs the `StandardAuthorizer`, answers the code 0 to every principal and refuses with an **empty** `cluster_authorized_operations` instead (see "Broker quirks and observations") |

### The fenced brokers of KIP-1073 (v2)

Kafka **4.0** raised the api to the version 2: "Version 2 adds IncludeFencedBrokers for KIP-1073 support" stands
above the `validVersions` of `DescribeClusterRequest.json` @ 4.0.0 and "Version 2 adds IsFenced field to Brokers
for KIP-1073 support" above those of the answer. The request appends one boolean behind the `endpoint_type`, and
every broker of the answer one boolean behind its rack; nothing else changed. `DescribeClusterRequestV1`,
`DescribeClusterResponseV1` and `Data\DescribeClusterBrokerV1` are the keep-behind classes of the frames below.

A KRaft controller **fences** a broker it has registered but that may not serve - one that has not caught up with
the metadata log since it started, or whose heartbeats stopped - and every broker list a client could read until
Kafka 4.0 left such a broker out, a DescribeCluster answer as well as a Metadata answer. KIP-1073 lets an
operator see it: with `include_fenced_brokers` set the answer names the fenced brokers too,
with `is_fenced` true. `Admin.describeCluster(new DescribeClusterOptions().includeFencedBrokers(true))` of the Java
client @ 4.0.0 sends the flag and refuses it towards the controllers on the client side ("Cannot request fenced
brokers from controller endpoint"); `AdminClient::describeCluster()` takes it as its third argument and lists the
ids of the fenced brokers in `ClusterDescription::$fencedNodeIds` next to the nodes - `Node.isFenced()` of the Java
client, which `Protocol\Kafka\Common\Node`, the broker of a Metadata answer, has no field for.

Measured on the 4.3.1 node, whose one broker serves the request itself and is therefore never fenced:

| Request | Answer |
|---|---|
| v2, `include_fenced_brokers` false | the code 0 and the one broker with `is_fenced` **false** - the version 1 answer plus one byte |
| v2, `include_fenced_brokers` true, with the acl flag | the same broker, `is_fenced` false, and the bit field **8096** of a super user (**0** for the SASL user `acltest`) |
| v2, `endpoint_type` 2 and `include_fenced_brokers` true | the **114** of the version 1, unchanged: the broker listener refuses the endpoint type before it looks at the flag |

A fenced broker needs a second broker process that registers and stops heartbeating, which the one combined node of
this repository cannot provide: the `true` of the field is declared and never observed here.

## DescribeProducers API (key 61, v0)

Which producers a partition still remembers. New in Kafka **2.8** (KIP-664), **v0**, flexible from that version.

```
DescribeProducersRequest => [Topics]
  Topics => Name [PartitionIndexes]
    Name             => compact string
    PartitionIndexes => compact array of int32
```

```
DescribeProducersResponse => ThrottleTimeMs [Topics]
  ThrottleTimeMs => int32
  Topics => Name [Partitions]
    Partitions => PartitionIndex ErrorCode ErrorMessage [ActiveProducers]
      PartitionIndex => int32
      ErrorCode      => int16
      ErrorMessage   => compact nullable string
      ActiveProducers => ProducerId ProducerEpoch LastSequence LastTimestamp CoordinatorEpoch
                         CurrentTxnStartOffset
        ProducerId            => int64
        ProducerEpoch         => int32
        LastSequence          => int32   (-1 when unknown)
        LastTimestamp         => int64   (-1 when unknown)
        CoordinatorEpoch      => int32
        CurrentTxnStartOffset => int64   (-1 when no transaction of this producer is open here)
```

KIP-664 — *"Provide tooling to detect and abort hanging transactions"* — made the **producer state of a log**
visible. Every partition keeps, for each producer id that wrote to it, the epoch, the last sequence number and the
last timestamp it saw (that is how `ProducerStateManager` recognises a duplicate of the idempotent producer), and
the first offset of a transaction of that producer that is still open in the partition. Before Kafka 2.8 the only
way to read it was `kafka-run-class.sh kafka.tools.DumpLogSegments`.

**The request goes to the leader of each partition**, because the state lives in the log:
`AdminClient::describeProducers()` groups the requested partitions by their leader and sends one request per
broker. A broker that does not lead a partition answers **3** `UnknownTopicOrPartition` for it — not 6.

**There is no top-level error code**: every partition carries one of its own, and a partition that remembers no
producer is the code 0 with an **empty** producer array.

**`producer_epoch` is an `int32` here** although it is an `int16` in every other api of this protocol — the
specification writes it wide in `ProducerState` — and the broker sends the same value in both places.

**Quirk: the `coordinator_epoch` is written by the transaction MARKER, not by the batch.** The two transaction
fields of `ProducerState` move on different beats, which matters to anyone reading them as a pair.
`ProducerAppendInfo` sets `currentTxnFirstOffset` from the first batch of a transaction and the *marker* clears
it, so `current_txn_start_offset` is exactly the base offset of that batch while the transaction is open and -1
afterwards. `coordinator_epoch`, on the other hand, is only assigned when `ProducerStateEntry` sees the
`EndTxnMarker`, so a producer whose **very first** transaction is still open is reported with the -1 of a producer
that has none, and a producer whose second transaction is open still carries the epoch the **previous** marker
wrote. Measured on the container, both ways round:

| Moment                                     | `coordinator_epoch` | `current_txn_start_offset` |
|--------------------------------------------|---------------------|----------------------------|
| first transaction open                     | **-1**              | base offset of its first batch |
| after its commit marker                    | **0**               | -1                         |
| second transaction open                    | 0 *(of the marker before it)* | base offset of its first batch |
| after its abort marker                     | 0                   | -1                         |

An **abort** marker clears the first offset exactly as a commit marker does; nothing in this answer says which of
the two was written.

Error codes observed on the container:

| Code | Where | Request that produces it                                             |
|------|-------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 0    | per partition | The state could be read — with or without a producer in it      |
| 3    | per partition | A partition the broker does not have, or does not lead — with a **null** message for a partition of a known topic and the default sentence of the code, `This server does not host this topic-partition.`, for a topic the cluster does not know at all |
| 17   | per partition | A topic name `Topic.validate` refuses, with its sentence: `Topic name is invalid: …`. The client never sends one — `AdminClient::describeProducers()` cannot route an unknown topic and refuses it before the request is built |
| 29   | per partition | A topic the principal may not `READ`, with `Topic authorization failed.` — measured on the 3.9.2 KRaft node with its `StandardAuthorizer` and the SASL user `acltest`; the 2.8.2 container ran without an authorizer and could not produce it |

## DescribeTransactions API (key 65, v0)

The state one transactional id is in, as its **transaction coordinator** holds it. New in Kafka **3.0**, **v0**,
flexible from that version, as every api key the 3.x line adds is. Neither `DescribeTransactionsRequest.json` nor
`DescribeTransactionsResponse.json` @ 3.0.2 names a KIP.

```
DescribeTransactionsRequest => [TransactionalIds]
  TransactionalIds => compact string
```

```
DescribeTransactionsResponse => ThrottleTimeMs [TransactionStates]
  ThrottleTimeMs => int32
  TransactionStates => ErrorCode TransactionalId TransactionState TransactionTimeoutMs TransactionStartTimeMs
                       ProducerId ProducerEpoch [Topics]
    ErrorCode              => int16
    TransactionalId        => compact string
    TransactionState       => compact string   (`Empty`, `Ongoing`, `PrepareCommit`, …)
    TransactionTimeoutMs   => int32
    TransactionStartTimeMs => int64            (-1 while no transaction of this id has started)
    ProducerId             => int64
    ProducerEpoch          => int16
    Topics => Topic [Partitions]
      Topic      => compact string
      Partitions => compact array of int32
```

**Where DescribeProducers (61) reads the producer state of a *log*, this reads the state of the
*coordinator*.** The two answer the halves of one question: the partition says which producer id still has a
transaction open in it and at which offset, and this api says which transaction that is, whose it is, when it
started and which other partitions belong to it. Before Kafka 3.0 the coordinator's half could only be read by
dumping `__transaction_state` with `DumpLogSegments --offsets-decoder`.

**The request goes to the transaction coordinator of each id**, the broker a GroupCoordinator request (key 10)
of the type `COORDINATOR_TYPE_TRANSACTION` (1) points at: the state lives in the `__transaction_state` partition
of that id. A broker that does not coordinate it answers **16** (`NotCoordinator`) in the entry of that id - not
producible on the one-node container, whose single broker coordinates every partition.
`Admin\AdminClient::describeTransactions()` therefore looks every id up first and sends one frame per
coordinator; the ids of one coordinator travel in a single frame, and the entries come back in the order of the
request.

**There is no top-level error code**: every transactional id carries one of its own, as every partition of a
DescribeProducers answer does. An entry whose code is not 0 carries the transactional id and **the defaults of
the specification** behind it - the empty state name, the timeout **0**, the start time **0**, the producer id 0
and the epoch 0 - so the code has to be read before the numbers. Note that the 0 of a refused entry is not the
-1 of an `Empty` one: the field is only a "no transaction yet" -1 when the coordinator really answered for the
id.

**The eight state names** are `TransactionState.name` of `kafka.coordinator.transaction.TransactionMetadata`
@ 3.9.2, and they are what `Admin\TransactionState` parses:

| Name | What it means |
|------|---------------|
| `Empty` | The id is known - `InitProducerId` has run - and no transaction is in flight |
| `Ongoing` | A transaction is open and at least one partition has been added to it |
| `PrepareCommit` / `PrepareAbort` | The coordinator has written its decision and is writing the markers |
| `CompleteCommit` / `CompleteAbort` | Every marker has been written; the id waits for the next transaction |
| `PrepareEpochFence` | The epoch of the id is being bumped, which fences the producer that held it (KIP-360) |
| `Dead` | The metadata of the id is being expired - **never** reported: the coordinator answers 105 for it |

**`beginTransaction()` is not on the wire, and the coordinator says so.** A producer that has called
`InitProducerId` and begun a transaction is still `Empty` here: the state only moves to `Ongoing` with the first
`AddPartitionsToTxn` of that transaction, because that request is the first thing the coordinator hears about it.
Measured on the node: `Empty` after `initTransactions()`, `Empty` after `beginTransaction()`, `Ongoing` after the
first partition was added.

**`transaction_start_time_ms` outlives its transaction.** `TransactionMetadata.txnStartTimestamp` @ 3.9.2 is set
when the transaction opens and is *not* cleared by the markers, so a `CompleteCommit` entry still carries the
start time of the transaction that was committed, while the `topics` array of the same entry is empty. Only an id
that has never had a transaction answers the **-1** of the specification. The `topics` array itself is the set of
partitions of the **current** transaction; an id preparing to commit or abort lists only the partitions whose
marker is still missing, and an id between two transactions lists none.

**`producer_epoch` is an `int16` here**, where the `ProducerState` of a DescribeProducers answer writes the same
number as an `int32`.

**An empty id array is "no id", never "every id"**: the request is accepted and answered with an empty entry
array in 14 bytes. An id that is the **empty string** is refused per entry with **42** (`InvalidRequest`,
`TransactionCoordinator.handleDescribeTransactions` @ 3.9.2 checks `transactionalId.isEmpty`), and the other ids
of the same frame are still answered.

Error codes observed on the node:

| Code | Where | Request that produces it |
|------|-------|---------------------------|
| 0    | per id | The coordinator holds a state for the id |
| 16   | per id | *(a broker that does not coordinate the id; one broker cannot produce it)* `NotCoordinator` |
| 42   | per id | The transactional id is the empty string |
| 53   | per id | The principal may not `Describe` this transactional id - measured as the SASL user `acltest`, which is not one of the `super.users` of the node. `Admin\AdminClient::describeTransactions()` never sees it, because the **coordinator lookup** of the same principal is refused with the same code first |
| 105  | per id | An id the coordinator has no state for: one that never ran `InitProducerId`, one whose metadata has expired, and one whose state is `Dead` |

## ListTransactions API (key 66, v0 to v2)

Which transactional ids a broker coordinates, optionally filtered. New in Kafka **3.0**, **v0**, flexible from
that version; its **v1** is Kafka **3.8** and adds the `duration_filter` of KIP-994, its **v2** Kafka **4.1** and
adds the `transactional_id_pattern` of KIP-1152. `ListTransactionsRequest.json` @ 3.0.2 names no KIP for the
version 0 either.

```
ListTransactionsRequest => [StateFilters] [ProducerIdFilters] DurationFilter TransactionalIdPattern
  StateFilters           => compact string
  ProducerIdFilters      => int64
  DurationFilter         => int64                    -- since version 1, -1 for every transaction
  TransactionalIdPattern => compact nullable string  -- since version 2, null for every id
```

```
ListTransactionsResponse => ThrottleTimeMs ErrorCode [UnknownStateFilters] [TransactionStates]
  ThrottleTimeMs      => int32
  ErrorCode           => int16
  UnknownStateFilters => compact string
  TransactionStates => TransactionalId ProducerId TransactionState
    TransactionalId  => compact string
    ProducerId       => int64
    TransactionState => compact string
```

**This api has a top-level error code, and it stands *behind* the throttle time** - the other way round than in
OffsetDelete (47), where the top-level code comes first. There is no per-entry code at all: the whole answer of a
broker succeeds or fails together, because nothing was asked for by name.

**Every broker answers for itself.** The entries are the ids of the `__transaction_state` partitions that broker
coordinates, so a client that wants the transactions of the whole cluster asks every broker and merges, exactly as
it does with ListGroups (16); `Admin\AdminClient::listTransactions()` does that. On the one-node container the
single broker coordinates all 50 partitions, so one frame is the whole cluster - and the answer carries the
transactional ids of **every** suite that ever ran against the container, which is why the unfiltered answer is
not stored as a vector.

**The two filters are ANDed and an empty one means "everything"**
(`TransactionStateManager.listTransactionStates` @ 3.9.2 applies a filter only while it is non-empty). A filter
that matches nothing is the error code 0 with an empty array, never an error. The `Dead` state is accepted as a
filter and never matches: an id whose metadata is being expired is dropped from the listing before the filters
are applied.

**A state name the coordinator does not know comes back in `unknown_state_filters`, and the error code stays 0.**
`TransactionState.fromName` @ 3.9.2 looks the name up in a map of the eight names above, and a miss is *reported*
rather than refused. The names are matched **verbatim**: `ongoing` in lower case is an unknown filter, where the
`states_filter` of ListGroups on the same node is lower-cased and trimmed before it is compared (see "Broker
quirks and observations"). The trap of the report is that the filter itself stays non-empty, so a request whose
state filters are **all** unknown is answered with an empty list and the code 0 -
`Admin\AdminClient::listTransactions()` hands the names back in its `$unknownStateFilters` parameter for exactly
that reason, and its `Admin\TransactionState` cases keep a caller from writing one by hand.
