  with `endpoint_type` 2 (a controller) on a broker listener answers **114** (`The request was sent to an endpoint
  of type BROKER, but we wanted an endpoint of type CONTROLLER`). `DescribeTopicPartitions` v0 with an **empty**
  topic array describes **every** topic of the cluster (an empty array is "all", as the null array of DescribeLogDirs
  was), and a topic that does not exist answers 3 in its row with a null `next_cursor`.
  `ConsumerGroupHeartbeat` v0 for a group that does not exist answers **69** (`Group <id> not found.`) whatever the
  member epoch, and creates nothing; `ConsumerGroupDescribe` v0 answers 69 in the row of such a group.
* **(3.7) The `controller_id` of a DescribeCluster answer is a random broker, not the controller.**
  `KafkaApis.handleDescribeCluster` @ 3.9.2 maps a `KRaftCachedControllerId` to
  `metadataCache.getRandomAliveBrokerId` - the controller of a KRaft cluster is not a broker and has no endpoint a
  client may use - and `AuthHelper.computeDescribeClusterResponse` replaces even that with **-1** when the id is
  not in the broker list it just built. On this one-node container the field is therefore the **1** of the single
  broker at both api versions, which looks like the 2.8.2 answer and means something else: "a node that will
  forward your controller request", not "the leader of the metadata quorum", which is what DescribeQuorum (55)
  answers. → "DescribeCluster API (key 60, v0 to v2)".
* **(3.7) An `endpoint_type` the server refuses costs the whole answer, and the unknown type is checked first.**
  Both refusals of KIP-919 are built as a bare `DescribeClusterResponseData`, so a **114** or a **115** comes back
  with the `endpoint_type` **1** of the schema default - never the type that was asked for - the cluster id as the
  **empty string**, the controller id -1, an empty broker array and the `Integer.MIN_VALUE` of a bit field nobody
  filled. The order is: a type that is neither 1 nor 2 is the 115 (`Unsupported endpoint type <byte>`, measured
  with **3** and with **0**, which is the `UNKNOWN` of the enum itself), a type the server is not of is the 114,
  and a version **0** request would be the 42 in both places - which no frame reaches, because version 0 carries
  no type. → "The endpoint type of KIP-919 (v1)".
* **(3.7) A node without a client-metrics receiver plugin speaks all three apis of KIP-714 and drops what it is
  given.** `ClientMetricsManager.processPushTelemetryRequest` @ 3.9.2 calls the plugin only for a non-empty blob,
  and an empty plugin list exports nothing, so a PushTelemetry of two bytes is answered **0** exactly like an
  empty one - 0 means "taken", not "stored". The `subscription_id` of a GetTelemetrySubscriptions answer is
  **never a sentinel**: it is the CRC-32C of the subscription xor the hash code of the instance id, so an instance
  that no `client-metrics` resource matches carries a number as arbitrary as any other and the empty
  `requested_metrics` is the only thing that says "nothing subscribed". The refusals of PushTelemetry are checked
  in the order terminating (**42**), throttling (**89**), subscription id (**117**), codec (**76**, measured with
  the byte 7) and size (**118**, measured with 1048577 bytes), and the **zero** client instance id is refused
  **42** before all of them. A subscription written with `kafka-configs.sh --entity-type client-metrics` reaches
  the answer at once - its `interval.ms` as the `push_interval_ms` and its `metrics` as the prefixes - and its
  `match` is applied to the client id of the **request header**, which is the only thing about the caller a
  GetTelemetrySubscriptions frame carries. Of the three keys only **71 and 72** are filtered out of the
  ApiVersions answer while `isTelemetryReceiverConfigured` is false; **74** is listed like any other api.
  → "Client metrics (KIP-714) — wire only".
* **(3.x) `message.format.version` is ignored: no log below the record batch v2 exists any more (KIP-724).** A
  topic created with `--config message.format.version=0.9.0` is accepted with the warning `This configuration will
  be ignored if ... the inter.broker.protocol.version is 3.0 or newer. This configuration is deprecated and it
  will be removed in Apache Kafka 4.0`, and `DumpLogSegments` on its log shows `magic: 2` for a record produced in
  the message format v0. `KafkaApis.handleFetchRequest` @ 3.9.2 says the same in a comment: "If the inter-broker
  protocol version is `3.0` or higher, the log config message format version is always `3.0` ... As a result, we
  always go through the down-conversion path if the fetch version is 3 or lower". So on the 2.8.2 ZooKeeper broker
  the topic decided the format of the log and the broker converted **on append**; on the node the log is always
  magic 2 and every conversion happens **on the way out**. The three integration tests that made the broker store
  a v0 or v1 log are dropped with this line. The consequences for a client are that the **43**
  (`UnsupportedForMessageFormat`) of a timestamp lookup on a log without timestamps has no reachable topic left
  (every partition has a time index), and that the up-conversion of a Produce v0-v2 message set is the only
  conversion left on the append path. → "MessageSet and Message", "RecordBatch (message format v2)",
  "What the broker converts, and when".
* **(3.x) The down-conversion matrix itself is unchanged, and it is now taken for every low Fetch version.**
  `Produce` v0-v2 and `Fetch` v0-v3 are served (`[0, 11]` and `[0, 17]` in the api table): the node accepts a
  message set v0/v1 in a Produce v2 and up-converts it, and it converts its v2 log down to magic 0 for a Fetch v0
  or v1 and to magic 1 for a Fetch v2 or v3, record for record, with the absolute offsets and the timestamps the
  formats can carry. A topic with `message.downconversion.enable=false` still answers **35**
  (`UnsupportedVersion`) per partition with `high_watermark -1`, and a zstd log still answers **76**
  (`UnsupportedCompressionType`) to a Fetch below v10. → "KIP-283 (Kafka 2.0): lazy down-conversion, and the switch
  that refuses it", "Version 10 and the zstd codec (KIP-110)".
* **(3.x) A Fetch partition that carries an error carries a `null` record set, not an empty one.**
  `FetchResponse.partitionResponse(tp, error)` @ 3.9.2 sets the partition index, the error code and the high water
  mark and leaves `Records` at the `"default": "null"` of `FetchResponse.json`, so the length on the wire is
  **-1** where the 2.8.2 broker wrote **0**. It is the answer of every refusal that is built that way - the 35 of a
  topic with the down-conversion switched off and the 76 of a zstd log below Fetch v10 among them. The record layer
  of this client reads both as "no records at all" ({@see FetchResponsePartition::getRecords()} maps `null` to an
  empty buffer), so nothing but a byte-exact assertion can tell them apart. → "Fetch API (key 1, v0 to v18)".
* **(3.x) A Fetch below v3 whose `max_bytes` does not fit the first message answers nothing at all.**
  `hardMaxBytesLimit` is still true for a version below 3, so `ReplicaManager.readFromLog` @ 3.9.2 keeps the
  incomplete first entry of the log instead of replacing it with an empty set - but that entry is a **record batch
  v2** now and the answer has to be down-converted, and `LazyDownConversionRecords` converts whole batches only.
  The client is answered `error_code 0`, the real high water mark and an **empty** record set, where the 2.8.2
  broker handed out the truncated bytes of that one message. The state a consumer has to recognise is unchanged -
  no complete message below a high water mark that has one, i.e. "raise `max.partition.fetch.bytes`", which is what
  {@see FetchResponsePartition::isSingleMessageTooLarge()} answers - but
  {@see MemoryRecords::hasPartialTrailingRecord()} is **false** for it now. → "Fetch API (key 1, v0 to v18)".
* **(3.x) The fetch-session cache is sharded, and its top eight session ids answer -1.** A 3.9.2 node splits the
  cache into `KafkaBroker.NumFetchSessionCacheShards = 8` shards and picks one with
  `sessionId / (Int.MaxValue / 8)` (`FetchSessionCache.getCacheShard`). For every id from
  `8 * (Int.MaxValue / 8) = 2147483640` up to `Int.MaxValue` that is the shard **8** of a sequence of eight, and the
  `java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException: 8 is out of bounds (min 0, max 7)` reaches the generic handler of
  `KafkaApis`: the client is answered the code **-1** (`UnknownServerError`) with the session id of the *request*
  echoed back and the requested partitions in the answer, where the 2.8.2 broker had one unsharded cache and
  answered **70** (`FetchSessionIdNotFound`) with the session id 0 for the whole range. Any id below 2147483640
  that the node does not know is answered 70 as before, and the ids the node hands out are always inside a shard,
  so a client only meets this by inventing a session id. The same sharding decides what
  **"the cache is full"** means: a new session is put into the next shard of a **round-robin**
  (`FetchSessionCache.getNextCacheShard`, a global counter modulo eight) and every shard holds
  `max.incremental.fetch.session.cache.slots / 8` sessions of its own, so a single refusal only says that the
  shard this request landed in is full - the cache as a whole refuses when eight requests in a row are. The 2.8.2
  broker had one list of 1000 slots and refused the 1001st session, full stop.
  → "Fetch sessions (v7, KIP-227)".
* **(3.x) A Fetch v13 that names an id the node does not host is answered 100 per PARTITION, never per topic.**
  The topic entry of the answer echoes the id that was asked for and its partition entry carries **100**
  `UnknownTopicId` with the high water mark, the last stable offset and the log start offset at -1 and a `null`
  record set - the same shape a version 12 answer gives the **3** `UnknownTopicOrPartition` of a topic that does
  not exist. The **zero** uuid is answered the same 100, because no topic of a cluster ever carries it, so a
  client that does not know the id of a topic has nothing to send at all: it refreshes its metadata instead,
  which is what `FetchRequest` throws `UnknownTopicIdException` for before it writes a frame.
  → "The topic ids of the fetch path (v13, KIP-516)".
* **(3.x) 106 `FetchSessionTopicIdError` is produced by mixing ids and names inside one fetch session, in both
  directions.** A session that was opened by a version 13 full fetch (topics named by id) and continued by a
  version 12 incremental fetch (topics named by name) is refused with the code, and so is the mirror image - a
  session opened at version 12 and continued at version 13. The code is a **top-level** one, like the 70 and the
  71 of KIP-227: the answer carries the session id **0** and an empty topics array, whatever version asked, and
  the client starts over with a full fetch. A session that is opened and continued with ids serves every
  incremental fetch as before, `forgotten_topics_data` included, where a partition is dropped under the id of its
  topic. → "The topic ids of the fetch path (v13, KIP-516)".
* **(3.x) A Metadata request that mixes topic ids and topic names loses the named half without a word, and a
  version below 12 that is asked by id is refused with a whole error response.**
  `KafkaApis.handleTopicMetadataRequest` @ 3.9.2 sets `useTopicId` as soon as **one** entry carries a non-zero id
  and then answers `knownTopicNames`, the names those ids resolved to, so the entries that named their topic by
  name are simply not in the answer - no error, no entry. And before that, the same method throws
  `InvalidRequestException` for every entry whose name is null or whose id is not the zero uuid while the version
  is below 12, which reaches the client as an answer with **zero brokers**, a `null` cluster id, the controller id
  **-1** and the error code **42** `InvalidRequest` in every topic entry, an empty name next to the id that was
  asked for. An empty broker array is what `Cluster::reload()` treats as "this broker has no metadata yet", so a
  by-id question must never be asked below version 12. An entry that carries neither a name nor an id - a null
  name and the zero uuid at version 12 - is answered with the topic error code **-1** (`UnknownServerError`).
  An id the cluster does not host is the ordinary case and is answered **100** `UnknownTopicId` with a **null**
  name, which is the reason version 12 made that field nullable.
  → "Metadata by topic id (v12, KIP-516)".
* **(3.x) A refused Produce batch names its record errors twice, and the summary is the long one now.**
  `LogValidator.processRecordErrors` @ 3.9.2 - the record validation moved to
  `org.apache.kafka.storage.internals.log` with Kafka 3.0 - builds the partition-level `error_message` as `One or
  more records have been rejected due to <n> record errors in total, and only showing the first three errors at
  most: [RecordError(batchIndex=1, message='Compacted topic cannot accept message without key in topic partition
  <topic>-0'), …]`, where the 2.8.2 broker sent the first sentence alone. The per-record `record_errors` array of
  v8 is unchanged (one entry per bad record, by its index in the **sent** batch), so the summary is a repetition of
  it; a client that shows the array should not also show the summary. → "The record errors of a refused batch (v8,
  KIP-467)".
* **(3.8) A Produce v11 is answered 120 `TransactionAbortable` where the very same frame at v10 is answered 48,
  and the api version alone decides it.** `KafkaApis.handleProduceRequest` @ 3.9.2 turns the header into the
  `TransactionSupportedOperation` of the append in one line — `val transactionSupportedOperation = if
  (request.header.apiVersion > 10) genericError else defaultError` — and `AddPartitionsToTxnManager` @ 3.9.2 maps
  a **120** of the transaction coordinator back to the **48** `InvalidTxnState` for everything below ("For
  backward compatibility with clients"). Measured with the partition 0 of a two-partition topic added to the open
  transaction and the batch sent to the partition **1**: at v11 the partition answers 120 with `base_offset`,
  `log_append_time` and `log_start_offset` all -1 and **no `error_message` at all**, at v10 the 48 with the
  message "Partition was not added to the transaction" — 60 against 102 bytes of body, out of two requests that
  differ in the two bytes of the api version and the correlation id. The message is not part of the bargain:
  `ReplicaManager.handleProduceAppend` @ 3.9.2 writes a custom one for the 48 alone. → "The abortable transaction
  error of KIP-890 (v11)".
* **(3.8) `transaction.version` is not a feature of a 3.9.2 node**, so the 120 of this line is the one the
  *partition verification* produces and not the one the transaction protocol v2 of KIP-890 part 2 would. The node
  finalizes exactly two features — `metadata.version` at 21 (`3.9-IV0`) and `kraft.version` at 0 — in the
  ApiVersions v3 answer as in `kafka-features.sh --bootstrap-server localhost:9092 describe`, and
  `transaction.partition.verification.enable` is `true`, which is what makes a transactional produce ask the
  coordinator at all. A client of this line therefore keeps sending the `AddPartitionsToTxn` of KIP-98 before its
  batches, exactly as it did below 3.8. → "The abortable transaction error of KIP-890 (v11)".
* **(3.x) ListOffsets: the target time `-3` of KIP-734 is version-gated per partition, and the gate is 35.**
  `KafkaApis.handleListOffsetRequestV1AndAbove` @ 3.9.2 maps every negative target time to the api version that
  introduced it (`timestampMinSupportedVersion`: `-2`/`-1` → 1, `-3` `MAX_TIMESTAMP` → **7**, `-4`
  `EARLIEST_LOCAL_TIMESTAMP` → 8, `-5` `LATEST_TIERED_TIMESTAMP` → 9) and answers a partition whose target time
  needs more than the version of the request with **35** (`UnsupportedVersion`), timestamp, offset and leader epoch
  `-1`, leaving the connection open and serving the other partitions of the same frame. The 2.8.2 ZooKeeper broker
  knew neither the value nor the check — and **a 3.0 broker did not have the check either**: it was added after
  3.0.2, whose `KafkaApis.scala` passes every negative value straight into `fetchOffsetForTimestamp`. So the
  refusal is a fact of the node, not of the release the version belongs to. Measured: a `-3` of version 6 and a
  `-4` of version 7 are both answered 35; a `-3` of version 7 is answered the largest timestamp of the partition
  with the offset that carries it - the **offset 1** of a three-record log that ends at 3, because the records were
  stamped `t0`, `t0 + 5000`, `t0 + 2000` - and an empty log is answered the code 0 with `-1` / `-1`.
  → "Offsets API (key 2, v0 to v11), a.k.a. ListOffset".
* **(3.5) The local log start offset of KIP-405 (`-4`, ListOffsets v8) is the log start offset on this node, and
  an empty partition answers `0`, not `-1`.** `remote.log.storage.system.enable` is off - the node carries no
  tiered storage at all - so `UnifiedLog.localLogStartOffset` @ 3.9.2 is the log start offset itself and the
  target time `-4` answers exactly what `-2` answers: the offset **0** with the timestamp `-1` and the leader
  epoch of the partition, on a three-record log and on an **empty** one alike. That is the difference to the max
  timestamp `-3` of KIP-734, which has nothing to report on an empty log and is answered `-1` / `-1` there. The
  `-5` `LATEST_TIERED_TIMESTAMP` of KIP-1005 needs version 9 and is the per-partition 35 for the version 8 this
  client sends. → "Offsets API (key 2, v0 to v11), a.k.a. ListOffset".
* **(3.5) The 109 `OffsetMovedToTieredStorage` of Fetch v14 cannot be produced here, and a follower fetch of
  Fetch v15 is refused by the replica set, not by its epoch.** Without remote storage a fetch below the log start
  offset is the ordinary **1** `OffsetOutOfRange` at the versions 13, 14 and 15 alike, so the code 109 that
  version 14 exists for is documented on the wire alone. The `replica_state` of version 15 (KIP-903) travels as
  the **tag 1** of the request, 13 bytes - an int32 replica id, an int64 replica epoch and the tag buffer of the
  structure - and is left out altogether for the `-1` / `-1` of a consumer, which is why a version 15 consumer
  fetch is four bytes shorter than the version 14 one. A frame that really names a replica id is a follower fetch:
  `CLUSTER_ACTION` is required for it and the `super.users` of this container grant it to `User:ANONYMOUS`, so the
  node serves the request and answers the **partition** - the one broker of the node is the *leader* of every
  partition and not one of its followers, so `Partition.followerReplicaOrThrow` @ 3.9.2 answers **75**
  `UnknownLeaderEpoch` when the partition entry named a `current_leader_epoch` and **6** `NotLeaderForPartition`
  when it did not, for the replica ids 1 and 42 and for every epoch alike. The debugging replica id `-2` and a
  state of `-1` with an epoch are served as ordinary consumer fetches, because `isFromFollower` is `replicaId >=
  0`. → "The tiered-storage error of KIP-405 (v14)", "The replica state of KIP-903 (v15)".
* **(3.5) A fetch session survives a raise of the api version.** A session opened by a version 13 full fetch and
  continued by a version 15 incremental request keeps its id and is served normally; the **106**
  `FetchSessionTopicIdError` of Kafka 3.1 fences a session whose topics change the *kind of name* they travel
  under, not one whose requests change their version. → "The replica state of KIP-903 (v15)".
* **(3.7) The leader discovery of KIP-951 is reachable on a one-broker node - through the follower fetch of
  KIP-903, and at Fetch v16 alone.** `KafkaApis.handleFetchRequest` @ 3.9.2 fills the tagged `current_leader` of a
  partition entry and the tagged `node_endpoints` of the body in for the codes **6** `NotLeaderForPartition` and
  **74** `FencedLeaderEpoch`, and only inside an `if (versionId >= 16)`: the `current_leader` has been on the wire
  since version 12, but no version below 16 ever carries a value in it. The 6 is producible here, because a fetch
  that claims to be the replica 1 is refused by the replica set (the (3.5) item above), and the node then names
  **itself**: `current_leader` `1` / `0` and `node_endpoints` `1 ⇒ 127.0.0.1:9092` with a `null` rack, the
  endpoint of the listener the request arrived on. The very same frame at version 15 is answered the same 6 in
  **76** bytes instead of 110 and names neither. The **74** is not reachable: it needs a `current_leader_epoch`
  below the one of the partition, and the log of this node never leaves the epoch 0; an epoch *above* it is the
  **75** `UnknownLeaderEpoch`, which is not one of the two codes of the KIP and is answered without a hint of any
  kind. → "The leader discovery of KIP-951 (v16)".
* **(3.7) A Produce v10 answer of this node never carries the hint at all.** The produce half of KIP-951 is
  written for the error code **6** alone (`KafkaApis.handleProduceRequest` @ 3.9.2, the `apiVersion >= 10` branch
  of the send callback), and the one broker of the node is the leader of every partition it hosts, so no produce
  of a client can be answered 6: an accepted batch is the version 9 answer byte for byte - three empty tagged
  sections, 60 bytes of body - and the one produce error a client can provoke by itself, the partition 99 of a
  topic with one partition, is the per-partition **3** `UnknownTopicOrPartition` with nothing in its tagged
  sections either. The version is therefore in the client with its fields decoded, its answer measured and one
  **constructed** frame for the shape (`produce.response.v10.current-leader`), whose two structures are the ones
  the same node really writes into the Fetch v16 answer above. → "The leader discovery of KIP-951 (v10)".
* **(3.7) Neither version changes the request.** `ProduceRequest.json` and `FetchRequest.json` @ 3.7.2 declare no
  field of v10 and v16 - "Version 10 is the same as version 9 (KIP-951)", "Version 16 is the same as version 15
  (KIP-951)" - and the node accepts both frames as the ones of the version below with another number in the
  header: 158 bytes for the produce of this wave at v9 and at v10, 109 for the consumer fetch at v15 and at v16.
  A fetch session opened by a version 15 full fetch is continued by a version 16 incremental request without a
  word, as it was across 13 → 15. → "Produce API (key 0, v0 to v13)", "Fetch API (key 1, v0 to v18)".
* **(3.9) The `replica_directory_id` of Fetch v17 is parsed and ignored by every fetch of an ordinary topic.**
  KIP-853 put the field into the partition entry of the request for the replication of the **metadata** log:
  `KafkaRaftClient.handleFetchRequest` @ 3.9.2 builds `ReplicaKey.of(FetchRequest.replicaId(request),
  fetchPartition.replicaDirectoryId())` out of it, and that handler serves `__cluster_metadata` on the controller
  listener. `ReplicaManager.fetchMessages` @ 3.9.2, which serves every other fetch, never reads the field.
  Measured on the node, against a topic of one partition and two records: a consumer fetch that names the real
  `directory.id` of `/tmp/kafka-logs`, one that names the id of the other log directory and one that names 16
  random bytes are all answered the same records in the same 170 bytes; a fetch that claims to be the replica 1 is
  answered the **6** `NotLeaderForPartition` with the leader hint of KIP-951 whether it names a directory or not,
  and with a `current_leader_epoch` the **75** `UnknownLeaderEpoch` the same way — the answers are byte for byte
  the ones of the very same frames at v15 and v16. The directory of KIP-853 is never reached for the same reason
  the epoch of KIP-903 is not: `Partition.followerReplicaOrThrow` refuses the claim first.
  → "The replica directory id of KIP-853 (v17)".
* **(3.9) A Fetch v17 of a consumer is the v16 frame byte for byte, and a session lives across the raise.** The
  zero uuid is the default of the new tag, so a consumer writes no tagged field at all and the partition entry
  still ends in the empty `00`: 109 request bytes at v16 and at v17, 170 answer bytes at both. A session opened by
  a version 16 full fetch and continued by a version 17 incremental request keeps its id and is served, as it was
  across 13 → 15 and 15 → 16. → "The replica directory id of KIP-853 (v17)", "Fetch API (key 1, v0 to v18)".
* **(3.9) `-5` `LATEST_TIERED_TIMESTAMP` answers the offset `-1` with the error code 0, on a filled log and on an
  empty one alike.** `UnifiedLog.fetchOffsetByTimestamp` @ 3.9.2 answers `highestOffsetInRemoteStorage()` only
  inside an `if (remoteLogEnabled())` and writes `TimestampAndOffset(NO_TIMESTAMP, -1L, Optional.of(-1))` when it
  is off, which is how this node runs: the answer of a two-record log and of an empty one is the same `0` / `-1` /
  `-1` / `-1`, where `-4` answers the offset **0** for both. It is the one target time of this api whose `-1` does
  not mean "nothing matched" but "nothing of this partition is tiered". The same map that gates `-3` and `-4`
  demands version **9** for it — a `-5` at version 8 is the per-partition **35** — and a target time the map does
  not know at all, `-6` and below, is that same 35 at **every** version, the version 9 of this client included.
  **(4.2)** Kafka 4.2 gave `-6` a meaning, the earliest pending upload offset of KIP-1023 at version 11, which the
  4.3.1 node answers `-1` with the code 0 as it answers `-5`; `-7` is the first value it refuses at every version.
  → "Offsets API (key 2, v0 to v11), a.k.a. ListOffset", "The earliest pending upload offset of KIP-1023 (v11)".
* **(3.x) An auto-created topic is answered `3`, not `5`, and it has its leader at the next request.** On a
  ZooKeeper-backed broker the Metadata handler created the topic in ZooKeeper itself and could answer
  **5** (`LeaderNotAvailable`) with an empty partition array for it. On the node `AutoTopicCreationManager` sends a
  CreateTopics request to the controller and answers the Metadata request from the metadata image of that instant,
  in which the topic does not exist: the answer is **3** (`UnknownTopicOrPartition`) with an empty partition array,
  for `allow_auto_topic_creation = true` and `false` alike. What tells the two apart is what happens next - with
  the flag on, the topic is complete about 100 ms later, with its **leader already elected** (the controller elects
  it with the creation, so there is no `LeaderNotAvailable` window at all), and with the flag off it never appears.
  Every helper that waits for a fresh topic must therefore retry on **3** as well as on 5 and 6.
  → "`AllowAutoTopicCreation` (v4, Kafka 0.11, KIP-4): asking without creating".
* **(3.x) The one broker of the container is the node id `1`, not `0`.** A KRaft node is formatted with the
  `node.id` of its `controller.quorum.voters` entry, which is 1 for this container, so every `replicas`, `isr`,
  `offline_replicas`, `leader` and `controller_id` of a Metadata answer names **1**. The 2.x line's broker was the
  broker 0. A test reads the id out of the answer (`brokers`), it never writes it down. → "Metadata API (key 3, v0
  to v11)", "`ControllerId`: which broker is the controller".
* **(3.x) ControlledShutdown (7) has no method in the admin client any more.** The api is `["zkBroker",
  "controller"]`, so a client listener neither announces nor serves it, and `AdminClient::controlledShutdown()` -
  which the 2.x line still sent - is removed together with the three tests of `AdminApiTest` that exercised it. The
  message classes and the vectors of key 7 stay: the api is on the 3.9.2 wire, on the controller listener.
  → "ControlledShutdown API (key 7, v0 to v3)".
* **(3.x) A delegation token is a record of the metadata log, and it is there a moment after the answer that
  created it.** KIP-900 (Kafka 3.6) moved CreateDelegationToken (38), RenewDelegationToken (39) and
  ExpireDelegationToken (40) to the controller, which writes a `DelegationTokenRecord` or a
  `RemoveDelegationTokenRecord`; every token cache of the cluster is filled by the `DelegationTokenPublisher` when
  that record is **replayed**, which happens after the answer has left. Measured on the node: about **66 ms** in
  which a renew or an expire of a token that was just created answers **62**, and about **77 ms** in which a
  describe does not list it. A 62 right after a create is a race, not a lost token; the suite polls for the token
  instead of sleeping. The setting is `delegation.token.secret.key` here, and there is no ZooKeeper znode behind a
  token any longer. → "Delegation tokens (KIP-48)".
* **(3.x) An expired token can still be expired, and a renew of it still cannot.**
  `DelegationTokenControlManager.expireDelegationToken` @ 3.9.2 handles the **negative** period before it tests the
  timestamps, so an immediate expiry of a token that ran out of its maximum lifetime writes the removal record and
  answers **0** with the clock of the node, where the 2.8.2 ZooKeeper broker answered 66 for it; a second expiry is
  the 62 of a token that is gone, and a renew is still 66. → "ExpireDelegationToken API (key 40, v0 to v2)".
* **(3.x) Who may describe which token is decided by `super.users` now.** The 2.x line measured "without an
  authorizer every authenticated principal describes every token"; with the `StandardAuthorizer` on,
  `DelegationTokenManager.filterToken` asks it for `DESCRIBE_TOKENS` on the `User` resource of the owner and falls
  back to "owner or renewer" when it says no. The super users `admin` and `kafkatest` therefore still see every
  token with its hmac, while `acltest` sees only the tokens it owns or may renew - and a foreign owner is answered
  with an empty array and the code 0, never with a 29 or a 63.
  → "DescribeDelegationToken API (key 41, v0 to v3)".
* **(3.x) Two changes of one user in one AlterUserScramCredentials request are 92, mechanism or not.**
  `ScramControlManager.alterCredentials` @ 3.9.2 keys the changes it collects by the **user name alone**, so the
  SHA-256 and the SHA-512 credential of one user - which a 2.8.2 broker wrote in one request - are *"A user
  credential cannot be altered twice in the same request"* here and take two requests. Both SCRAM apis are answered
  from the metadata log as well: a describe that follows an alter reads the image of the broker, which is about
  30 ms behind the controller. → "AlterUserScramCredentials API (key 51, v0)".
* **(3.x) The node finalizes `metadata.version`, and a feature update is refused with 95 instead of 42.** The
  ApiVersions answer carries `metadata.version` 1 … 21 as supported and 21/21 as finalized, with the offset of the
  metadata log as the epoch, where a ZooKeeper-backed 2.8.2 cluster had nothing at all and the epoch 0.
  `FeatureControlManager.updateFeature` answers **95** (`InvalidUpdateVersion`) with a message that names the
  controller and the range it knows - `Local controller 1 does not support this feature.`, `Local controller 1 only
  supports versions 1-21`, `Can't downgrade the version of this feature without setting the upgrade type to either
  safe or unsafe downgrade.` - and the **deletion of a feature that was never finalized is accepted**, because the
  level 0 is a level every node supports. → "UpdateFeatures API (key 57, v0 to v2)".
* **(3.x) The version 1 of UpdateFeatures really does not write, and the node forwards the request.** With
  `validate_only = true` the controller answers the per-feature **0** of an update it would make and leaves the
  cluster alone: the finalized `metadata.version` of the node stays 21 after a *safe* and after an *unsafe*
  downgrade to 20 have both been answered 0, and the level 0 of `kraft.version` stays 0 after the same dry run
  said it would be raised to 1. The `upgrade_type` byte is what those two rows differ in - a version 0 request
  cannot tell them apart - and the byte **0** (`UNKNOWN`) has a refusal of its own, **95** with *"The controller
  does not support the given upgrade type."*. The api is `"listeners": ["zkBroker", "broker", "controller"]` from
  Kafka 3.0 on, so **41** (`NotController`) is not producible on this node at all: any broker forwards the request
  to the controller in an Envelope (KIP-590), and the **31** a principal outside `super.users` is answered carries
  the `toString` of that forwarded request - `Request(processor=1, connectionId=127.0.0.1:9096-…,
  listenerName=ListenerName(CONTROLLER), …, envelope=Some(Request(…))) is not authorized.` - as its
  `error_message`. → "The upgrade type and the dry run of KIP-778 (v1)".
* **(3.x) DescribeQuorum is served on a client listener, and the combined node is one voter with no observer.**
  The key 55 is in the api table of the node (the raft apis 52, 53, 54 and 59 are not), and a request for the
  partition 0 of `__cluster_metadata` answers the top-level 0 with the leader **1**, its epoch, the high watermark
  of the metadata log and exactly one `current_voters` entry - the node itself - and an empty `observers` array,
  because a `process.roles=broker,controller` node votes and observes nothing. The two timestamps of KIP-836 are
  the **current time** in the leader's own entry, not the -1 the `about` of `LastFetchTimestamp` in
  `DescribeQuorumResponse.json` announces for it: `LeaderState.describeReplicaState` @ 3.3.2 sets both to
  `currentTimeMs` for the local id. Any other topic is answered **3** per partition with every other field of the
  entry left at the zero of its type - the `leader_id` is 0, not -1 - an empty topic array is answered the
  top-level 0 and nine bytes, and a principal without `Describe` on the cluster is answered the top-level **31**
  with no topic at all. → "DescribeQuorum API (key 55, v0 to v2)", "The two timestamps of a replica state (v1,
  KIP-836)".
* **(3.9) The `nodes` array of a DescribeQuorum v2 names the CONTROLLER listener, and every directory id in the
  answer is the zero uuid.** The four fields KIP-853 added are all in the answer of the node, and two of them say
  something a client should not be surprised by. The top-level `nodes` array carries the node id **1** with one
  listener, `CONTROLLER` at `localhost:9096` — the listener *inside* the container, which no client of this
  repository connects to: the array describes the raft quorum, not the broker the request arrived at, so the
  endpoint in it is not one a client can use. And every `replica_directory_id` is 16 zero bytes, although the
  `meta.properties` of the container carries a real `directory.id`: the quorum runs the **static**
  `controller.quorum.voters` of KIP-595, i.e. its `kraft.version` feature is finalized at **0**, and a static voter
  set has no directory ids. A request about a topic the node could not describe is answered with an **empty**
  `nodes` array. → "The nodes, the directory ids and the error messages of KIP-853 (v2)".
* **(3.9) The two `error_message` fields of a DescribeQuorum v2 are the empty string, not a null.** Both are
  declared nullable with the default null, and the node writes the compact `01` of an empty string wherever there
  is no error: the generated `DescribeQuorumResponseData` initialises them with `""` and the handler sets them
  only when it has something to say — the same thing the 3.3 wave measured at DescribeAcls. Where there *is* an
  error the message is worth reading: a partition that no raft quorum replicates carries `This server does not
  host this topic-partition.` next to its 3, and a principal without `Describe` on the cluster is answered
  `Cluster authorization failed.` next to the top-level 31, which the version 1 had no field for.
  → "The nodes, the directory ids and the error messages of KIP-853 (v2)".
* **(3.9) The node supports two features, and a client sees the second one only at ApiVersions v4.** The tagged
  field 0 of an ApiVersions answer holds `metadata.version` 1…21 in every version of the api and `kraft.version`
  **0**…1 only from the version 4 on: a feature whose `min_version` is 0 is filtered out of every answer below it
  (`ApiVersionsResponse.maybeFilterSupportedFeatureKeys` @ 3.9.2, KAFKA-17011), because a client of Kafka 3.0 to
  3.8 reads the 0 as "there is no such feature". The two answers are the same 61 rows, the same throttle time and
  the same finalized features; the v4 is **19 bytes** longer, and those 19 bytes are the whole bump. The
  *finalized* map names `metadata.version` alone in both, because `kraft.version` is finalized at the level 0 and
  a feature at level 0 is not finalized at all. → "ApiVersions API (key 18, v0 to v4)".
* **(3.9) AddRaftVoter and RemoveRaftVoter are in the api table and refuse everything, in three places.** The two
  reconfiguration apis of KIP-853 are `["controller", "broker"]`, so a client listener lists them and a broker
  forwards them; what comes back is a refusal in every shape the probe could build. A **foreign** cluster id is the
  **104** (`InconsistentClusterId`), a voter key the api cannot read — the zero directory id, an empty listener
  array — is the **42** (`InvalidRequest`) with `Add voter request didn't include a valid voter`, and a
  **well-formed** voter is the **35** (`UnsupportedVersion`) with `Cluster doesn't support adding voter because the
  kraft.version feature is 0`. The order is the order of the checks in `KafkaRaftClient.handleAddVoterRequest`
  @ 3.9.2: cluster id, voter key, feature. **The error codes 125, 126 and 127 are therefore declared on this line
  and produced by nothing**: they live behind a `kraft.version` of 1, which this node does not have.
  → "The raft-voter apis (keys 80 and 81) and the share groups — probe only".
* **(3.9) The nine share-group apis are not refused with a code, they are not in the protocol.** 76 to 79 and 83
  to 87 all carry `"latestVersionUnstable": true`, so `ApiKeys.toApiVersion(false)` leaves them out of the
  ApiVersions answer and `isApiEnabled` refuses every version of them: a ShareGroupHeartbeat v0 ends in `Received
  request api key SHARE_GROUP_HEARTBEAT with version 0 which is not enabled` and a **closed connection**, exactly
  like a `zkBroker` api. The four error codes 121 to 124 of KIP-932 are declared here and unreachable on this node.
  → "The raft-voter apis (keys 80 and 81) and the share groups — probe only".
* **(3.x) The reassignment refusals are the words of the KRaft controller, and an unknown partition is 3 where the
  2.8.2 broker answered 85.** `ReplicationControlManager.alterPartitionReassignment` @ 3.9.2 resolves the topic id
  and the `PartitionRegistration` **before** it looks at whether `replicas` is null, so a cancellation and a
  reassignment of a partition that does not exist are the same **3** - `Unable to find a topic named <topic>.` or
  `Unable to find partition <topic>:<partition>.` - and the **85** is left for a partition that exists and has
  nothing in flight. A replica set that names an unregistered broker is still 39, with `The manual partition
  assignment includes broker 7, but no such broker is registered.` instead of the `Replica assignment has brokers
  that are not alive …` of the 2.8.2 broker. → "AlterPartitionReassignments API (key 45, v0 and v1)".
* **(3.x) ElectLeaders names the topic and the partition it could not find.**
  `ReplicationControlManager.electLeader` @ 3.9.2 answers the code 3 with `No such topic as <topic>` and `No such
  partition as <topic>-<partition>`, where the 2.8.2 broker answered the generic `The partition does not exist.`;
  the 84 of a partition that needs no election keeps its `Leader election not needed for topic partition.`, and an
  election of a topic that does not exist still creates nothing. → "ElectLeaders API (key 43, v0 to v2)".
* **(3.x) The node is the broker `1`, and every broker id a client writes down has to say so.** A KRaft node needs
  a `node.id` and the image sets `node.id=1`, where every ZooKeeper image of the lines below ran as the broker `0`.
  The metadata answers the replicas of a partition as `[1]`, `ConfigResource::broker(0)` is refused with **42** and
  `Unexpected broker id, expected 1 or empty string, but received 0` (the sentence itself is the one of KIP-226,
  only the id in it moved), and a manual replica assignment that names the 0 is refused with **39**.
  → "CreateTopics API (key 19, v0 to v7)", "CreatePartitions API (key 37, v0 to v3)",
  "DescribeConfigs API (key 32, v0 to v4)".
* **(3.x) A CreateTopics assignment IS checked against the registered brokers now.** The 2.8.2 broker deliberately
  did not ("we don't check that replicaAssignment contains unknown brokers"): the topic was written to ZooKeeper,
  never got a leader, and the request answered **7** after its timeout.
  `ReplicationControlManager.validateManualPartitionAssignment()` @ 3.9.2 looks every id up in
  `clusterControl.brokerRegistrations()` and refuses the topic with **39** and `The manual partition assignment
  includes broker 0, but no such broker is registered.` — nothing is created, and the leaderless topic the 2.x
  document describes cannot arise. The same check runs for CreatePartitions, where 2.8.2 already had one.
  → "CreateTopics API (key 19, v0 to v7)".
* **(3.x) `timeout_ms = 0` creates nothing any more — on any of the controller apis.** `ZkAdminManager.
  createTopics()` @ 2.8.2 wrote the topic into ZooKeeper and only then waited for the timeout, so a 0 answered
  **7** for a topic that appeared a moment later; the same held for CreatePartitions. `ControllerApis` @ 3.9.2
  turns `timeout_ms` into a DEADLINE (`requestTimeoutMsToDeadlineNs`) that travels with the controller event, and
  an event whose deadline has already passed expires before its records are written: the answer is the same code
  **7**, with a **null** `error_message`, and the metadata log never sees the topic or the partitions (measured
  over three seconds after the answer, where the node publishes a topic it really creates within ~40 ms). A
  DeleteTopics with `timeout_ms = 0` is answered with the 7 in EVERY entry, before any name is resolved — which is
  why the controller probe of a client without Metadata v1 (an illegal topic name, answered with 3 by the
  controller and 41 by a follower) has to carry a real timeout here; with one it answers **3** and the default
  message of the code, `This server does not host this topic-partition.`. An empty topic array is still answered
  with an empty result whatever the timeout is. → "CreateTopics API (key 19, v0 to v7)",
  "DeleteTopics API (key 20, v0 to v6)", "CreatePartitions API (key 37, v0 to v3)".
* **(3.x) Every refusal of the three controller apis is worded by `ReplicationControlManager` @ 3.9.2.** The codes
  are the ones of the lines below, the sentences are new, and two of them carry something the 2.8.2 sentence did
  not (the topic name of a shrink, the registered broker count of a replication factor). Measured on the node, next
  to what the 2.8.2 ZooKeeper broker answered:

  | Request | Code | On the 2.8.2 ZooKeeper broker | On the 3.9.2 KRaft node |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | CreateTopics, replication factor 2 on one broker | 38 | `Replication factor: 2 larger than available brokers: 1.` | `Unable to replicate the partition 2 time(s): The target replication factor of 2 cannot be reached because only 1 broker(s) are registered.` - the 4.3.1 node appends ` or some brokers have all their log directories cordoned.` (`StripedReplicaPlacer` @ 4.3.1; 4.0 to 4.2 end at "registered.") |
  | CreateTopics, `num_partitions = 0` | 37 | `Number of partitions must be larger than 0.` | `Number of partitions was set to an invalid non-positive value.` |
  | CreateTopics, an assignment next to 1/1 | 42 | `Both numPartitions or replicationFactor and replicasAssignments were set. Both cannot be used at the same time.` | `A manual partition assignment was specified, but replication factor was not set to -1.` |
  | CreatePartitions, fewer partitions than the topic has | 37 | `Topic currently has 3 partitions, which is higher than the requested 2.` | `The topic <name> currently has 3 partition(s); 2 would not be an increase.` |
  | CreatePartitions, the count the topic already has | 37 | `Topic already has 3 partitions.` | `Topic already has 3 partition(s).` |
  | CreatePartitions, too few assignments | 39 | `Increasing the number of partitions by 2 but 1 assignments provided.` | `Attempted to add 2 additional partition(s), but only 1 assignment(s) were specified.` |
  | CreatePartitions, an unregistered broker | 39 | `Unknown broker(s) in replica assignment: 7.` | `The manual partition assignment includes broker 7, but no such broker is registered.` |
  | CreatePartitions, a topic that does not exist | 3 | `The topic '<name>' does not exist.` | *(no message at all)* |

  The last row is the one a client notices: `createPartitions()` @ 3.9.2 throws the bare
  `new UnknownTopicOrPartitionException()`, so `ApiError.fromThrowable` sends `error_message = null` and the answer
  says nothing about the topic. AlterConfigs still names it (`The topic '<name>' does not exist.`), because the
  configuration path throws the exception with a message of its own.
  → "CreateTopics API (key 19, v0 to v7)", "CreatePartitions API (key 37, v0 to v3)".
* **(3.x) A DeleteTopics entry that names a topic by its name AND its id is refused per ENTRY, and the rest of the
  request is carried out.** On the 2.8.2 broker the `InvalidRequestException` escaped `handleDeleteTopicsRequest`,
  the whole request was answered with the code 42 and nothing was deleted. `ControllerApis.deleteTopics()` @ 3.9.2
  reads the entries first and appends a response of its own for every one it cannot use — **42** with
  `You may not specify both topic name and topic id.`, and `Neither topic name nor id were specified.` /
  `Duplicate topic name.` / `Duplicate topic id.` for the other three malformed shapes — while every entry it can
  read is deleted. A client that batches deletions has to read the answer entry by entry: a malformed neighbour no
  longer protects the others. → "DeleteTopics API (key 20, v0 to v6)".
* **(3.x) `message.format.version` is a `DEFAULT_CONFIG` of a fresh topic again.** The image of the 2.x line set
  `log.message.format.version=2.8-IV1`, so the topic option inherited the source `STATIC_BROKER_CONFIG`; the option
  is ignored from Kafka 3.0 on (KIP-724), the KRaft image writes no `log.message.format.version` at all, and
  `log.segment.bytes=1073741824` is the only broker option of the image whose topic synonym (`segment.bytes`) a
  fresh topic reports as a non-default. → "DescribeConfigs API (key 32, v0 to v4)".
* **(3.x) The config refusals moved between the codes 40, 42 and -1, in both directions.** The validation is split
  on a KRaft node: `ConfigAdminManager` @ 3.9.2 runs on the BROKER, before the request is forwarded, and
  `ConfigurationControlManager` @ 3.9.2 on the controller. Measured on the node:

  | Request | 2.8.2 | 3.9.2 | The sentence of the node |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | CreateTopics, a value the `ConfigDef` cannot parse | -1 | **40** | `Invalid value soon for configuration retention.ms: Not a number of type LONG` |
  | AlterConfigs, a value the `ConfigDef` cannot parse | 42 | **40** | `Invalid value soon for configuration retention.ms: Not a number of type LONG` |
  | AlterConfigs, a null value | -1 | **42** | `Null value not supported for : retention.ms` |
  | AlterConfigs / IncrementalAlterConfigs, an unknown option name (SET) | 40 | 40 | `Unknown topic config name: no.such.option` |
  | IncrementalAlterConfigs, a null value outside a DELETE | 42 | 42 | `Null value not supported for : retention.ms` (2.8.2: `Null value not supported for : SET:retention.ms`) |
  | IncrementalAlterConfigs, the same option twice | 42 | 42 | `Error due to duplicate config keys` (2.8.2: `Error due to duplicate config keys : retention.ms`) |
  | IncrementalAlterConfigs, APPEND to an option that is not a LIST | 42 | **40** | `Can't APPEND to key retention.ms because its type is not LIST.` (2.8.2: `Config value append is not allowed for config key: retention.ms`) |
  | IncrementalAlterConfigs, APPEND to an option that does not exist | -1 | **40** | `Can't APPEND to key not.an.option because its type is not LIST.` |

  `validateAlterConfig()` @ 3.9.2 catches the plain `ConfigException` of the config framework by its type and
  answers `INVALID_CONFIG` — where a 2.8.2 CreateTopics let it fall through `Errors.forException` to the -1 and a
  2.8.2 AlterConfigs wrapped it in an `InvalidRequestException` (42) whose sentence carried the prefix `Invalid
  config value for resource Resource(type=TOPIC, name='…'}: `, which the node does not send. A null value never reaches the controller at all, because
  `ConfigAdminManager` refuses the whole resource on the broker. And an APPEND is checked against the SCHEMA
  (`isSplittable`) BEFORE the key is looked up, so an unknown key is "not a LIST" rather than the unknown server
  error the `NoSuchElementException` of `ConfigDef.listType()` used to be — the only refusal of these two apis that
  a 2.8.2 broker answered with -1 and a KRaft node answers with a code at all.
  → "AlterConfigs API (key 33, v0 to v2)", "IncrementalAlterConfigs API (key 44, v0 and v1)".
* **(3.x) The documentation strings of the topic options moved and were rewritten.** They live in
  `clients/…/common/config/TopicConfig.java` @ 3.9.2, not in `core/…/log/LogConfig.scala`, and the prose of
  `cleanup.policy` no longer begins with "A string that is either "delete" or "compact"" but describes the two
  policies one at a time (`This config designates the retention policy to use on log segments. The "delete" policy
  … The "compact" policy will enable <a href="#compaction">log compaction</a> …`). The `config_type` of KIP-569 is
  unchanged. → "DescribeConfigs API (key 32, v0 to v4)".
* **(3.x) A quota the controller accepted reaches DescribeClientQuotas a moment later, and the entries are not
  ordered.** AlterClientQuotas is a controller write: the node answers it once the `ClientQuotaRecord` is committed
  to the metadata log, and the `ClientQuotaMetadataManager` of the broker fills the cache DescribeClientQuotas
  reads when it REPLAYS that record. A read that follows a write in the same process therefore has to be repeated
  — the 2.8.2 broker had the same gap around its ZooKeeper watch, and the 44 ms Nagle delay that every request of
  this client carried before the io fix of #166 covered it. The ENTRIES of the answer come out of a `HashMap` in
  `ClientQuotaCache.describeClientQuotas()` @ 3.9.2, so their order is not the sorted one of the ZooKeeper children
  the 2.8.2 broker walked: a filter that matches two entities may answer them either way round, while the values
  INSIDE one entity keep a stable order. → "DescribeClientQuotas API (key 48, v0 and v1)",
  "AlterClientQuotas API (key 49, v0 and v1)".
* **(3.x) The two refusals of a DescribeClientQuotas filter are worded and coded differently.** An **unknown entity
  type** is still the top-level **35** with the null entry array, but the sentence is `Unsupported entity type
  t1-nonsense` where the 2.8.2 broker said `Custom entity type 't1-nonsense' not supported`. An **unknown match
  type** is the **42** with `Unknown match type 7`, where the 2.8.2 broker let the `IllegalArgumentException`
  escape into the generic handler of `KafkaApis` and answered **-1** with no message at all.
  → "DescribeClientQuotas API (key 48, v0 and v1)".
* **(3.0) `beginTransaction()` never reaches the coordinator, and DescribeTransactions proves it.** A producer
  that has run `InitProducerId` and begun a transaction is reported `Empty` by the key 65; the state moves to
  `Ongoing` only with the first `AddPartitionsToTxn` of that transaction, which is the first frame the coordinator
  sees of it. The start time of the transaction, on the other hand, **outlives** it:
  `TransactionMetadata.txnStartTimestamp` @ 3.9.2 is never cleared, so a `CompleteCommit` entry still names when
  the committed transaction began while its `topics` array is already empty, and only an id that never had a
  transaction answers the **-1** of the specification. An entry that carries an *error* answers 0 there, not -1 -
  the defaults of the specification, not a measurement of the id. → "DescribeTransactions API (key 65, v0)".
* **(3.0) The `state_filters` of ListTransactions are matched verbatim, where the `states_filter` of ListGroups on
  the same node is not.** `TransactionState.fromName` @ 3.9.2 looks the name up in a map of the eight state names,
  so `ongoing` in lower case is **unknown** - it comes back in `unknown_state_filters` with the error code 0 -
  while `GroupMetadataManager.listGroups` lower-cases and trims its filter and accepts `stable`. The trap is that
  an unknown name does not widen the filter: a request whose state filters are all unknown is answered with an
  **empty** list, because the filter itself is still non-empty. → "ListTransactions API (key 66, v0 to v2)",
  "ListGroups API (key 16, v0 to v5)".
* **(3.0) The authorizer treats the two transaction admin apis differently.** With the `StandardAuthorizer` on,
  DescribeTransactions answers **53** (`TransactionalIdAuthorizationFailed`) in the entry of an id the principal
  may not `Describe` - and the GroupCoordinator lookup of that id answers the same code first, so a client that
  routes the request never sees the per-entry one - while ListTransactions answers the error code **0** with the
  ids it may not describe silently **removed** (`KafkaApis.handleListTransactionsRequest` @ 3.9.2 filters the
  answer after the coordinator built it). Measured as the SASL user `acltest`, the one principal of the node that
  is not a super user: 53 for the describe, an empty list for the listing, where `ANONYMOUS` on the PLAINTEXT
  listener saw the whole cluster. → "DescribeTransactions API (key 65, v0)", "ListTransactions API (key 66, v0 to v2)".
* **(3.8) The duration filter of ListTransactions is an age of the *transaction*, and an id that never started one
  passes it.** `TransactionStateManager.listTransactionStates` @ 3.9.2 drops an entry while
  `now - txnStartTimestamp <= duration_filter`, so the filter is strictly "older than" and it is measured from the
  start of the transaction, never from the last thing that happened to it: the same `CompleteCommit` entry is
  listed by a filter of 0 and dropped by one of 10000 for exactly as long as its *start* is less than ten seconds
  ago, although the commit itself just happened. The trap is the id **without** a transaction: its
  `txnStartTimestamp` is the -1 of "never started", `now - (-1)` is bigger than any filter a client can send, and
  an `Empty` id is therefore listed by *every* duration filter — measured on the node with the filter 60000, which
  answered the `Empty` id and dropped the transaction that was seconds old. A version 0 frame behaves like the
  filter -1, because `ListTransactionsRequestData.durationFilter()` gives that default to a request that cannot
  carry the field. → "ListTransactions API (key 66, v0 to v2)".
* **(3.8) DescribeTopicPartitions sorts, pages and reports the acl bit field without being asked.** The api of
  KIP-966 answers the topics **sorted by name** (`DescribeTopicPartitionsRequestHandler` @ 3.9.2 sorts the names
  before it asks the metadata cache), so the order of the request is lost and a client that pages has to merge by
  name; the `response_partition_limit` is clamped into `[1, max.request.partition.size.limit]`, whose default is
  the 2000 of the field itself, so the limit **0** is a page of one partition and the limit 1000000 a page of two
  thousand; and `topic_authorized_operations` is
  filled for every entry the handler answers — the unknown ones included, which carry the bit field **3576** of
  `ANONYMOUS` next to their 3 — because the request has no flag to ask for it with. The **`next_cursor` names the
  first partition that is *missing***, never the last one that was delivered, and it points at the partition 0 of
  the next topic when a whole topic did not fit. → "DescribeTopicPartitions API (key 75, v0)".
* **(3.8) The ELR fields of KIP-966 are empty arrays on this node, not nulls.** `eligible_leader_replicas` and
  `last_known_elr` are `"nullableVersions": "0+"` with the default `null` in `DescribeTopicPartitionsResponse.json`
  @ 3.8.1, but a KRaft node writes `Replicas.toList(partition.elr)`, which turns the empty replica array of the
  metadata image into an **empty list**: every partition of this node carries the compact `01` of a zero-length
  array in both fields, whatever `eligible.leader.replicas.version` is. A client that treats "null" and "empty" as
  the same thing therefore never learns which of the two it was given. → "DescribeTopicPartitions API (key 75,
  v0)".
* **(3.8) A cursor the node refuses is an error answer that names every topic of the request.** A cursor whose
  topic is not in the topic array of the same request, and a cursor whose partition index is negative, are both
  **42** (`InvalidRequest`) — and the frame that carries the code is not a top-level error but one entry per
  requested topic, with the zero topic id, no partition and the `-2147483648` of "no acl bit field", because
  `DescribeTopicPartitionsRequest.getErrorResponse` builds it that way. A cursor that is *legal* but points past
  the end of its topic is no error at all: the topic is answered with the code 0 and an **empty** partition array.
  The one request of this api that makes a 3.9.2 node log a stack trace is the topic whose name is the **empty
  string**: the handler compares it with the empty default of the cursor topic name, finds them equal and
  dereferences the cursor that is null, which reaches the client as the **-1** `UnknownServerError`
  (`java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "…Cursor.partitionIndex()" because "cursor" is null` in the log
  of the node). → "DescribeTopicPartitions API (key 75, v0)".
* **(3.8) The authorizer hides a topic from DescribeTopicPartitions in two different ways.** A topic that was
  **named** by a principal that may not `Describe` it is answered **29** (`TopicAuthorizationFailed`) with the zero
  id and no acl bit field, appended *behind* the topics that were answered, because the handler collects the
  refused ones in a set of its own; a request with the **empty** topic array — which is "every topic of the
  cluster" in this api, not "no topic" — is answered the topics the principal may see and nothing about the
  others, so `acltest` gets the twelve-byte frame of an empty topic array and a null cursor rather than a refusal.
  → "DescribeTopicPartitions API (key 75, v0)".
* **(3.x) DescribeLogDirs honours the partition selection again, and the raft log is not part of it.**
  `ReplicaManager.describeLogDirs` @ 3.9.2 ends the topics of a directory with
  `.filterNot(_.partitions().isEmpty)` — a filter Kafka **3.7** added and 3.6 still lacked — so a topic that keeps
  nothing the request named is dropped from the answer instead of being listed with an empty partition array.
  Measured on the node against the three shapes of the request: the **null** array is still every replica of the
  broker (16 topic entries and 70 partition entries when this was measured), the **empty** array still nothing at
  all (the two directories with no topic), and a request that names **one** partition is answered with exactly one
  topic entry and one partition entry — where the 2.8.2 broker answered the same 16 391 bytes to all three and
  made `describelogdirs.response.v1`/`.v2` constructed vectors. `__cluster_metadata-0` is **not** in any of those
  answers although it lives in `/tmp/kafka-logs`, the first entry of `log.dirs` and the default `metadata.log.dir`:
  the raft log belongs to the `KafkaRaftManager`, not to the `LogManager` the api reads. What the two directories
  do hold from the start are the internal topics, spread over both of them — the 50 `__transaction_state`
  partitions and the 5 `__consumer_offsets` ones were split 25/25 and 3/2 when this was measured.
  → "DescribeLogDirs API (key 35, v0 to v4)".
* **(3.2) The refusal of a whole DescribeLogDirs is a code from the version 3 on, and an empty array below it.**
  `KafkaApis.handleDescribeLogDirsRequest` @ 3.9.2 asks the authorizer for `DESCRIBE` on `CLUSTER` *before* it
  reads the topics of the request and, when the answer is no, builds
  `(List.empty, Errors.CLUSTER_AUTHORIZATION_FAILED)`. Measured on the node as the SASL user `acltest`, the one
  principal that is not in `super.users` and that no acl of the `StandardAuthorizer` names: a **version 3** is
  answered `error_code = 31` with an empty `log_dirs` (17 bytes), a **version 2** the empty compact array alone
  (15 bytes) and a **version 0 or 1** the same answer in the plain encoding (16 bytes) — below the version 3 the
  frame of a refusal and the frame of a broker without a single log directory are the same bytes, which is why the
  Java admin client guessed 31 from an empty map and, at 3.2.3, still does whenever the new field is 0. The
  authorization is of the **request**, not of the topics it names: the shape of the topic array (null, empty, one
  named partition) makes no difference to the refusal, and the three super users of the node (`ANONYMOUS` on
  PLAINTEXT, `kafkatest` and `admin` on SASL) are answered the directories in every version.
  → "DescribeLogDirs API (key 35, v0 to v4)".
* **(3.x) A log directory has an identity now, and a replica move is a controller write (KIP-858).** Each entry of
  `log.dirs` carries a `directory.id` in its `meta.properties` (`MzbBIWW4cqEHHmhGTesuKw` for `/tmp/kafka-logs` and
  `yXqn-Ss4u9zIyySkLqwnFA` for `/tmp/kafka-logs-2` on this node), the JBOD support of KIP-858 that
  `metadata.version=3.9-IV0` enables. The controller writes the `PARTITION_RECORD` of a fresh topic with
  `directories: ["AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAQ"]` — `DirectoryId.UNASSIGNED` @ 3.9.2, the `Uuid(0, 1)` — and the broker
  reports the directory it really created the log in about **130 ms** later with **AssignReplicasToDirs** (key 73,
  `"listeners": ["controller"]`, a frame no client sends), which the controller stores as a
  `PARTITION_CHANGE_RECORD` carrying the directory id. An AlterReplicaLogDirs of this client behaves as it did on
  the lines below — the answer comes in ~3 ms and the future log already exists at it, the logs are swapped in
  ~160 to 210 ms for a 2 MB partition — and about **90 ms after that answer** a second `PARTITION_CHANGE_RECORD`
  names the new directory. None of it is visible in a DescribeLogDirs answer of any version: the directory id has
  no field in this api, it lives in the metadata log alone
  (`kafka-run-class.sh kafka.tools.DumpLogSegments --cluster-metadata-decoder` reads it).
  → "AlterReplicaLogDirs API (key 34, v0 to v2)", "DescribeLogDirs API (key 35, v0 to v4)".
* **(3.x) A transactional batch for a partition the transaction does not hold is refused (KIP-890).**
  `transaction.partition.verification.enable` is **true** by default since Kafka 3.6
  (`TransactionLogConfigs` @ 3.9.2) and the image leaves it there, so the leader asks the coordinator whether the
  partition is in the transaction before it appends — with an **AddPartitionsToTxn v4** of its own, the version
  whose `verify_only` flag KIP-890 added and which `AddPartitionsToTxnRequest.json` @ 3.9.2 reserves for brokers
  ("versions 4 and above will be used by brokers"). Measured on the node: a Produce of a transactional batch for a
  partition that was never named in an AddPartitionsToTxn is answered **48** (`InvalidTxnState`) in that partition,
  with the per-partition `error_message` of KIP-467 `Partition was not added to the transaction`, where the 2.8.2
  broker appended the batch and left the hanging transaction KIP-890 is about. The `TransactionManager` of this
  client adds every partition before the first record goes out, so no test of the suite meets the refusal — a
  client that writes the frames by hand does.
  → "Transactions", "Produce API (key 0, v0 to v13)", "AddPartitionsToTxn API (key 24, v0 to v5)".
* **(3.5) The AddPartitionsToTxn v4 of KIP-890 is a broker frame, and the node says so in three ways.** The
  version that Kafka 3.5 added is announced on the client listeners of a 3.9.2 node (the key 24 is `0-5` in the
  api table, the `latestVersionUnstable` of the 3.5.2 specification is gone since the version 5), and it is served
  to whoever holds `CLUSTER_ACTION`: `KafkaApis.handleAddPartitionsToTxnRequest` @ 3.9.2 runs
  `if (version >= 4) authHelper.authorizeClusterOperation(request, CLUSTER_ACTION)` before it looks at a
  transaction and skips the `WRITE` authorization of the transactional id and of the topics that every version
  below 4 does. Measured: on **PLAINTEXT** the frame is answered, because `ANONYMOUS` is in the `super.users` of
  this image; as the SASL user **`acltest`** it is refused with the **top-level 31**
  (`ClusterAuthorizationFailed`) and an empty `results_by_transaction`, 13 bytes behind the size field — which is
  what a client is answered on any cluster whose authorizer grants `CLUSTER_ACTION` to the brokers alone. And its
  per-partition codes are broker codes: a `verify_only` of a partition the transaction does not hold is **120**
  (`TransactionAbortable`, the code Kafka 3.8 declared — the version 4 predates it), a transactional id that has a
  producer id but no open transaction answers the same 120 on every partition, an epoch below the stored one is
  **90** and an unknown topic **3**. `AddPartitionsToTxnManager` @ 3.9.2 maps the 90 to the 47, the 120 to the 48
  and even the top-level 31 to a 48 before the producer of the batch sees any of it. This client therefore keeps
  sending the **version 3** and carries the version 4 for the wire alone.
  → "AddPartitionsToTxn API (key 24, v0 to v5)", "Transactions".
* **(3.8) The version 5 of the same api is a broker frame as well, and the four client-facing bumps of KIP-890
  part 2 change nothing a node of this line can show.** The authorization above reads `if (version >= 4)`, so the
  version Kafka 3.8 added is refused the same **top-level 31** as `acltest` — measured — and
  `Client::addPartitionsToTxn()` stays at the version 3 for the whole line. The five version bumps of Kafka 3.8
  (InitProducerId v5, AddPartitionsToTxn v5, AddOffsetsToTxn v4, EndTxn v4, TxnOffsetCommit v4) declare **no
  field** and all say the same sentence, "adds support for new error code TRANSACTION_ABORTABLE (KIP-890)", and
  `Errors.TRANSACTION_ABORTABLE` is written by exactly one line of a 3.9.2 broker,
  `TransactionCoordinator.handleVerifyPartitionsInTransaction` — the `verify_only` path of the key 24, which is
  the **partition verification** of KIP-890 part 1. A client meets it either by sending that broker frame itself,
  or through a request whose partition the broker has to verify — and there
  `AddPartitionsToTxnManager` folds the 120 back into the 48 unless the request version promises the code, a gate
  each api spells out for itself: `if (apiVersion >= 4) genericError else defaultError` in
  `GroupCoordinator.handleTxnCommitOffsets` for **TxnOffsetCommit**, `if (request.header.apiVersion > 10)` in
  `KafkaApis.handleProduceRequest` for Produce. So **TxnOffsetCommit v4 really does answer the 120**: a commit
  whose `__consumer_offsets` partition the open transaction does not hold (no AddOffsetsToTxn preceded it) is
  answered 120 per partition where the same commit at the version 3 is answered the 48 — measured, and the
  difference between a producer this client calls finished and one that can abort and carry on. The other three
  verify no partition and answer what they always did: a fenced InitProducerId is the **90**, an AddOffsetsToTxn
  with a producer id the coordinator does not hold the **49**, an EndTxn that aborts a committed transaction the
  **48**. → "The transaction protocol v2 of KIP-890 (Kafka 3.8), and what a client reaches on this node",
  "AddPartitionsToTxn API (key 24, v0 to v5)", "TxnOffsetCommit API (key 28, v0 to v5)".
* **(3.8) The node finalizes no `transaction.version`, so the behaviour half of KIP-890 part 2 is out of reach.**
  The ApiVersions v3 answer of the node names **one** supported feature, `metadata.version` 1 to 21, finalized at
  21 (`3.9-IV0`); `kafka-features.sh --bootstrap-server localhost:9092 describe` adds `kraft.version` 0 to 1 with
  the finalized level 0 and nothing more. Two different rules hide two different things: `transaction.version` is
  **not in the broker's supported map at all**, because `BrokerFeatures.defaultSupportedFeatures` @ 3.9.2 adds a
  production feature only `if (maxVersion > 0)` and `TransactionVersion.latestProduction` at the metadata version
  `3.9-IV0` is `TV_0` — both `TV_1` and `TV_2` declare `bootstrapMetadataVersion = IBP_4_0_IV0`, Kafka 4.0 — while
  `kraft.version` is dropped from a v3 *answer* alone, by `ApiVersionsResponse.maybeFilterSupportedFeatureKeys`,
  which omits every feature whose minimum level is 0 below the version 4 (KAFKA-17492); a hand-built **ApiVersions
  v4** frame carries it. A missing feature reads as the level 0, so the node runs the transaction coordinator at
  **TV_0**: there is no epoch bump per transaction and no implicit AddPartitionsToTxn of a Produce to measure, and
  the only thing `transaction.version` gates at that tag is `TransactionStateManager.usesFlexibleRecords()`, the
  record format of `__transaction_state`. → "The transaction protocol v2 of KIP-890 (Kafka 3.8), and what a client
  reaches on this node", "ApiVersions API (key 18, v0 to v4)".
* **(3.x) `__transaction_state` is created by the controller, and the producer ids come from it too.** The first
  type 1 lookup still creates the topic, but nothing logs the ZooKeeper sentence *"Auto creation of topic
  `__transaction_state` with 50 partitions and replication factor 1 is successful"* any more: the node logs
  `Sent auto-creation request for Set(__transaction_state) to the active controller.
  (kafka.server.DefaultAutoTopicCreationManager)` and the 50 partitions of
  `transaction.state.log.num.partitions` appear in **both** log directories about 160 ms later
  (`cleanup.policy=compact`, `segment.bytes=104857600`). Once the topic is there, a lookup of a transactional id
  that was never used is answered **0** in about 1 ms, with the node **1** as the coordinator and the
  `error_message` `"NONE"` the 2.8.2 broker also sent. The producer id of an InitProducerId is no longer taken
  from a ZooKeeper counter: the controller hands the broker a block of 1000 through **AllocateProducerIds**
  (key 67, controller listener) and writes a `PRODUCER_IDS_RECORD` with `nextProducerId: 1000` into the metadata
  log, so the ids of a fresh node start at **0** and climb one per InitProducerId — the coordinator logs each one
  as `[TransactionCoordinator id=1] Initialized transactionalId <id> with producerId <n> and producer epoch 0 on
  partition __transaction_state-<p>`.
  → "Transactions", "InitProducerId API (key 22, v0 to v5)", "GroupCoordinator API (key 10, v0 to v6)".
* **(3.x) DescribeCluster is answered to everyone, and its refusal is an empty bit field.** The 31 of the error
  table of the api is not what a principal without rights gets: `handleDescribeCluster` @ 3.9.2 answers the cluster
  id, the controller and the brokers to every authenticated principal and only asks the authorizer for the
  `cluster_authorized_operations`. Measured on the node over all four listeners: a **super user** (`ANONYMOUS` on
  9092, `admin` and `kafkatest` over SASL) gets the **8096** the 2.8.2 broker answered without an authorizer at
  all, the SASL user **`acltest`** gets the same brokers, the code **0** and the bit field **0** — not one
  operation. `error_message` is **null** in both, not the empty string of DescribeAcls, DescribeQuorum and
  UnregisterBroker, and `controller_id` is the node **1**. The endpoint in the answer is the one of the listener
  the request arrived on, exactly as in a Metadata answer (port 9094 over SASL_PLAINTEXT, 9092 over PLAINTEXT).
  → "DescribeCluster API (key 60, v0 to v2)".
* **(3.x) DescribeProducers answers three different messages, and its 29 is producible now.** The per-partition
  `error_message` of the api says which half of `handleDescribeProducersRequest` @ 3.9.2 refused: a partition the
  broker does not have but whose **topic** it knows comes back as the 3 with a **null** message (the
  `PartitionResponse` that `replicaManager.activeProducerState` builds), a topic the cluster does not know at all
  as the 3 with the default sentence of the code, `This server does not host this topic-partition.` (the
  topic-level `ApiError`), and an illegal topic name as **17** with the sentence of `Topic.validate` —
  `Topic name is invalid: 't4 not a legal name' contains one or more characters other than ASCII alphanumerics,
  '.', '_' and '-'`, and `Topic name is invalid: the empty string is not allowed` for the empty one. The **29** of
  the table is no longer theory: the api authorizes `READ` on the topic, so `acltest` is answered 29 with
  `Topic authorization failed.` in every partition it names.
  → "DescribeProducers API (key 61, v0)".
* **(3.x) The SASL exchange is the 2.8.2 one; what the principal may do afterwards is not.** Handshake and tokens
  are unchanged on this node — `["PLAIN"]` as the enabled mechanisms, the 33 of a mechanism the node does not
  have, the 34 with `SaslAuthenticate request received after successful authentication`, the 58 with
  `Authentication failed: Invalid username or password` and with `Invalid SASL/PLAIN response: expected 3 tokens,
  got 1`, the empty error message of a successful answer and the `session_lifetime_ms` **0** of a listener without
  a `connections.max.reauth.ms`. What the node adds is the `StandardAuthorizer` behind them: with
  `allow.everyone.if.no.acl.found=false` the SASL user **`acltest`** authenticates exactly like a super user —
  code 0, empty message, lifetime 0 — and is then refused by everything it asks for, a Metadata of an existing
  topic with the topic error **29** and no partition, DescribeProducers with 29 per partition, DescribeAcls with
  **31**. Authentication and authorization are two answers here, where every broker of the lines below authorized
  whatever it had authenticated.
  → "SaslAuthenticate API (key 36, v0 to v2)", "SASL/PLAIN", "API keys".
* **(4.2) A WriteTxnMarkers of a negative producer epoch escapes the handler.** A marker with the epoch -1 is
  answered **-1** with no message for its partition, and the 4.3.1 node logs `Unexpected error handling request`
  with `IllegalArgumentException: Invalid negative producer epoch` out of `MemoryRecordsBuilder.validateProducerState()`:
  `KafkaApis.handleWriteTxnMarkersRequest()` builds the control batch before the log could refuse the epoch with
  the 47 an epoch below the partition's gets. Only a broker sends this api, and a
  coordinator never has a negative epoch to send. → "What Kafka 4.2 changed here (KIP-1228): the version 2".
* **(4.2) The share-partition lag of a group appears with its first acknowledgement.** A DescribeShareGroupOffsets
  v1 of a share group whose member has acquired records but acknowledged none answers the start offset -1 and the
  lag **-1** for the partition; the first acknowledgement brings both. A group whose start offset an
  AlterShareGroupOffsets set has a lag at once, with a delivery-complete count of 0.
  → "The share-partition lag of KIP-1226 (v1)".


## Error codes

The authority is `clients/src/main/java/org/apache/kafka/common/protocol/Errors.java` @ 3.9.2, which ends at `127`
(`VOTER_NOT_FOUND`). The 0.10 line added the codes in three steps (**32-35** with 0.10.0, **36-42** with 0.10.1,
**43-44** with 0.10.2), Kafka 0.11 added **45-55** in one (45-47 the idempotent producer, 48-53 the transactions,
54-55 the ACL apis), the 1.x line added **56-71** in two (**56-60** with Kafka 1.0 — a storage failure, a log
directory, the SASL authentication of KIP-152, the unknown producer id of the five-batch window, a reassignment in
progress — and **61-71** with Kafka 1.1, the seven delegation-token codes of KIP-48, the two group codes of
DeleteGroups and the two fetch-session codes of KIP-227), the 2.x line added **the 33 codes 72 to 104**, more than
any line before it, in eight steps:

| Release | Codes | What they belong to |
|---------|-------|---------------------|
| 2.0 | 72 | The listener a Metadata v6 arrived on has no endpoint for the leader |
| 2.1 | 73-76 | DeleteTopics v3, the two leader-epoch codes of KIP-320 and the zstd codec of KIP-110 |
| 2.2 | 77-81 | The broker epoch of KIP-380, the offset of KIP-207, the member id of KIP-394, the preferred-leader election of KIP-183 and the group size of KIP-389 |
| 2.3 | 82 | The static membership of KIP-345 |
| 2.4 | 83-87 | The election types of KIP-460, the reassignments of KIP-455, the OffsetDelete of KIP-496 and the record errors of KIP-467 |
| 2.5 | 88 | The read-committed offset fetch of KIP-447 |
| 2.7 | 89-96 | The mutation quota of KIP-599, the fenced producer of KIP-588, the three SCRAM codes of KIP-554, the raft voters of KIP-595 and the two feature codes of KIP-584 |
| 2.8 | 97-104 | The forwarding of KIP-590, the raft snapshots of KIP-630, the topic ids of KIP-516 and the broker lifecycle of KIP-631 |

**Seven of the thirty-three were codes a ZooKeeper-backed broker never sent to a client** — that is the 2.x line's
measurement, on its 2.8.2 broker: 94, 97, 98, 99, 101, 102 and 104 belong to the KRaft quorum, to the request
forwarding and to the broker lifecycle of KIP-500, three more were all but unreachable (**77** arrived only because
the probe sent a broker-to-broker request on purpose, and **95** and **96** were refused as **42** first, because a
ZooKeeper-backed cluster finalizes no feature at all). On a KRaft node the picture turns: 95 and 96 are the codes
of a cluster that *does* finalize features, and 77 has no api to arrive from on a client listener. What of it the
node really answers is re-measured by the milestones, api by api.

**And this line adds the 23 codes 105 to 127**, read off `Errors.java` at the tags `3.0.2` to `3.9.2`, in eight
steps as well:

| Release | Codes | What they belong to |
|---------|-------|---------------------|
| 3.0 | 105 | DescribeTransactions (65): a transactional id the coordinator does not know |
| 3.1 | 106 | A fetch session (KIP-227) that mixes topics named by id (Fetch v13, KIP-516) with topics named by name |
| 3.3 | 107-108 | AlterPartition (56): an ineligible replica in the new ISR, and a leader that changed while the request was applied — broker→controller codes |
| 3.5 | 109-112 | The offset that moved to tiered storage (Fetch v14, ListOffsets v8, KIP-405), and the first three codes of the KIP-848 protocol (ConsumerGroupHeartbeat, 68): a fenced member epoch, an instance id another member still holds, an assignor the group does not support |
| 3.6 | 113 | The stale member epoch of the same protocol, **measured** on the node with OffsetCommit v9 |
| 3.7 | 114-119 | The endpoint type of DescribeCluster v1 (KIP-919): the wrong endpoint, an unsupported one, an unknown controller id; the two refusals of PushTelemetry (72); a broker or controller registration the controller considers invalid |
| 3.8 | 120 | The abortable transaction error of KIP-890 |
| 3.9 | 121-127 | Share groups (KIP-932): a record state, a share session, its epoch and the state epoch of the share coordinator; and the voters of the raft quorum: AddRaftVoter (80) and RemoveRaftVoter (81).
