### `writetxnmarkers.response.v2`

Refused with **47** (`INVALID_PRODUCER_EPOCH` in `Errors.java`, `ProducerFencedException` in this client): a marker of
the transaction version 2 has to carry an epoch **above** the one of the open transaction, because a coordinator of
the protocol v2 bumps the epoch with every EndTxn - `ProducerAppendInfo.checkProducerEpoch()` @ 4.3.1 logs `Epoch of
producer 89 at offset 1 in t4-42-vectors-marker-0 is 0, which is <= the last seen epoch 0 (TV2)`. The transaction
stays open. The answer is the frame of the version 1.

### `produce.request.v9`

Produce request v9 (Kafka 2.8), the FLEXIBLE version of the api (KIP-482): the request header v2, the nullable transactional_id as a compact string (the single byte 00 for the null of a plain producer), a compact topic array and name, a compact partition array, the record set as a COMPACT byte array and a tagged-field section behind every structure. Not one field was added: ProduceRequest.json @ 2.8.2 says "Version 9 enables flexible versions" and nothing else.

### `pushtelemetry.response.v0`

**A throttle time, the code 0 and the two tag buffers**, twelve bytes behind the size field - among the shortest answers this protocol has. The node accepts the push although no receiver plugin is configured - `ClientMetricsManager.processPushTelemetryRequest` @ 3.9.2 only calls the plugin when the blob is non-empty, and an empty plugin list exports nothing - so 0 here means "taken", not "stored".

### `joingroup.response.v9.static-return`

The answer that carries `skip_assignment` = **true** (the byte 01 behind the leader id): the coordinator did not rebalance the group at all - it answered in milliseconds, the generation is still 1 - it only replaced the member id of that instance, and this member is the leader. ### `describequorum.response.v1`

The quorum of the one combined node: the leader is the node id **1** in the epoch 1, the high watermark is the offset the metadata log is replicated to, and the single **voter** is that node itself - a `process.roles=broker,controller` node votes and observes nothing, so the observer array is empty. The two timestamps of KIP-836 are the ones this version adds: the leader answers the **current time** for both of its own, not the -1 the `about` of the specification names for `LastFetchTimestamp` (`LeaderState.describeReplicaState` @ 3.3.2 sets both to `currentTimeMs` for the local id).

The same quorum without the timestamps: a replica state of the version 0 is the replica id and the log end offset, and the answer is 16 bytes shorter than the version 1 one for that reason alone. ### `describequorum.response.v2`

The quorum of the one combined node at the version 2, with the four additions of KIP-853 in it: the top-level
`error_message`, which the node writes as the **empty string** (the compact `01`) and not as the null the
specification defaults it to; the same `error_message` inside the partition; a `replica_directory_id` in front of the
log end offset of every replica state, which is the **zero uuid** here because the quorum of this node is the static
`controller.quorum.voters` of KIP-595 and its `kraft.version` feature is finalized at 0 - the `meta.properties` of the
container carries a real `directory.id`, and the answer still does not; and the top-level `nodes` array, which names
the node id 1 with its **CONTROLLER** listener at `localhost:9096` - the listener a client never connects to, and the
only place in this answer where an id of a replica state can be resolved to an address. The port is the one `uint16`
of the protocol.

The code 31 (ClusterAuthorizationFailed) and no resource: `AclApis.handleDescribeAcls` @ 3.9.2 asks the authorizer for DESCRIBE on the CLUSTER resource BEFORE it reads the filter, so a principal cannot even read the acls that are written for itself. The `error_message` is the whole request object of the broker, which `AuthHelper.authorizeClusterOperation` builds with `s"Request $request is not authorized."` - a processor number, a connection id, the identity hash of a Java object and the listener of the connection.

The node answers **-1** (UnknownServerError) with a NULL message: `CreateAclsRequest.aclBinding` @ 3.9.2 builds a `ResourcePattern` out of the entry before any validation of the api runs and that constructor throws the plain `IllegalArgumentException("patternType must not be ANY")`, which `ApiError.fromThrowable` can only map to the unknown error. The Java admin client never sends such a request, because `AclBinding` refuses to be built.

### `fetch.response.v15.replica-state`

The answer of the node: the top-level error code 0 and the partition error 6 NotLeaderForPartition, with the high water mark and the log start offset -1 and an empty record set. A fetch whose replica id is not negative is a FOLLOWER fetch (FetchRequest.isFromFollower), the caller is authorized for it because ANONYMOUS is a super user of this node - and the broker 1 is the LEADER of the partition, not one of its followers, so Partition.followerReplicaOrThrow @ 3.9.2 finds no replica 1 to record a position for. The replica epoch is never even looked at.

### `produce.response.v10.current-leader`

it can never answer a produce with 6 NotLeaderForPartition and never writes the hint into a Produce answer. These
are the bytes a 3.9.2 broker writes when the partition has moved to another node: the partition entry carries the
error code 6 and the tagged current_leader (tag 0 of the ENTRY, the count 01, the tag 00, the size 09 and the leader
id 2 with the leader epoch 4), and the body carries the tagged node_endpoints (tag 0 of the BODY) that names where
the node 2 can be reached. The two structures are the ones the same node really writes into a Fetch v16 answer of

### `fetch.request.v16.replica-state`

A version 16 fetch that claims to be the FOLLOWER 1 with the broker epoch 0, i.e. the version 15 frame of KIP-903
with the tagged replica_state at its end and the api version 16 in its header. The one broker of this node is the
leader of the partition and not one of its followers, so this is the one way a client of a one-broker cluster can
make it answer 6 NotLeaderForPartition - and with it the leader discovery of KIP-951.

<!-- vector: fetch.request.v16.replica-state -->
```

00 01                                             # apiKey = 1
```

### `fetch.response.v18.follower-high-watermark`

and an empty node_endpoints - the answer the same claim gets without the tag. The broker is the leader of the
partition, not a follower of it, and nothing on the fetch path of a broker partition reads the high watermark of the
request at 4.1.0 to 4.3.1: KIP-1166 is read by the KRaft leader of the metadata log

### `listgroups.response.v5.unknown-type`

The error code **0** and an **empty** group array: `UNKNOWN` is a type no group ever has, so an unknown type is a
filter nothing matches and never an error. A client can not use this api to validate a type name, exactly as it can
not use it to validate a state name.

### `listgroups.response.v5.empty-group`

The group is still listed, now in the state `Empty` - it outlives its last member as long as its committed offsets
do - and its **type is still `consumer`**: the type is a property of the group and not of its membership, so an
empty group of the new protocol stays a `consumer` group until the coordinator forgets it.

### `groupcoordinator.response.v5.transaction`

The transaction coordinator of that id, with the code 0. A transactional id is not registered by the lookup - the
coordinator only hashes the key onto a partition - so an id that was never used is a legal question with a normal

`KafkaApis.handleFindCoordinatorRequest` @ 3.9.2 has no path that writes it.

### `groupcoordinator.response.v6.share-type`

The node answers the error code **15** `CoordinatorNotAvailable` with the coordinator `-1:"":-1` and the empty
message - not the 42 of every version below 6. `KafkaApis.getCoordinator` @ 3.9.2 passes the version gate and the
`CLUSTER_ACTION` check and then returns that code out of the `CoordinatorType.SHARE` branch of its match, under the
comment *"When share coordinator support is implemented in KIP-932, a proper check will go here"*: the share
coordinator does not exist on a 3.9.2 node at all. The 15 is a **retriable** code for `Common\CoordinatorLookup`, so
a client that asked for this type would retry it until its timeout ran out - which is one more reason the share
groups are out of this line.

### `consumergroupheartbeat.v0.join.request`

itself, a subscription of one topic, the rebalance timeout of `max.poll.interval.ms` and the EMPTY `topic_partitions`

### `updatefeatures.response.v2.validate-only`

The answer of the version 2: the throttle time, the top-level **0**, a **null** `error_message` and nothing else - thirteen bytes behind the size field. There is no `results` array to name the feature in: a top-level 0 is the 0 of every feature of the request. The 3.9.2 node wrote the empty string here; `QuorumController.updateFeatures` @ 4.0.0 sets the message of `ApiError.NONE`, which is null.

### `updatefeatures.response.v2.downgrade-refused`

The top-level **95** (`InvalidUpdateVersion`), and no result: a 4.x controller refuses the whole request at the first feature it cannot change, and the message is the reason of that feature behind the sentence `The update failed for all features since the following feature had an error:`. The reason is the one KIP-778 wrote for the `upgrade_type` of the version 1.

### `addraftvoter.response.v1.voter-in-backoff`

Another **7**, with another sentence: `New voter ReplicaKey(id=4243, …) is not ready to receive requests`. The raft client of the leader backs off a replica id whose last request failed for `controller.quorum.retry.backoff.ms` (20 ms by default, `RequestManager` @ 4.3.1), and `DefaultRequestSender.send` refuses to send the ApiVersions in the meantime - `AddVoterHandler` answers that refusal before an operation is even started. The refusal: **48** `InvalidTxnState` with the defaults -1/-1 of the two new fields. There is no transition from
`CompleteCommit` to a commit that is not a retry, which is why a producer does not end a transaction that never
started (`transactionStarted` of the Java `TransactionManager` @ 4.0.0).
